suggestion.title: YesWiki page mass-deletion in single request (suppr[] array >10 elements)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'deletes every wiki page whose tag appears in that array' — single POST can destroy multiple pages. Existing UCs flag the request but not the scope of destruction. Pipeline missed impact-layer detection keying on array size as blast-radius indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST to erasespamedcomments with suppr[] element count ≥10, or any suppr[] targeting >5 distinct page-tags in single request. Correlate with web server HTTP 200 responses (successful POST) to confirm exploitation. Flags wide-scale data destruction attempts.

suggestion.title: YesWiki erasespamedcomments POST without prior authentication session
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated arbitrary page deletion' and 'no authorization check anywhere.' Existing UCs detect the POST itself but not the unauthenticated aspect. Critical gap: auth-bypass dimension not captured. Article phrase: 'any user who has page write access' suggests write access is sufficient, but erasespamedcomments should require delete/admin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag erasespamedcomments POST requests missing valid session cookie, JWT, or auth header. Baseline against known-good admin authentication tokens. YesWiki's 'allow-by-default action ACL' means any web access + write permission may trigger this; detection must key on missing auth checks (abnormal for a destructive action).

suggestion.title: YesWiki homepage (PagePrincipale) deletion via erasespamedcomments
suggestion.rationale: Existing UC_3_2 includes PagePrincipale detection as derivative field ('front_page_targeted'). Article does not explicitly state homepage is high-value target, but destroying wiki homepage is maximum-impact availability attack. Pipeline should flag this as distinct severity tier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST to erasespamedcomments where suppr[] array contains 'PagePrincipale' tag. Treat as severity-elevated from standard page deletion (homepage is wiki's entry point; deletion cascades to user impact). Correlate with subsequent 404/HTTP 200 access logs to PagePrincipale in minutes following exploit POST.

suggestion.title: npm Malicious Package Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names @injectivelabs/sdk-ts@1.20.21 as malicious, downloaded 310 times. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite package name and version being central to the threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package repositories for version anomalies on high-dependency packages (87+ direct deps). Flag rapid version increments with minimal changelog, commits from newly-active/compromised contributors on June 8-9 timeframe, and versions downloaded <500 times then deprecated/removed within 24hrs.

suggestion.title: Wallet Key/Seed Phrase Exfiltration via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'captures the full mnemonic seed phrase and private key and encodes the data in base64' and 'exfiltrated via an HTTP POST request.' This is the core detection—payload pattern and C2 channel—yet pipeline generated no HTTP signature or credential-capture UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests with base64-encoded payloads to Injective Labs infrastructure endpoints; payload should decode to cryptographic patterns (hex-like structure, mnemonic word lists). Article notes 2-second batch window—correlate multiple key exports within 2s window followed by single POST.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise Introducing Malicious Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface: 'attacker compromised a GitHub account belonging to a legitimate project contributor and made the first suspicious commits on June 8.' Pipeline did not map GitHub compromise, account takeover detection, or commit content analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify commits from known-contributor accounts with no prior access (first commits June 8) introducing require() statements for new remote URLs or base64 decode operations. Cross-ref commit author IP, MFA status, and device posture against historical baseline.

suggestion.title: SDK Wallet Function Hook/Call Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'activates when the developers use SDK functions that generate or import wallet keys.' Detection should focus on SDK function invocation patterns, not just network signatures. Article phrase: 'The malware activates when the developers use SDK functions that generate or import wallet keys.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hook or monitor calls to @injectivelabs/sdk-ts wallet generation functions (mnemonic, privateKey creation). Flag if followed by base64.encode() or btoa() calls on sensitive output within 100ms, or HTTP network I/O in same execution context.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Supply Chain Impact
suggestion.rationale: Article: '87 direct dependencies' and '112,000 cumulative download count.' Pipeline did not model dependency tree risk, multi-stage propagation, or downstream package consumers. This is supply-chain amplification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate malicious package @injectivelabs/sdk-ts@1.20.21 against downstream dependent packages; identify all applications that transitively included it via package-lock.json or yarn.lock. Alert on any package installation events for affected consumers during June 8-10 window.

suggestion.title: Malicious Release Artifact Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the malicious GitHub release artifacts are still available' and 'the malicious version of the package was downloaded 310 times before it was deprecated, not removed.' Pipeline missed persistence indicator: artifacts remain accessible post-discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for deprecated (not deleted) npm package versions with known malicious content; flag if GitHub release artifacts remain downloadable 24+ hours after deprecation. This indicates attacker persistence or slow takedown.

suggestion.title: Ruckus/ASUS Router Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploits known vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers' as UAT-7810's primary initial access method; pipeline extracted zero indicators for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Ruckus/ASUS router management interfaces (port 80, 443, 8080) with known CVE exploitation signatures. Alert on sequences: reconnaissance traffic (OPTIONS, HEAD) followed by POST/PUT to /admin, /cgi-bin, or firmware endpoints, especially if followed by 500 errors or device reboot.

suggestion.title: LONGLEASH/DOGLEASH Malware Deployment on Network Edge
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'upgraded LONGLEASH and DOGLEASH backdoors' as persistence mechanism deployed on compromised routers; pipeline missed both malware family names and deployment detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process creation or binary execution from router-adjacent paths (/tmp, /var/tmp, /etc/init.d) with network connections. Alert on cron jobs or systemd services executing LONGLEASH or DOGLEASH patterns. Cross-reference with credential access to router admin panels within prior 6 hours.

suggestion.title: ORB Network Multi-Hop Proxy Activity on Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes UAT-7810 builds 'decentralized proxy network that easily bypasses traditional perimeter defenses' and describes ORBs 'routing malicious traffic through seemingly innocuous nodes'; pipeline failed to map this to T1090.3 or detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline: routers should not originate outbound connections to external proxies or tunnel protocols. Alert on: CONNECT requests from router source IPs, SOCKS/SSH tunnels established from edge device management interfaces, or netflow records showing router IP appearing in the middle of connection chains (traffic transiting through it when routing should terminate). Require correlation with suspicious authentication or file operations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Router Administrative Access from External IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article notes ORBs provide 'infrastructure for other APT groups to launch attacks'; implies secondary actors access compromised routers—requires detection of unauthorized admin login attempts and successful access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP Basic Auth or POST login attempts to router management interfaces from IPs outside organization's trust boundary. Flag successful authentications from residential proxies, VPN exit nodes, or geographically impossible locations (same IP logging in from two continents within 10 minutes). Require deviation from baseline of authorized admin IPs.

suggestion.title: Unusual Proxy Behavior on Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends defenders 'Monitor network traffic for unusual proxying behavior or unauthorized connections on devices that typically lack complex services'; pipeline produced no detection for this guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish behavioral baseline for each edge device type (routers rarely proxy, typically only forward). Alert if router or access point device acts as proxy (e.g., HTTP CONNECT method, SOCKS handshakes, hostname resolution from device not normally used for DNS). Monitor for sudden increase in data volume or connection count from a single edge device to non-standard external IPs.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Detection from Talos Telemetry
suggestion.rationale: Article lists four malware hashes (9f1f11a7..., 621c6d42..., 9896a6fc..., afc8a008...) with detection classifications; pipeline returned empty IOC dict despite hashable values available for signature matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or process execution matching provided hashes. Given detections include coinminer (9f1f...), process patcher (9896a6...), and KMS activator (afc8a00...), flag as potential commodity malware or post-exploitation tools. Correlate hash detection with network telemetry to determine if part of ORB network toolkit or unrelated prevalent malware.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Encryption Activity via Avalon Framework
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states malware framework 'packs' ransomware capabilities—direct statement of encryption impact. Pipeline missed T1486 entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid file modification patterns matching ransomware encryption signatures: high-frequency writes to file extensions associated with encryption (e.g., .locked, .encrypted), modified file extensions in bulk across directories, paired with process executing from temp/appdata paths.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note Creation and Display
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware framework articles typically describe ransom note deployment (README.txt, RANSOM.html). Pipeline missed this impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation of common ransom note names (README.txt, RANSOM.html, DECRYPT_ME.txt, note.html) in multiple directories simultaneously, especially when paired with bulk file modifications or encryption patterns in the same timeline.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Malware Framework Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'Avalon Malware Framework'—frameworks are tools for spreading across infrastructure. No lateral movement detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag transfer of framework binaries to multiple internal hosts via SMB, RDP, or lateral execution tools (PsExec, WMI). Correlate process spawning framework executables on systems with no recent software deployment or admin activity.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Security Service Disruption Pre-Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware frameworks typically disable EDR, AV, and backup services before encryption. Article does not detail this but pipeline should infer from framework type.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of net.exe, powershell.exe, or wmic.exe with stop/disable commands targeting Windows Defender, backup services (VSS), or security product services immediately preceding bulk file operations.

suggestion.title: Avalon Framework Process Execution Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Framework delivery mechanism and initial execution not detailed in available text; pipeline missed execution phase mapping for unknown malware families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of processes named 'avalon.*' or 'crownx.*' (case-insensitive variants), spawning from temp directories, Office processes, or browser contexts. Flag suspicious DLL loads into explorer.exe or svchost.exe.

suggestion.title: Ransom Demand Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware frameworks typically establish C2 or payment site links in ransom notes. No communication pattern detection in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ransom note file creation with DNS queries to newly registered domains, Tor exit nodes, or .onion resolution attempts. Flag HTTP requests to payment portals or cryptocurrency exchanges from affected systems.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-48282 scanning and exploitation attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and 'federal patch due 2026-07-10' — scanners and attackers are actively probing for this. No detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\) targeting ColdFusion application paths, or CVE-2026-48282 signatures in WAF/IDS logs. Correlate with ColdFusion process startup and child spawning.

suggestion.title: Monitor ColdFusion process for post-exploitation code execution

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, cfengine.exe) without corresponding application deployment or update activity. Flag outbound connections from ColdFusion process to unusual ports.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory: identify and prioritize ColdFusion instances
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries require urgent remediation by federal due date (2026-07-10 per article). Pipeline omitted asset-hunting entirely despite this being the canonical first step for vulnerability response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all ColdFusion deployments via port/banner scanning (default ports 8500, 8501), check version against known-vulnerable range, cross-reference against patch-management records. Prioritize publicly exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Hunt for CVE-2026-48282 path traversal in application access logs

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search application logs for requests with encoded or double-encoded traversal sequences (e.g., %2e%2e, ..%252f, backslash variants) targeting ColdFusion directories. Baseline normal ColdFusion path patterns and flag anomalies.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify exposed Adobe ColdFusion instances (port 8500, 8501, CFML file extensions) accessible from internet. Cross-reference against patch inventory to confirm vulnerability window. CISA KEV means active exploitation — asset exposure is the critical first hunt.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP request logs for ColdFusion endpoints (URIs with .cfm extensions) containing path traversal sequences. Alert on both unencoded `../` and URL-encoded variants (%2e%2e%2f, ..%2f, etc.). Path traversal is rarely legitimate in production web traffic.

suggestion.title: Detect ColdFusion Runtime Spawning Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Successful exploitation yields process execution. Pipeline missed the execution-phase detection entirely. ColdFusion runtime (java.exe/cfusion.exe) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl.exe is exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by ColdFusion services. Flag cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, or network utilities originating from ColdFusion context. Establish baseline of legitimate process spawning first.

suggestion.title: Monitor Asset Exposure and Patch Status for CVE-2026-48282

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Adobe ColdFusion instances with CVE-2026-48282 vulnerability status. Cross-reference asset inventory for network-exposed instances. Verify patch application against today's federal deadline. Any unpatched instance = critical incident.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous File Access Outside ColdFusion Application Directories

ColdFusion service account accessing system directories (C:\Windows\System32, C:\Program Files) or directories outside application root (c:\coldfusion*) indicates traversal exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access logs from ColdFusion process account. Flag access to directories outside configured application root, especially system/config directories. Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Hunt for Post-Exploitation Artifacts in ColdFusion Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited.' Pipeline generated zero post-exploitation detection. Successful exploitation typically leaves traces in ColdFusion error logs: Java exceptions, permission errors, or unusual stack traces during HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search ColdFusion error logs for patterns consistent with path traversal exploitation: NullPointerException, FileNotFoundException, or AccessDeniedException during unusual file/path operations. Look for repeated failed attempts followed by successful execution or command output.

suggestion.title: Alert on Patch Deadline Compliance: ColdFusion Instances Unpatched Past 2026-07-10
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' (today) and 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal auditors will ask. Pipeline failed to translate deadline + active exploitation into operational alerting. This is a compliance + incident risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management system for all ColdFusion instances. Flag any running affected versions without patches applied by 2026-07-10. Alert security, infrastructure, and business owners immediately. Document as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public-Facing Application Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability impacts public-facing ColdFusion instances and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Explicit guidance: hunt for exposed ColdFusion servers (non-internal routes, listening on 80/443).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Traversal

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Patch Compliance Scan Coverage

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Unusual File Access Patterns (Post-Traversal)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of 404/403 responses followed by 200 responses in ColdFusion logs, or filesystem access attempts outside normal application directories. Correlate with path traversal URI patterns in same session.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Detected in Vulnerability Scanner

suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated stealer malware (especially 'Armored' actor campaigns) typically employ anti-analysis, sandbox evasion, or injection. No evasion techniques surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for obfuscation indicators: code caves, unusual PE section names, reflective DLL injection, or API hooking attempts. Flag parent-child anomalies (e.g., system process spawning svchost with suspicious module loads).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-48282 and CISA KEV lists only exploited-in-the-wild CVEs. 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet' establishes the need for scanner-based inventory control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for systems flagged CVE-2026-48282 or running unpatched Adobe ColdFusion. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed instances. Alert on any match, even if marked 'remediated' — patch lag is the killer here.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Attempts (Web Access Logs)
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Must detect attempts to traverse ColdFusion directories before exploitation succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web server and WAF logs for HTTP requests targeting ColdFusion paths with ../ sequences, URL-encoded traversal (e.g., %2e%2e), or common ColdFusion admin paths (cfadmin, CFIDE). High-confidence if request succeeds (HTTP 200) and logs show unusual file access.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution in ColdFusion Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Path traversal that reaches successful execution. Must detect when ColdFusion spawns child processes or loads/executes external binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous process creation under ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java.exe if using Lucee). Flag unexpected child processes, especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripts spawned from web-accessible paths. Correlate timing with path-traversal web attempts.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Due Date Risk: CVE-2026-48282 (2026-07-10)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10. Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators.' Compliance/risk reporting required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch status of CVE-2026-48282 against 2026-07-10 deadline. Flag any systems still unpatched as of due date. Generate compliance report for audit trail. This is both a technical and regulatory gap.

suggestion.title: Detect Ransomware Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on BlackCat ransomware attacks causing 'encryption' of victim systems; pipeline failed to map T1486 or suggest detection for bulk file encryption patterns characteristic of ransomware impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes performing high-volume file modifications with encryption-like signatures (rapid writes to .lock, .encrypted, or ransom-note-named files; correlate with parent process indicative of ransomware families like BlackCat variants).

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Harvesting Prior to Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: BlackCat attacks described in prosecution articles typically involve credential theft (T1087, T1555, T1111) to move laterally; no detection logic for discovery or credential-access phases was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, ProcDump, procdump.exe with lsass target, or living-off-the-land binary misuse like reg query HKLM\\SAM) or suspicious LSASS access prior to remote execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement via Remote Services
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware prosecution articles implicate lateral movement to propagate encryption; pipeline did not suggest detection for T1021 variants or suspicious RDP/PsExec/WMI usage typical of BlackCat post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious execution of psexec.exe, mstsc.exe with unusual parent processes, WMI command-line invocations, or RDP traffic to internal IP ranges from single sources targeting multiple hosts in short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Exfiltration to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: BlackCat employs double-extortion tactics (article context implies data theft prior to encryption); pipeline did not suggest use cases for T1041 or detection of exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure or cloud staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large data transfers (>500 MB in short window) to external IPs or known attacker-operated storage/C2 domains with file access patterns preceding encryption; flag Rclone, 7zip, WinRAR spawned alongside network egress.

suggestion.title: Detect Command-Line Execution by Ransomware Processes
suggestion.rationale: BlackCat and similar RaaS variants spawn cmd.exe or PowerShell for lateral movement, data enumeration, and system reconnaissance (T1059.001, T1059.003); pipeline produced no detections for this execution phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned from suspicious parents (explorer.exe, winword.exe, chrome.exe, or unknown binaries) with command-line arguments targeting AD discovery (net group, dsquery), file enumeration, or disabling defenses (Defender exclusions, firewall rules).

suggestion.title: Detect Ransom Note Placement and System Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes criminal facilitation of attacks concluding in ransom extortion; pipeline did not suggest detection for ransom-note file creation or Windows startup/wallpaper modification typical of ransomware post-encryption taunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of .txt, .html, or .bmp files named with common ransom-note patterns (RECOVERY_KEY, DECRYPT_ME, etc.) in user home directories, or modification of registry keys for wallpaper/startup programs combined with file encryption indicators.

suggestion.title: Authenticated session + BazaR exploit within time window
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Authenticated PHP Object Injection.' Pipeline should correlate successful login events to the target system with subsequent POST /BazaR requests within minutes, establishing authentication-to-exploitation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication events (login, session creation) to the YesWiki application with POST requests to /BazaR/vue=importer within a 5-10 minute window. Alert on authenticated accounts performing exploit-phase activity outside normal user behavior windows.

suggestion.title: Base64-encoded serialized PHP object in HTTP POST body
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack uses 'base64_decode($entry)' and 'unserialize()' on POST parameter importfiche. Pipeline should detect base64 strings matching PHP serialization grammar ('O:' or 'Tzo' base64 prefixes) in POST bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to YesWiki endpoints for parameters containing base64-encoded strings that decode to PHP serialized object prefixes (Tzo, O:, etc.). Pair with CSVManager.php or importfiche parameter names for high-confidence detection.

suggestion.title: Doctrine gadget chain class instantiation in error logs
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Doctrine RCE1 gadget outcome.' PHP object injection exploitation via specific Doctrine versions typically triggers __destruct/__wakeup methods that log class name errors (e.g., 'Object of class Doctrine\ORM\... could not be converted').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search PHP error logs for attempts to instantiate or convert Doctrine ORM classes (Doctrine\ORM, Doctrine\Common, etc.) in contexts outside normal ORM initialization. Look for __destruct/__wakeup method invocation logs or 'could not be converted to string' errors mentioning Doctrine classes.

suggestion.title: YesWiki config file wakka.config.php modification by non-root account
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies wakka.config.php as post-exploitation persistence target. Web-server processes (php-fpm, apache) should never modify this file during normal operation; modifications indicate successful RCE and persistence attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file modifications to wakka.config.php initiated by php-fpm, apache, nginx, or web-server user accounts. Exclude legitimate system updates. Correlate with POST /BazaR requests from the previous 30 minutes for high-fidelity persistence detection.

suggestion.title: YesWiki unauthenticated request followed by authenticated exploit attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article requires authentication but does not describe whether attackers enumerate or test valid accounts first. Detection should look for failed login attempts followed by successful authenticated POST to BazaR exploit endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences: (1) failed authentication attempts to YesWiki within 15-minute window, followed by (2) successful login, followed by (3) POST /BazaR/vue=importer within 5 minutes. Indicates credential stuffing or compromise before exploitation.

suggestion.title: web.xml / Apache reverse proxy logging of BazaR import endpoint access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes POST to /BazaR/vue=importer endpoint. Organizations running YesWiki behind reverse proxies (nginx, Apache) may log endpoint requests differently. Detection should account for proxy-layer logging patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In reverse proxy (nginx/Apache mod_proxy) logs, look for POST requests to paths matching /bazar, /BazaR, or /tools/bazar with vue=importer parameters. May be logged as encoded URLs (/bazar%2Fimport or similar). Correlate with backend PHP error logs for __destruct/__wakeup failures.

suggestion.title: YesWiki authorization bypass: write-only user invoking unrestricted delete action (CVE-2026-52766)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'no authorization check anywhere in the action body or in the page-deletion path'—the exploit is privilege escalation via action invocation without delete ACL. Missing UC to detect users with write-only permission triggering delete operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate identity/access-management logs showing user assigned write-only role with subsequent POST to erasespamedcomments action targeting pages where user lacks delete permission. Flag if user's ACL lacks delete privilege but action succeeds (HTTP 200/204).

suggestion.title: YesWiki bulk page deletion impact: mass 404 spike post-exploitation (CVE-2026-52766)
suggestion.rationale: Article states action 'deletes every wiki page whose tag appears in that array'—aftermath is accessible pages becoming inaccessible. Missing impact detection via 404/access-denial spike correlating to suppr[] array contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden spike in HTTP 404 responses for wiki page GET requests within 5–15 minutes after POST to erasespamedcomments. Correlate deleted page names against subsequent 404 targets. Alert if 404 count exceeds baseline+3σ.

suggestion.title: YesWiki ACL misconfiguration: erasespamedcomments accessible to unauthenticated or write-only users
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause as 'allow-by-default action ACL model'—action should require delete permission but does not. Missing configuration audit to detect overly-permissive action ACL grants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query YesWiki action ACL for erasespamedcomments: flag if execute permission granted to 'all users', 'authenticated', or roles explicitly lacking delete ACL. Compare against approved baseline; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: YesWiki suspicious write-permission grant preceding delete action (CVE-2026-52766 pre-exploitation indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation often follows rapid permission escalation. Missing detection for write-access grant immediately preceding action invocation—may indicate account compromise or misconfiguration discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequence: (1) user assigned write permission to YesWiki pages, then (2) same user POSTs to erasespamedcomments within <5 minutes. Flag if permission grant originated from unexpected admin or failed auth attempts preceded it.

suggestion.title: YesWiki suppr[] array size anomaly: bulk deletion vs single-item cleanup (CVE-2026-52766 behavioral)
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate admin cleanup typically affects 1–3 pages; exploitation abuse exploits bulk deletion. Missing volumetric detection to distinguish normal maintenance from mass-deletion abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract suppr[] array size from POST URI/body. Alert if single request deletes >10 pages or if daily deletion volume by user exceeds historical +3σ baseline. Cluster on user + source IP + deletion count to detect bulk-operation patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation - Injective SDK
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21 as malicious with 310 downloads before deprecation. Pipeline failed to generate package-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm installs for @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21 or detection of package.json modifications that reference this version. Alert on installation of compromised version within known window (2026-06-08 to 2026-06-XX). Correlate with developer environments and CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: Wallet Credential Exfiltration via SDK Function Call
suggestion.rationale: Article describes precise trigger: 'malware activates when developers use SDK functions that generate or import wallet keys' and captures 'mnemonic seed phrase and private key'. Pipeline missed this behavioral detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of code containing Injective SDK wallet functions (InjectiveWallet generation/import methods). Flag calls to mnemonic or private key functions, especially if followed by base64-encoding operations. Correlate with subsequent HTTP traffic to external endpoints.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST Exfiltration with Base64-Encoded Credentials in Headers
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'encoded the data in base64' and 'sent them' via 'HTTP POST request header' to Injective Labs endpoint, with 2-second queue batching. Pipeline provided no exfiltration detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests from npm package processes (node/npm) to external or infrastructure endpoints containing base64-encoded data in request headers. Flag requests with payloads matching patterns of wallet mnemonics (typically 12–24 space-separated words encoded) or 64-character hex private keys. Alert on batched exfiltration patterns (multiple keys in single POST).

suggestion.title: Compromised GitHub Account Publishing Malicious npm Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker compromised a GitHub account belonging to a legitimate project contributor and made the first suspicious commits on June 8'. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for GitHub account compromise and automated malicious release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub contributor account activity for anomalies: commits from new IP/device, rapid commit-to-release cycles (hours), publishing to multiple dependent packages simultaneously, and version tags that jump or use unusual patterns. Flag accounts that push directly to main without PR review and immediately trigger CI/CD release pipeline.

suggestion.title: Multi-Package Coordinated Malicious Release
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker also published version 1.20.21 for another 17 packages associated with the project, pinning all of them to the compromised SDK version.' Single-package detection insufficient; needs correlation across dependency tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect simultaneous or near-simultaneous (within minutes) publishing of malicious versions across multiple npm packages from same owner/organization. Alert on coordinated version pinning to a common dependency (e.g., 17 packages all pinning to same SDK version in single release batch). Correlate with GitHub commit timestamps.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Poison - Transitive Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: '87 direct dependencies on npm and very likely multiple additional transitive dependencies', 'cumulative download count of a little over 112,000'. Pipeline missed transitive compromise scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan installed dependencies for presence of @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21 anywhere in dependency tree, not just direct installs. Flag projects with 87+ direct dependencies (high transitive risk) that have installed malicious version. Generate software bill of materials (SBOM) and cross-reference against known-compromised package registry.

suggestion.title: Embedded Device Privilege Escalation via Filesystem Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unpatched flaws' in filesystem bundled into devices—filesystem vulnerabilities are canonical privilege escalation vectors, yet no elevation-detection UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor embedded device processes for direct filesystem syscalls (open, read, write, ioctl) targeting /proc, /sys, or device files from unprivileged context. Flag transitions from low to high privilege after filesystem operations.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Structure Exploitation - Abnormal Inode/Metadata Access
suggestion.rationale: Filesystem flaws often enable direct inode/metadata manipulation; article mentions flaws in 'filesystem' itself, requiring detection of low-level filesystem access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes attempting direct block-device or filesystem metadata access via ioctl, pread, or raw device operations. Alert on writes to filesystem reserved areas or unexpected calls to fsck, mkfs, or partition-manipulation tools.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Embedded Device Inventory Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'millions of embedded devices' ship with vulnerability—pipeline should map affected device OS versions, manufacturers, and product lines to enable inventory correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate embedded device OS/firmware versions against known-vulnerable filesystem builds (once CVEs/vendors identified). Enumerate devices reporting vulnerable filesystem versions via management protocols (SSH banner, SNMP sysDescr, HTTP User-Agent).

suggestion.title: Persistence via Filesystem Boot/Init Vector
suggestion.rationale: Filesystem vulnerabilities in embedded systems often persist across reboot; article's critical severity and embedded-device scope suggest persistent compromise is a threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to mount points, fstab, init.d, or systemd-boot configurations on embedded devices. Detect attempts to install or modify filesystem drivers, loadable kernel modules, or bootloader-stage code.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Filesystem Syscall Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Unpatched filesystem flaws in publicly available embedded firmware are immediate RCE targets; article severity 'crit' signals likely remote exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect crash/OOM patterns on embedded devices after network inbound (indicating crash-based exploitation). Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by system daemons or root-owned network services after filesystem-heavy operations.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear T1190 exploitation narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion servers for HTTP requests containing directory traversal patterns (.., encoded variants) in request paths, particularly targeting administrative or file-system resources. Correlate with CVE-2026-48282 scanner alerts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline missed execution-phase detection despite explicit RCE impact in threat description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from ColdFusion runtime (java.exe under cfusion parent) with unexpected command-line arguments, environment changes, or file I/O to sensitive paths post-path-traversal exploitation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' in Recommended hunts section with template substitution for CVE-2026-48282. Pipeline failed to instantiate despite template guidance provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all ColdFusion instances (ports 8500/8501/8000) Internet-accessible. Correlate patch levels against CVE-2026-48282. Flag unpatched instances and cross-reference against scanner silence (patches not applied despite vulnerability awareness).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Administrator Panel Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploitation typically precedes administrative access attempts. Article mentions execution 'in context of current user,' implying escalation from web context to privileged operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to ColdFusion Administrator paths (/CFIDE/administrator/) for authentication anomalies, failed login sequences preceding path traversal patterns, or access from non-administrative source networks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status guarantees active exploitation. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends 'one quick check across your fleet.' Pipeline should trigger scanner-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline ColdFusion vulnerability scanner submissions for CVE-2026-48282. Flag scanner results showing 'vulnerable' status post-patch-due-date (2026-07-10). Cross-reference with network flow data for exploitation attempts to flagged instances.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Unpatched Adobe ColdFusion (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unpatched ColdFusion instances exposed to internet; cross-reference asset inventory against CVE-2026-48282 patch status. Flag any systems showing ColdFusion version < [vendor-specified patched version] with network-accessible admin or application ports.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt: ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'path traversal vulnerability' as attack vector; this is a detectable exploitation pattern that pipeline omitted entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints for path traversal payloads (e.g., `../`, `..\`, `%2e%2e`, `....//`); alert on sequences that access sensitive system paths or configuration files outside intended ColdFusion application directories.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Execution: ColdFusion Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' — RCE is the impact, but pipeline captured no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new process creation or command execution spawned from ColdFusion worker processes (cfusion.exe, coldfusion service account context); especially suspicious if child processes are cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or outbound network tools immediately following exploitation timeframe.

suggestion.title: Adobe ColdFusion Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states this is 'currently being exploited' and requires federal remediation by 2026-07-10. Baseline hunt for ColdFusion web servers (port 8500, HTTP server fingerprints). Article establishes the attack surface explicitly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ColdFusion instances exposed on the network via HTTP banners (Server: Adobe ColdFusion/...), port scanning results, or vulnerability scanner confirmations. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify unpatched versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' that 'could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Detect exploitation attempts using directory traversal patterns in HTTP requests to known ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to ColdFusion web roots containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e) or attempts to access sensitive directories (WEB-INF, admin, etc.) that are consistent with CVE-2026-48282 exploitation. Filter for HTTP 200 responses indicating successful path resolution.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Post-Exploitation RCE Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploit, expect command execution, file write, or process spawn from ColdFusion application processes (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful path-traversal indicators (HTTP 200 to ColdFusion traversal payloads) with subsequent spawning of child processes from ColdFusion application threads (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash). Look for unusual parent-child process relationships where ColdFusion initiates system commands.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Web Shell Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal → code execution likely results in web shell upload to ColdFusion web root. Article does not explicitly mention this, but RCE vulnerability exploitation pattern is well-established.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion web root directories (typically /<COLDFUSION_ROOT>/wwwroot and subfolders) for new file creation or unexpected modification of .cfm, .jsp, .asp files. Correlate with path-traversal HTTP requests. Alert on files with suspicious naming (shell, admin, upload, cmd, etc.) or recently modified binaries/scripts in web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability'—this is the core attack step. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being directly detectable: HTTP requests containing ../, ..\, and URL-encoded variants targeting ColdFusion application paths (e.g., /cfusion/, /CFIDE/).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints (URI patterns matching /cfusion, /CFIDE, /admin) containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode variants, null bytes). Correlate with ColdFusion process user privileges. Flag any 200-range responses to these patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Access from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states path traversal 'could lead to arbitrary code execution'—RCE implies file system access beyond normal application scope. Missing detection: ColdFusion process reading files outside its intended directory tree (e.g., accessing system configs, web root parent directories, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ColdFusion process (java.exe, cfusion.exe) accessing files with paths traversing upward (../, parent directory navigation). Baseline normal ColdFusion data paths; flag access to system folders, Windows, Program Files, etc. Consider parent-child process relationship (ColdFusion spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe post-traversal).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection + Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV with federal patch due 2026-07-10. Pipeline failed to surface compliance-centric detection: asset inventory + vulnerability confirmation. Missing: hunt for ColdFusion instances vulnerable to this CVE, correlated with patch status and exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for ColdFusion instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282. Cross-reference against CMDB/asset inventory to identify internet-facing instances. Correlate patch management logs to detect systems past federal due-date (2026-07-10) without remediation. Flag for immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Child Process Execution Post-Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—this implies process spawning. Missing detection: unusual child processes spawned by ColdFusion (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, rundll32.exe) as post-RCE activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ColdFusion process (java.exe, cfusion.exe) spawning shell interpreters or LOLBins (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, wmic.exe, rundll32.exe). Filter baseline/expected child processes (e.g., legitimate scheduled tasks). Flag any unsigned, obfuscated, or network-connected child processes.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Access (ColdFusion Privilege Escalation Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal to ColdFusion config files (neo-security.xml, Application.cfm, web.config) could expose credentials or enable privilege escalation. Article mentions 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—config theft is a likely precursor to lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process reading neo-security.xml, neo-datasource.xml, Application.cfm, cfapplication.cfc, or web.config files multiple times within short time window. This suggests adversary enumerating config for credentials or application secrets.

suggestion.title: Network Outbound Activity from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, article doesn't explicitly mention exfil, but RCE in ColdFusion context often leads to C2 communication or data exfil. Missing detection: unusual outbound connections initiated by ColdFusion application process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections initiated by ColdFusion process (java.exe, cfusion.exe) to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially non-HTTP/HTTPS ports or known C2 infrastructure. Correlate timing with path traversal attempt detection. Flag HTTPS/DNS tunneling patterns.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attempt Detection (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'contains a path traversal vulnerability' — direct initial-access attack surface against public-facing application. T1190 explicitly listed in article but pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Adobe ColdFusion endpoints for path traversal payloads (../, ..\ , %2e%2e%2f, Unicode variants). Correlate with HTTP 403/401 responses or ColdFusion application logs showing access-denied events. Flag successful traversals (2xx HTTP) or file-access attempts outside application directory root.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Arbitrary Code Execution (CVE-2026-48282 RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' — attack consequence critical to detection. No UC generated despite this being the impact driver.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java.exe) with suspicious command-line arguments (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe, whoami). Alert on privilege-escalation indicators (SYSTEM/Administrator process inheritance) or process execution within 5 minutes of path-traversal HTTP requests to same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Inventory and Patch Compliance (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status ('observed exploited in the wild') and federal due date 2026-07-10; asset exposure hunt template explicitly referenced but not instantiated. Patch lag is noted as 'silent killer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate systems running Adobe ColdFusion (software inventory, listening ports 8500/8501, registry keys). Cross-correlate against vulnerability scanner results flagging CVE-2026-48282 vulnerable status. Alert on patch lag >30 days past due date (2026-07-10) and systems with conflicting patch-claimed vs. scanner-detected status.

suggestion.title: Exposed ColdFusion Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'public-facing application' as attack surface. T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) requires initial discovery. No UC generated for detecting external-facing ColdFusion instances via port fingerprinting or HTTP headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to ColdFusion default ports (8500, 8501) or CFIDE admin paths from external networks. Correlate with ColdFusion-specific HTTP headers or CFML error responses indicating service discovery.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack vector as 'path traversal vulnerability.' No UC generated for detecting exploitation attempts. Standard traversal patterns (../../, %2e%2e, Unicode encoding) targeting ColdFusion file/admin endpoints should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences (/, %2e%2e, %252e, ..%252f) in URI or parameters targeting ColdFusion paths (/CFIDE/, /cf_scripts/, /cfusion/). Flag requests from external sources with HTTP 200 or 302 responses.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanning Gaps
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE ID, criticality, and federal remediation deadline (2026-07-10). CISA KEV means active exploitation in the wild. No UC generated for detecting unpatched ColdFusion instances against this specific CVE despite explicit guidance in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference ColdFusion software inventory against known-vulnerable version ranges for CVE-2026-48282. Flag any instances with versions below patch release date of 2026-07-10 as immediately exploitable assets.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Post-Exploitation Process Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Path traversal-to-RCE chains typically involve shell spawning or tool staging. No UC generated for detecting execution phase despite clear impact statement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe, cfusion_exe, java.exe) spawning unexpected command shells, creating files in web-accessible paths, or establishing outbound connections to non-allowlisted IPs within minutes of path traversal HTTP activity.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Webshell Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal → code execution typically chains to .cfm webshell writes for persistence. Article describes arbitrary code execution but no correlation-based UC generated for detecting file creation followed by HTTP execution of that file.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem writes of .cfm or .cfc files to web-accessible directories (webapp root, /uploads/, /temp/) with subsequent HTTP GET/POST requests to those paths returning HTTP 200 within a short window, indicating webshell execution.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Admin Console Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal commonly targets admin endpoints (/CFIDE/administrator/, /CFIDE/adminapi/) to bypass authentication and modify configuration. Article implies RCE but no UC generated for detecting admin console compromise post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated HTTP 200 responses to /CFIDE/administrator/ or /CFIDE/adminapi/ endpoints from external sources, or successful admin login events followed immediately by configuration file modifications or new user creation in ColdFusion datasource settings.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Public-Facing Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and sets federal patch due 2026-07-10. Any detection is urgent and requires immediate remediation per CISA KEV policy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any asset where vulnerability scanners report CVE-2026-48282. Cross-reference public-facing Adobe ColdFusion instances via internet-facing port scans or Shodan-equivalent telemetry. Set threshold to zero—federal due date enforcement.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Patterns on ColdFusion Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack vector. HTTP request logs (WAF, web server) will contain traversal payloads (../, ..%2f, encoded variants) targeting CF admin or upload paths prior to compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests with path traversal patterns on known ColdFusion endpoints (/cfadmin, /administrator, /upload). Correlate HTTP 200 responses or 5xx errors that precede process spawning. Encode for both unencoded (../) and URL-encoded (..%2f) variants.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Spawning Shell Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploitation will manifest as ColdFusion (w3wp.exe, java.exe, cfusion) launching cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or scripting interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal ColdFusion child processes; alert on spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, wget, curl from CF process without prior approval. Correlate process timing with HTTP logs from same source IP to confirm path traversal → RCE chain.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Writes to ColdFusion Webroot
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attacker writes webshells or payloads to web-accessible directories. Article's 'arbitrary code execution' implies persistent tool deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification in ColdFusion webroot (htdocs, wwwroot, webapps) by CF process user context. Flag .cfm, .jsp, .asp, or executable payloads (.exe, .dll, .sh). Cross-correlate with preceding HTTP path traversal requests in web server logs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE compromise will establish outbound callbacks. Monitor dormant ColdFusion hosts for anomalous network egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal ColdFusion egress (Windows Update, internal LDAP, optional plugin repos); alert on new external IPs, high-frequency connections to non-standard ports (8080–8888, 4443, 9999), or DNS to domains outside whitelist. Correlate with process spawning events.

suggestion.title: Title/Body CVE Mismatch — Data Quality Halt
suggestion.rationale: Article title claims CVE-2024-13161 (Ivanti EPM) while body describes CVE-2026-48282 (Adobe ColdFusion). This is a critical discrepancy that should trigger validation before any rules are published.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Not a detection rule. Implement schema validation: title CVE must match body CVE. If mismatch detected, return error and request source clarification. Both CVEs should be validated independently to prevent downstream confusion and wasted analyst time.

Flag any instances where vulnerability scanner reports 'not vulnerable' but ColdFusion version is known-affected (patch lag).

Path traversal payloads use ../ or similar sequences; detection should inspect HTTP request URIs and POST bodies for these patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt web access logs for HTTP requests targeting ColdFusion application directories (e.g., /cf_root, /CFIDE) that contain path traversal sequences (../ or ..\). Look for encoded variants (%2e%2e/, %2f) and requests with unusual file-extension sequences (.cfm, .jsp, .asp combined with ../).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution from ColdFusion Process Context

Flag unexpected process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, perl, python) from these parents, especially when preceded by HTTP requests containing path traversal patterns. Correlate process creation with suspicious file modifications in web-accessible directories.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access by ColdFusion processes for reads outside typical application directories: parent traversal (..\config, ..\..\windows), system configuration files (web.config, machine.config, cfusion.ini), authentication stores (SAM registry, shadow files), or encryption keys. Correlate with HTTP request logs showing path traversal patterns in the same time window.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Administrative Console Exploitation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to /CFIDE paths (e.g., /CFIDE/administrator, /CFIDE/main/index.cfm) combined with path traversal payloads. Flag repeated 403/401 responses followed by 200 responses to /CFIDE, suggesting successful bypass of authentication. Monitor for POST requests to /CFIDE/administrator endpoints from external IPs.

Baseline per kernel version to account for legitimate application patterns.

suggestion.title: Session token creation anomaly (instant JWT/session issue post-login)
