suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file upload endpoints (typically /attachments, /uploads) for POST requests with executable file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5). Alert on 200 responses followed by GET requests to the uploaded file path. Baseline normal file types and sizes per endpoint.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning Shell - Post-Upload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution' but pipeline missed detection for process execution initiated by uploaded code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when web server processes (apache2, nginx, php-fpm, httpd) spawn unexpected child processes, especially shells (cmd.exe, bash, sh, powershell). Correlate process creation with recent file upload activities within web-writable directories. Flag if parent is web service and child is shell or encoding tool.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connection from Web Server - Reverse Shell Indicator
suggestion.rationale: PHP code execution could establish reverse shells; article's execution phase implies potential C2 activity not addressed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections initiated by web server processes to non-standard ports or external IP ranges. Alert on web server DNS queries for dynamic DNS providers or known C2 domains. Correlate with file upload timing to establish causal chain.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Hit - iCagenda Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates patching by 2026-07-13; pipeline failed to produce a basic asset-exposure UC for vulnerability scanning despite referencing templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner results matching CVE-2026-48939 or iCagenda version detection. Cross-reference against patching database to identify unpatched instances. Escalate to critical if exposed to internet-facing interfaces. Flag any instances past federal due date (2026-07-13) as non-compliant.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Encoding - Base64/Obfuscation Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dangerous type' uploads; sophisticated attackers often obfuscate PHP to evade detection. Pipeline did not address defense evasion within execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uploaded files containing base64_decode(), eval(), assert(), create_function(), or similar PHP deobfuscation patterns. Alert on multi-stage uploads where first file uploads a second file containing obfuscated code. Monitor for PHP errors related to execution of encoded payloads in upload directory.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Application Log - Failed/Successful Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates exploited CVE; application logs should show unusual file operations or upload failures/successes. Pipeline missing application-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate iCagenda application logs for upload feature errors or successes with unusual file types. Alert on repeated upload attempts with different file extensions (indicate scanning for bypass). Monitor application logs for PHP warnings/errors from upload directory execution. Flag any logs indicating file type validation bypasses.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure - iCagenda CVE-2026-48939
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Zero UCs generated despite clear, actionable guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scanner databases and asset inventories for CVE-2026-48939 or unpatched iCagenda instances. Correlate against federal remediation deadline (2026-07-13). Prioritize exposed instances reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via iCagenda File Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' No execution-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file upload endpoints for PHP-executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5, .phar) or MIME-type mismatches masking PHP payloads. Correlate uploads with subsequent code execution or process spawning events.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted Upload Mechanism Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'file attachment feature' as specific attack vector but no UC targets this input mechanism directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP multipart POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints with suspicious content-type headers, polyglot files, or binary content in documented attachment parameters. Alert on successful 200-201 responses to upload requests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' leading to 'PHP code upload.' No detection rule generated despite this being the exploit vector. Splunk/KQL rules should trigger on non-document file types (.php, .exe, .jsp, .phtml) uploaded via iCagenda.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints for file types with dangerous MIME types or executable extensions. Flag uploads that do not match whitelisted attachment types (e.g., .pdf, .docx, .jpg). Correlate with vulnerable iCagenda versions identified by vulnerability scanner.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Following Upload (Post-Compromise Signal)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution' but pipeline generated zero detections for the execution phase. This is the post-exploitation indicator confirming successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP process spawning from iCagenda installation directories or unexpected PHP script execution in upload/attachment directories. Cross-reference process creation with preceding suspicious file uploads. Web server logs should show HTTP 200 responses to attachment endpoint followed by unusual PHP execution patterns or system command invocations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Asset Inventory and Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry with federal patch deadline 2026-07-13 (active exploitation confirmed in wild). Pipeline omitted CVE as IOC. Vulnerability scanning and asset inventory must flag all iCagenda instances and enforce patch deadline enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-48939 matches. Generate automated high-priority alerts for unpatched iCagenda instances discovered on public-facing assets or DMZ. Cross-check software inventory against known vulnerable versions. Set automatic remediation deadline callback for 2026-07-13.

suggestion.title: Upload Validation Bypass Attempts via File Extension Fuzzing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers typically test multiple executable file extensions (.php, .php7, .phtml, .pht, .php5) to circumvent simplistic upload validation. Article does not exclude this defensive evasion; pipeline should anticipate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential upload attempts from same source IP/user session within short time window (5 min), testing multiple file extensions to the same attachment endpoint. Alert threshold: ≥3 rejected uploads with different file type extensions from single source indicates active exploitation probing.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Unpatched iCagenda Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in […/_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>.' Pipeline generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for iCagenda instances across your network via vulnerability scanners or active web probing. Correlate with patch status via CMDB or endpoint tools. High-confidence hit if version < patched build or CVE-2026-48939 detected.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Upload to Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload of arbitrary files … ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' This is the core attack execution step; no detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file upload endpoints for .php, .phtml, .php3+ extensions or double-extension bypasses (.php.jpg). Alert on write+execute patterns in upload directories. Baseline upload frequency per user/IP first.

suggestion.title: Post-Upload Process Execution in Web Application Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code execution' following upload; execution context not captured in kill chain or UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web server process creation (apache, nginx, php-fpm) spawning child processes immediately after successful POST to upload endpoint. Look for shell_exec, passthru, or system() calls in application logs if available.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Known Vulnerable Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'file attachment feature' as attack vector but pipeline did not map endpoint or behavior detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web logs for POST/PUT requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints (typically /attachments, /media/upload, etc.). Flag requests with suspicious Content-Type mismatches (e.g., application/x-php submitted as image/jpeg).

suggestion.title: iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 Exploitation Attempt — Public-Facing Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'. Pipeline generated zero use cases for this CISA KEV (active exploitation in wild).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP POST requests to iCagenda upload/attachment endpoints from external/untrusted sources. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unpatched iCagenda versions. Alert on successful uploads (HTTP 200/201) to publicly accessible instances.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Upload Detection — iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'PHP code upload and execution'. Pipeline missed this specific exploit step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload directories for creation of .php, .jsp, .asp files. Trigger on mismatches between submitted filename extension and Content-Type header. Alert on executable file types appearing in web-accessible attachment folders within 60s of upload request.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'. Pipeline did not generate an execution-phase detection despite this being the impact clause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi, apache2) spawning unexpected child processes (cmd, powershell, bash) within 2 minutes of file upload to iCagenda. Track HTTP GET requests to newly uploaded files with PHP extension and executable content.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Exposure Inventory — CVE-2026-48939
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-13'. Pipeline mentioned template reference but generated no asset-exposure use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all internet-accessible iCagenda instances via port scan, DNS CNAME/A records, or web signatures. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner patch status for CVE-2026-48939. Alert on any unauthenticated upload endpoints reachable from external networks.

suggestion.title: File Upload Validation Bypass — Extension/MIME Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unrestricted upload' explicitly indicates insufficient file type validation. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases for upload validation bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag uploads where filename extension differs from Content-Type header or file magic bytes. Specifically monitor for .php uploads with Content-Type: image/* or application/octet-stream. Establish baseline of expected file types per upload directory.

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' This is the exploit vector and entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda instances for POST requests to attachment/upload endpoints with suspicious file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .phar). Alert on successful uploads (HTTP 200/201) followed by immediate or near-immediate file access (GET requests to upload path) from same source IP.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution' as the impact. Detection must capture process spawning from web-server context or unexpected script interpretation in upload directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe, php-cgi, or php child processes spawned by web server processes (w3wp.exe, apache2, httpd) with parent command lines or working directories containing 'upload', 'attachment', or 'media' paths. Also flag unexpected cmd.exe/powershell.exe spawned from web server processes post-upload.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Inventory: iCagenda Public-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article implies exploitation against 'public-facing applications' and mandates federal remediation by 2026-07-13. Foundational hunt: identify and track all exposed iCagenda instances in asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for iCagenda instances on internet-facing IPs via ports 80/443. Fingerprint via HTTP headers, known admin paths (/administrator, /index.php?view=), or characteristic URL patterns. Cross-reference against patch inventory; flag any unpatched instances as 'CVE-2026-48939 exploitable.'

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Type Detection in iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dangerous type' uploads. Generic detection for non-image executable extensions appearing in iCagenda media/attachment directories after deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload directory (typically /media, /images/stories, or configured attachment path) for new files with code extensions: .php*, .exe, .jsp, .aspx, .sh, .pl, .py. Alert on creation + access pattern matching uploaded → executed sequence within minutes.

suggestion.title: Zimbra: Crafted Email Triggers Client-Side Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'crafted emails run malicious code in user sessions.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zimbra mail client (web or desktop) for spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or script interpreters within 10 seconds of email receipt. Correlate email event timestamps with process creation events. Alert if spawned process executes with SYSTEM or elevated context from user session.

suggestion.title: Zimbra: JavaScript/HTML Embedded Payload Execution Post-Email
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires malicious payload embedded in 'crafted email' — implies HTML/JavaScript execution. Pipeline missed execution-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zimbra webmail processes and JavaScript engine (jscript.dll, V8) for decoding/deobfuscation patterns (atob, eval, new Function). Flag emails containing Base64 payloads followed by eval() calls or DOM-manipulation methods (innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML) on untrusted content.

suggestion.title: Zimbra: Session Anomalies Following Email Receipt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code execution 'in user sessions' — implies session hijacking, unauthorized actions, or privilege escalation within authenticated context. Pipeline did not map session-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate incoming email timestamps with account activity: new forwarding rules, mass mail operations, contact list exports, or unusual API calls from same session within 5 minutes. Flag if actions differ from user baseline (time-of-day, geo, client) or target sensitive accounts/shared mailboxes.

suggestion.title: Zimbra: Malicious Email Content Filtering and Sandboxing
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'crafted emails' — content-level analysis missing. Pipeline did not generate email-filtering detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan emails targeting Zimbra users for script tags, event handlers (onload, onerror), obfuscated JavaScript patterns, hex/octal encoding, known exploitation payloads. Deduplicate phishing emails by content hash. Sandbox suspicious attachments/links and detonate in Zimbra client simulation environment if available.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Mass File Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware defining behavior not extracted. Gentlemen operations execute encryption post-reconnaissance; detection should trigger on rapid file modification patterns across shares.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single process or thread writing >500 unique files within 5 minutes across C$, D$, or UNC paths; filter legitimate backup/sync tools. Alert on file extension changes to known ransomware markers (.gentlemen suffix patterns if observed in variants).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SMB Scanning and Share Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: RaaS operations perform network reconnaissance pre-encryption. Keywords mention 'affiliate model' implying multi-stage attack. No reconnaissance detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single source enumerating SMB shares across 10+ internal hosts within 10 minutes (net view \\\\HOST or equivalent). Alert on failed access attempts to C$, ADMIN$ across subnets suggesting mapped reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via LSASS Dumping or Registry Secrets Extraction
suggestion.rationale: RaaS campaigns require valid credentials for lateral movement or persistence. No credential-access phase detection suggested despite prevalence in Gentlemen variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process memory access to lsass.exe (C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe read handle opening from non-system processes). Detect registry queries to HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath or credential vaults.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task or Service Creation Post-Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: RaaS infrastructure requires callback mechanisms. Keywords reference 'ruthless rise' suggesting active C2 post-compromise. No persistence or C2 detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe or sc.exe creating tasks/services with suspicious binaries in %Temp%, %AppData%, or obfuscated paths. Alert on services executing PowerShell, cmd.exe with encoded arguments or network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Unattributed External Hosts Prior to Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Gentlemen operates a known breach-and-exfil model before encryption. Keywords reference hospitality/retail targeting. No exfiltration detection suggested despite being core to RaaS workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large outbound data transfer (>100MB in 10 min) to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially cloud storage domains (mega.nz, dropbox, etc.) from database or file-share servers. Correlate with process execution of archive tools (7z, rar, tar) beforehand.

suggestion.title: Potential Defense Evasion via Endpoint Security Disablement
suggestion.rationale: RaaS affiliates routinely disable antivirus and EDR. Article title emphasizes 'ruthless' operations; no evasion-phase detections generated despite near-universal in ransomware playbooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sc.exe, powershell.exe, or reg.exe commands disabling Windows Defender (Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring), stopping WinDefend service, or deleting Event Log entries. Trigger on Windows Defender exclusion path creation for suspicious directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious outbound connection from backend service to TSDProxy management API
suggestion.rationale: Article states token 'forwarded to all proxied backend services'; compromised backend calling management API at 127.0.0.1:8080 with stolen token indicates exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Backend service processes (not TSDProxy itself) establishing outbound TCP connections to 127.0.0.1:8080 or management plane IP. Token leakage enables lateral movement within the service mesh.

suggestion.title: TSDProxy identityHeaders feature enabled on vulnerable build version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'When `identityHeaders` is enabled (the default)'; configuration inspection required to assess default-unsafe state before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection of TSDProxy startup flags or config files with identityHeaders:true or absence of identityHeaders:false. Registry/config file changes indicating feature enablement.

suggestion.title: Authentication token in HTTP request body or headers to backend service endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injects `x-tsdproxy-auth-token` into every upstream HTTP request'; detection of token presence in outbound requests to non-management services indicates credential leakage in action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP requests originating from TSDProxy to upstream backend services containing x-tsdproxy-auth-token header. Should not appear in normal traffic to non-privileged endpoints.

suggestion.title: Malicious Rust Crate `exploration` Installation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies `exploration` (v1, published 2026-06-02) as a malicious package on crates.io containing 'a method that attempted to download and execute a payload from a remote site.' Direct IOC for supply-chain detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for `exploration` crate presence in Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, or package registries. Flag any Rust project with dependency on this crate (any version). Correlate presence with subsequent process spawning or network activity during cargo build/check phases in CI/CD pipelines and developer machines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress During Rust Build
suggestion.rationale: Article states the crate method 'attempted to download' a payload. T1105 ingress must be detected via network telemetry originating from cargo/rustc and child processes during compilation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from cargo.exe, rustc.exe, or children during build execution. Establish baseline of expected package repository domains (crates.io, github.com, gitlab.com). Flag connections to newly-observed external hosts with High confidence if resolved IP has no whitelisted reputation history.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Execution from Cargo/Build Context
suggestion.rationale: T1203 execution of downloaded payload. Rust build.rs scripts and proc macros run at compile-time with full process spawning capabilities. This UC detects cmd/powershell/bash spawning from build tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Rust CI/CD and build environments, alert on child processes spawned by cargo.exe or rustc.exe (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget). Establish a whitelist of approved build scripts and proc macros. Flag unexpected interpreters or network tools as Medium-High confidence indicators of malicious build-time code injection.

suggestion.title: Newly-Published Crate Installed Before Abuse Removal
suggestion.rationale: The advisory notes the malicious crate was published and removed within ~1 hour. Orgs shipping code during this window with no cached lock files need detection of this transient supply-chain risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cargo for installation of crate versions published within 24 hours of first release (anomaly). Cross-reference Cargo.lock timestamps against crates.io publish timestamps. Alert on 'fresh' crate installation (version age < 24h) without prior org approval or release planning. Enforce Cargo.lock pinning in CI to prevent transient malicious version ingestion.

suggestion.title: Proxy Authentication Header Injection from Unexpected Network Path
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker sends 'forged HTTP header' and 'any unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server directly can impersonate any user.' Core attack is header forgery, not network access alone. Need behavioral detection of proxy auth headers appearing in direct (non-proxy) connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileBrowser endpoints for HTTP requests containing proxy authentication headers (X-Remote-User, X-Remote-Groups, REMOTE_USER, etc.) originating from IP addresses that bypass the reverse proxy. Correlate with absence of request in proxy logs for same timestamp. Flag any direct-path connection with these headers as forged authentication attempt.

suggestion.title: Successful Admin Impersonation via Proxy Header Forgery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'impersonate any user - including admin' as primary impact. Detection must identify when admin-level operations occur from non-admin accounts or unexpected network sources via forged headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to FileBrowser admin endpoints (/api/settings, /api/users, resource management) from a source that either: (a) previously failed authentication within 5 min, (b) shows no prior admin activity pattern, or (c) correlates with presence of proxy auth headers in direct connection. Alert on status 200/201 to admin endpoints following failed login or from non-whitelisted source IPs.

suggestion.title: Automatic User Account Creation Without Authentication Event
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'specifying a non-existent username causes the server to automatically create a new user account' — this is the persistence mechanism. Need to detect orphaned account creation events not preceded by legitimate admin action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileBrowser logs or audit events for account creation events (POST to /api/users with HTTP 201, or equivalent account add events). Flag any creation not preceded by authenticated admin action from expected management IPs. Spike detection: more than 3 new accounts created in 1 hour from same source IP outside normal provisioning windows.

suggestion.title: Session Context Confusion: Multiple User Impersonations from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Core attack allows impersonation of 'any user' via forged headers. Behavioral detection should flag rapid user-context switching from single network source, indicating header injection rather than legitimate multi-user access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify single source IP accessing FileBrowser API endpoints as 3+ different user identities within 5-minute window. Especially high-fidelity if: (a) users include admin account, (b) normal activity for those users is segregated by IP/time, or (c) requests use same session/cookie but different auth headers.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Proxy Auth Configuration Exposure via Failed Auth Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability only exploitable when 'configured with proxy authentication (auth.method=proxy).' Attackers probe for this via direct connections and observing auth behavior differences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect probing for proxy auth method by monitoring for repeated unauthenticated requests to FileBrowser endpoints that receive 200/success responses instead of expected 401/403. Alert on patterns: requests to /api/login, /api/settings, /api/users from external IP with no Authorization header but receiving 200 response, suggesting proxy auth is enabled and attacker controls the proxy path.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Operations Post-Proxy-Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: After gaining access via header forgery, attacker gains file access through impersonated identity. Detection should correlate unauthorized FileBrowser API success with subsequent file enumeration/exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FileBrowser /api/resources or file listing endpoints (typically GET /api/resources/path) receiving 200 responses immediately following failed-auth→header-injection sequence. Alert if file operations span sensitive directories or enumerate unusually large file trees in short timeframe, indicating reconnaissance/exfiltration attempt post-bypass.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — direct indicator of initial exploitation vector. Must detect upload POST/PUT requests to known iCagenda upload endpoints with file type validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda installations for POST/PUT requests to upload handlers (/images/upload, /files/upload, /attachments). Flag polyglot or double-extension payloads (.php.jpg, .phtml, .php5). Alert on MIME type mismatches (Content-Type: image/jpeg; Content: <?php). Baseline expected uploads per user/IP and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Web-Accessible Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution' — explicit execution phase. Must detect when uploaded .php files are accessed or when new PHP processes spawn from web server context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php-cgi processes spawning from web server (w3wp.exe, apache2, nginx). Monitor for new .php files written to web-accessible directories (/var/www/html, /inetpub/wwwroot, application upload folders) within 5 minutes of upload requests. Correlate file creation time with HTTP upload POST and subsequent process execution.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Upload Bypass — MIME Validation Failure
suggestion.rationale: Article title highlights 'Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type' — indicates insufficient MIME/extension filtering. Detect when file uploads contain PHP, executable, or script extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse upload POST bodies and HTTP headers to extract Content-Type and filename. Flag mismatches (e.g., .php in filename but image/jpeg in header). Block or alert on dangerous extensions: .php, .php3, .php4, .php5, .phtml, .phar, .jsp, .jspx, .jsw, .asp, .aspx, .cgi, .pl, .cfm, .cer, .asa, .sh. Use hexdump/magic-bytes validation to detect true file type vs. declared MIME.

suggestion.title: iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 — Known Exploited Vulnerability Scan Drift
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV entry: 'observed exploited in the wild' with federal due date 2026-07-13. Pipeline must flag iCagenda instances in vulnerability scans that report patched/missing despite active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system for iCagenda instances with CVE-2026-48939 status. Flag any asset reporting 'patched' or 'not vulnerable' but still running vulnerable version string. Correlate with network egress/HTTP access logs to iCagenda services. Priority: assets with external IP, DNS resolution, or historical web traffic spikes.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Web Server Process Tree — Child Process from PHP/CGI
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation leads to PHP code execution; attacker gains ability to spawn arbitrary child processes. Article's 'PHP code execution' phase implies command injection or system() calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or apache/nginx worker processes spawn children with suspicious cmdlines: cmd.exe /c, powershell.exe, wget, curl, nc.exe. Flag reverse shells (process creation + network connection to external IP on unusual port). Baseline normal PHP child processes (ImageMagick, ffmpeg) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: File Integrity Monitoring — Upload Directory Executable Modification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation results in PHP file write to web-accessible directory. FIM must alert on creation/modification of executable/script types in upload folders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable FIM on iCagenda upload directories (/attachments, /files, /images/upload). Alert on new or modified .php, .phtml, .sh, .bat, .exe files. Include hash baseline check and owner/permission changes. Require approval for uploads outside expected filename patterns (e.g., 'document_YYYYMMDD.pdf').

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'CVE: CVE-2026-48939 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and notes CISA KEV requires active remediation by federal due date 2026-07-13. Pipeline generated zero scanner-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all iCagenda instances in vulnerability scans where CVE-2026-48939 is exploitable. Prioritize systems past federal patch-due date (2026-07-13) and correlate against web-facing asset inventory.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload — Dangerous File Type Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core vulnerability as 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' No file-upload layer detection was produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment endpoints for POST requests uploading executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5, .phar, .exe) or MIME-type mismatches. Alert on success responses followed by directory writes to web-accessible paths.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies final attack outcome as 'PHP code upload and execution,' but pipeline generated no execution-layer detection despite this being the critical impact step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate iCagenda file upload operations with PHP interpreter spawning or HTTP GET/POST requests to recently-uploaded .php files in attachment directories. Look for command-line-like parameters (cmd, exec, system, shell) in request payloads.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Access via iCagenda Upload Directory

suggestion.rationale: Article pinpoints vulnerability in 'variable-base scalar multiplication gadget of `halo2_gadgets`.' No supply-chain hunt detects builds incorporating affected halo2_gadgets versions (< unspecified patch level).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cargo.lock files or build artifacts referencing halo2_gadgets without explicit version pinning or with known-vulnerable versions. Correlate with DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory for affected end-user binaries.

suggestion.title: Consensus rule violation: proof soundness failure in Orchard transactions
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'breaks Orchard Action circuit soundness'—a proof that should fail does not. No hunt detects transactions with invalid or re-created proofs that nonetheless pass consensus.
log_sources: Zcash node ledger, circuit proof logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Full-node operators can re-verify Orchard proofs independently. Hunt for transactions accepted by vulnerable nodes that fail proof re-verification on patched nodes or in isolated circuit validation environments.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted File Upload with Dangerous Type (CVE-2026-48939)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline must detect HTTP POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints with executable extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints for Content-Disposition headers or multipart form data containing PHP, phtml, php3, php4, php5, phar, phps, or other executable extensions. Correlate with recent CVE-2026-48939 scanner activity. Establish baseline upload file types per organization and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Web Root Following iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'PHP code upload and execution.' This is the post-exploitation phase: detection must correlate file uploads with child process spawning or PHP command execution within application directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) or executing system commands within 5 minutes of iCagenda file upload events. Look for PHP files in upload/attachment directories executing unusual binaries. Monitor PHP error logs for eval() or system() calls in recently-written files.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via iCagenda File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'PHP code upload and execution' implies web shell deployment. Pipeline must detect anomalous HTTP patterns (POST requests, rapid queries, encoded parameters) against newly-created PHP files in iCagenda directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to .php files in application upload directories that did not exist in baseline. Detect rapid request sequences, unusual parameter counts, or encoded payloads in POST body. Cross-reference HTTP access logs with filesystem logs showing file creation in upload paths within prior 24 hours.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Vulnerability Scanner Fingerprinting (Pre-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation in the wild. Pipeline should detect reconnaissance probes before exploit attempts. Article implies public exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to iCagenda application files (e.g., /administrator/manifests/packages.xml, /configuration.php, /index.php?option=com_icagenda) with scanner User-Agent patterns (nikto, nessus, qualys, masscan). Detect GET requests from external sources to known vulnerable iCagenda version endpoints.

suggestion.title: Bulk Exploitation Attempts Against iCagenda (CVE-2026-48939)
suggestion.rationale: Mass scanning and exploitation of CISA KEV vulnerabilities is a common attack pattern. Article's 'arbitrary files in file attachment feature' suggests potential for batch/automated exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints from single external IP address. Detect >10 uploads per minute or sequential upload attempts with different file extensions within 1-minute window. Correlate with known iCagenda hosting patterns or default paths.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation C2 Beacon Detection from iCagenda Web Shell
suggestion.rationale: Once PHP code executes (article's 'PHP code upload and execution'), web shell typically initiates outbound C2 connection. Pipeline should detect anomalous outbound connections originating from web application processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from web application processes (w3wp.exe, apache, nginx, php-fpm) to non-standard ports (8080, 8888, 9090) or to external IP addresses with no baseline justification. Monitor for DNS queries to C2 domain patterns or dynamic DNS services from application servers.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Attachment Upload to Dangerous Type
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — entirely unmapped to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart/form-data POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints (typically /index.php?option=com_icagenda with file upload parameters) where file extensions indicate executable or script types (.php, .phtml, .exe, .sh, .asp, .jsp). Alert on uploads lacking MIME-type or extension validation.

suggestion.title: PHP Execution from Recently Uploaded iCagenda Attachments
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'PHP code upload and execution' — execution pattern post-upload is critical attack indicator but entirely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate recently created .php files in iCagenda upload/attachment directories with HTTP GET/POST requests invoking those files. Flag newly-written PHP files in web root followed within seconds/minutes by requests that execute them (indicated by 200 responses, parameter injection, etc.).

suggestion.title: Web Shell Behavior from Uploaded iCagenda Files
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code execution' as final outcome — post-compromise shell behavior (command execution, data exfil) drives incident classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to uploaded PHP files for shell indicators: system-command parameters (cmd=, exec=, system=), encoded payloads, suspicious User-Agents, or patterns matching known web shells (c99, r57). High request volume to single .php file in short window suggests shell interaction.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Asset Exposure Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes active exploitation and federal patch deadline (2026-07-13). Asset discovery is prerequisite to all other hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for iCagenda instances and CVE-2026-48939 patch status. Cross-reference with proxy/WAF logs for traffic patterns matching iCagenda paths (/components/com_icagenda/, /index.php?option=com_icagenda). Flag instances older than vendor patch release date or with known unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Upload Volume to iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Article states arbitrary file upload capability; attack reconnaissance or batch exploitation may involve repeated upload attempts at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal spike in POST requests to iCagenda attachment upload endpoints from single source IP over short window. Baseline expected upload rate per endpoint; flag deviations 5x+ normal, especially with high failure rates (413, 415, file validation errors).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Attachment Directory Access and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability lives in attachment feature; uploads land in predictable directory. Detection must include directory enumeration + execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for directory traversal or path enumeration attempts targeting common iCagenda upload paths (/tmp/icagenda, /images/icagenda, variant paths). Flag 404 responses followed by successful uploads or execution requests; indicate reconnaissance of upload location.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload Endpoint Access (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — must hunt for POST requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints, especially from external IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints (typically /upload, /attachment, or similar) from external sources. Baseline expected file types (documents, images) and alert on executable or script file uploads (.php, .phtml, .exe, .jsp, etc.).

suggestion.title: PHP Web Shell Execution from Upload Directory (T1505.003)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'PHP code upload and execution' — detection must cover execution of newly uploaded PHP files from web-accessible upload directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP GET/POST requests to PHP files in iCagenda upload directories within 1–10 minutes of detected POST uploads. Correlate web server access logs with presence of .php files in upload paths and suspicious PHP process spawning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File in iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload...resulting in PHP code...execution' — file system monitoring must detect unexpected PHP files placed in upload directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload directories for creation of .php files. Establish baseline of expected PHP files (typically 0); alert on any new .php in upload paths. Cross-reference creation timestamps with web access logs to confirm exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'unrestricted upload' — must detect bypass of expected file-type controls, including double-extension, null-byte, or case-variation attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for upload POST requests with filename patterns that bypass restrictions: .php5, .phtml, .phar, .php.jpg, .php%00.jpg, or other polyglot techniques. Alert on requests where Content-Type header claims safe type (image/jpeg) but filename contains executable extensions.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: iCagenda Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability is product-specific to iCagenda; SOC must first identify all instances to scope impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for iCagenda instances. Search web logs for iCagenda-specific paths (/index.php?option=com_icagenda, /media/icagenda). Fingerprint iCagenda by HTTP response headers, page titles, or known path signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' Need detection for POST/PUT requests to iCagenda upload paths with suspicious MIME/extension mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to iCagenda URIs matching *upload*, *attachment*, *file* patterns. Flag when Content-Type header does not align with file extension (e.g., application/x-php declared as .jpg). Baseline legitimate upload patterns to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload and Execution via iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Direct language requires detection for .php and common bypass extensions (.php5, .phtml, .php.jpg) written to web-accessible directories followed by process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation with extensions .php, .php3, .php4, .php5, .php7, .php8, .phtml, .pht in iCagenda application directories. Escalate if php.exe or php-cgi process spawns from these file paths. Include bypass patterns: .php%00, .php...., .phtml.jpg.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Reverse Shell Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain endpoints in 'PHP code upload and execution'—standard post-upload TTP is command execution or outbound connection from web service process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or nc spawned by w3wp.exe, httpd, or apache processes in iCagenda app directories within 2 minutes of file upload. Alert on unexpected outbound TCP connections from web service processes to external IPs on non-standard ports (not 80/443).

suggestion.title: Scan/Brute-Force Pattern on iCagenda Upload Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'file attachment feature' is a discrete attack surface; exploitation typically involves probing. Detection should catch >5 failed requests to upload endpoints in short time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate failed HTTP POST responses (4xx/5xx) to iCagenda file upload paths by source IP. Alert if single source triggers ≥5 failures within 5 minutes, indicating scanning or bypass attempt iteration.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Exploitation Framework/Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active wild exploitation. Need detection for known PoCs, Metasploit modules, or vulnerability scanner fingerprints attempting this CVE against exposed iCagenda instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match User-Agent strings and request patterns against known iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 PoC signatures and Metasploit module behaviors. Correlate with network signatures from threat feeds documenting active exploitation of this CVE.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Suspicious File Upload to Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda's file-attachment endpoints for non-document file types (especially .php, .phtml, .pht).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to iCagenda upload paths (typically /upload, /attachment, /files, /media) containing executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5) or double-extension patterns. Correlate request volume against baseline to detect mass-exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: PHP Process Execution Following iCagenda File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Detect post-exploitation code execution directly tied to the file-upload vulnerability chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 200 POST responses to iCagenda upload endpoints with subsequent php.exe or php-cgi process creation. Flag if PHP process reads from web-accessible upload directories and executes with user-controlled input.

suggestion.title: Unpatched iCagenda Asset Inventory for CVE-2026-48939
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-13.' CVE listed in CISA KEV means active exploitation is underway; asset discovery is the fastest triage control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset management systems for iCagenda product instances. Cross-reference with patch inventory to identify unpatched versions prior to 2026-07-13 deadline. Prioritize externally-facing instances (web-exposed IP:80/443).

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'PHP code upload and execution' via file attachment. Uploaded PHP files can persist as web shells. Monitor attachment directories for suspicious PHP creation post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload/attachment directories for creation or modification of .php files. Alert on any PHP written to web-accessible paths that diverge from expected upload patterns (file type, size, modification time correlation with HTTP POST).

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—the core exploitation vector. Need detection for dangerous file types (PHP, PHTML, JSP, ASPX) uploaded to known iCagenda attachment endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints for uploads of executable file extensions (PHP, PHTML, PHPS, JSP, JSPX, ASP, ASPX). Alert on successful uploads of dangerous types to web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means 'observed exploited in the wild'—highest-priority indicator. Pipeline must flag active reconnaissance and exploitation attempts against this CVE-2026-48939.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to iCagenda matching known CVE-2026-48939 exploit patterns. Monitor for scanning of file attachment endpoints and suspicious parameter values targeting the vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Unexpected PHP Code Execution from Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability results in 'PHP code upload and execution'—post-compromise detection essential to catch active web shells and malicious execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server access logs for HTTP requests executing PHP files from iCagenda upload/attachment directories. Alert on php_cli or child processes spawned by web server user from upload paths.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Exposure and Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries carry federal remediation deadlines (2026-07-13 cited). Standard asset-exposure hunt is mandatory—identify all iCagenda instances and verify patch status before compliance deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for all iCagenda installations. Cross-reference with patch/version status for CVE-2026-48939 remediation. Escalate unpatched instances immediately.

suggestion.title: Zimbra RCE via Crafted Email Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'crafted emails run malicious code in user sessions.' Pipeline omitted IOC extraction and email-based UC entirely. Title establishes email as attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email gateways and Zimbra SMTP logs for crafted MIME structures, malformed headers, or polyglot payloads targeting Zimbra versions. Flag emails that trigger Zimbra server errors, bypass sanitization, or match known RCE exploitation patterns. Correlate with delivery to users running vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution from Zimbra Client Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies code executes 'in user sessions'—post-delivery execution phase. Pipeline produced zero UC for endpoint behavioral indicators. Attacker must achieve code execution via Zimbra (desktop or webmail session).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, sh, bash) directly from Zimbra mail client process or from unsigned binaries launched during email open/preview windows. Flag unexpected script execution tied to mail client session lifecycle. Monitor for LOLBin invocation patterns (regsvcs, InstallUtil, mshta).

suggestion.title: Zimbra Session Hijacking and Unauthorized API Access
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states code runs 'in user sessions'—implies session token theft or impersonation post-exploitation. Pipeline missed credential-access and lateral-movement UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zimbra authentication logs for anomalous session creation immediately following vulnerable email receipt. Detect API calls (GetMailbox, SearchConversation, ExportContacts) using leaked/hijacked session tokens. Flag rapid mailbox exports, forwarding rule creation, or delegate additions within seconds of email interaction.

suggestion.title: Zimbra Vulnerability Exploitation Network Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article references a 'critical flaw' in Zimbra—attackers will probe and exploit unpatched instances. Pipeline should detect exploitation attempts via network-layer signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zimbra web interface (port 8080/8443) and SMTP services (25/587) for requests containing known RCE payload patterns—malformed MIME headers, excessive content-length mismatches, or polyglot script injection. Correlate version detection probes with immediate exploitation attempts. Flag repeated attempts across multiple user mailboxes.

suggestion.title: Detect Ransomware Family 'The Gentlemen' File Activity Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'The Gentlemen Ransomware' but pipeline generated zero impact-phase detections. RaaS operations typically exhibit distinctive encryption signatures and file manipulation patterns that should drive baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file encryption operations on high-value data directories: rapid sequential writes to files with changing byte patterns, bulk file renames with consistent extension patterns (typical: .gentlemen or variant), process activity from unexpected users/services accessing file handles with write permissions, and sudden spikes in file I/O errors indicating encryption-induced failures.

suggestion.title: Detect RaaS Affiliate Lateral Movement (Scorpius-Linked)
suggestion.rationale: Article's RaaS affiliate model implies staged attacks with reconnaissance and lateral movement before encryption. Keywords 'Howling Scorpius' and 'Spikey Scorpius' were not extracted, preventing actor-specific behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SMB/RDP connection sequences from single internal host to multiple targets within minutes; credential validation failures followed by successful logon; and execution of remote admin tools (psexec, wmic, schtasks, Invoke-Command) from compromised endpoints targeting internal IP space.

suggestion.title: Detect Hospitality/Retail Credential Compromise (Pre-Deployment)
suggestion.rationale: Target sectors (hospitality/retail) and affiliate model indicate initial compromise via credential theft. No credential-access phase use case was generated despite this being first-stage for RaaS operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for password spray patterns against hospitality/retail domain accounts, phishing delivery sequences (email gateways), and deployment of password-capture tools (mimikatz, lsass dump, registry hives accessed) in these verticals; correlate with failed logon spikes.

suggestion.title: Detect Pre-Encryption Data Staging and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: RaaS operations exfiltrate data for extortion before encryption; this two-phase model is standard for 'Gentlemen' and similar contemporary families, but pipeline did not surface exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large sequential file reads from databases/shares followed by compression (zip, rar, 7z), archive creation in temp directories, uploads to cloud storage (esp. free tier: mega.io, proton, rclone to S3), and anomalous egress traffic volume/timing to geographically unexpected destinations.

suggestion.title: Detect External Remote Service Abuse for Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Affiliate-model ransomware commonly exploits exposed RDP, VPN, and web services in hospitality environments. No initial-access detection was provided despite this being a common Scorpius-associated TTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful logons to VPN/RDP from unusual geographies, failed authentication storms followed by success, public-facing service exploitation attempts (e.g., web shell uploads to unpatched services), and anomalous traffic to ports 3389/22/443 from non-standard source IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Gentlemen Ransomware C2 Communication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: No command-and-control detection use case generated. RaaS affiliates typically maintain persistent C2 for staging, tasking, and ransom negotiation after encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries to domains associated with Gentlemen/Scorpius infrastructure (track by domain registrar patterns, WHOIS privacy, hosting ASNs), beaconing traffic to newly registered domains, and HTTP/HTTPS POST requests with suspicious User-Agents or non-standard ports to known C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: TSDProxy auth-token forwarded in upstream HTTP requests to sensitive backend services
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'tsdproxy injects x-tsdproxy-auth-token into every upstream HTTP request'. Detection must capture token transit to non-public backends (databases, caches, internal APIs) where token reuse enables lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TSDProxy outbound HTTP requests for x-tsdproxy-auth-token header in upstream requests. Baseline expected backend destinations and alert on requests to sensitive internal services (databases on non-standard ports, management interfaces, configuration services). High-fidelity indicator of token leakage into supply-chain attack surface.

suggestion.title: Management API privilege escalation via replayed TSDProxy auth-token from non-localhost source
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'token is the same secret used by the management HTTP server to trust forwarded requests'. Post-theft exploitation: attacker replays stolen token to localhost management API from external host to escalate privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authenticated requests (x-tsdproxy-auth-token header) to /api/v1 management endpoints where source IP != 127.0.0.1. True positive rate high; attacker must exfiltrate token then replay externally. Correlate with backend /debug/headers access attempts.

suggestion.title: TSDProxy identityHeaders enabled configuration audit in production environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'identityHeaders is enabled (the default)'. Configuration-level detection identifies vulnerable deployments before exploitation. Correlate with sensitive backend inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit TSDProxy process arguments or config files for identityHeaders=true or --identityHeaders flag present. For each instance, enumerate configured backend services. Flag if backends include databases, internal APIs, credential stores, or other high-value targets.

suggestion.title: Adversary enumeration of TSDProxy management API endpoints via stolen token
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise: attacker uses replayed token to probe management API for accessible endpoints, configuration, or backend inventory to maximize lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential requests to /api/v1/* endpoints authenticated via x-tsdproxy-auth-token from single source IP, especially GET requests to /api/v1/backends, /api/v1/config, /api/v1/auth. Volume spike or 4xx response pattern followed by successful exploitation is high-fidelity compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Malicious Rust Package Installation via Cargo
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploration crate attempted to download and execute a payload.' Users running `cargo install exploration` or importing it as a dependency would trigger the malicious code. Package manager invocations are observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cargo add/install commands targeting known-malicious packages (exploration and future variants). Correlate with crate metadata (publication date near removal, zero downloads). Cross-reference against Rustsec advisory feed and Socket.dev threat intelligence.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution During Rust Build/Dependency Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempted to download and execute a payload from a remote site.' Payload download and execution occur at build time or import time. Detect child processes or network calls spawned by rustc, cargo, or build scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for subprocess creation (cmd.exe, powershell, bash) or download utilities (curl, wget) spawned by cargo, rustc, or Rust crate build scripts. Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to non-standard domains initiated during dependency resolution or build phases.

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Anomaly — Rapid Publication and Removal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'had 1 version published on 2026-06-02, approximately 1 hour before removal, and had no evidence of actual usage.' Short lifespan and zero adoption are red flags for test-publish-removal malware campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query crates.io registry API for packages with publication-to-removal intervals < 24 hours and zero download counts. Flag and cross-check against vulnerability advisories. Extend detection to npm, PyPI, and other registries using the same anomaly pattern.

suggestion.title: Outbound DNS/HTTP from Rust Crate Initialization Code
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malicious code 'attempted to download and execute a payload from a remote site.' Network egress during package import or build is anomalous and detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries or HTTP connections initiated from within Rust build/initialization contexts targeting unverified domains. Defanged payload URL(s) are likely in the full article; create pattern rules for similar domains and file hashes if IOCs surface in follow-up reporting.

suggestion.title: Proxy authentication header in direct connections (X-Remote-User origin anomaly)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can send a single forged HTTP header' and notes 'any unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server directly'. The attack's signature is X-Remote-User (or similar proxy headers) present in connections that bypass the proxy. Current UCs detect /api/login POST and admin endpoints but don't isolate the header forgery signal itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests containing proxy auth headers (X-Remote-User, X-Remote-Groups, X-Remote-Name, etc.) originating from non-internal, non-proxy-category IPs to FileBrowser. High fidelity: these headers should ONLY appear when traffic flows through the proxy. Direct connections with these headers indicate forgery or misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Successful authentication with non-existent user account creation (201/new user)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'specifying a non-existent username causes the server to **automatically create a new user account**'. This is a direct account creation primitive. Detections should target HTTP 201 (Created) or account-creation events correlated with /api/login requests using forged proxy headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate /api/login POST with HTTP 201 response or FileBrowser account creation events. Cross-reference source IP: if account is created from external IP with X-Remote-User header, user doesn't exist in system yet, and login succeeds, this indicates account-creation abuse. Flag especially if username is 'admin' or other privileged account.

suggestion.title: Admin-level API actions without standard privilege escalation workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates admin impersonation: 'impersonate **any user - including admin**'. Detection UC_9_4 flags admin endpoints, but should correlate with authentication path. An external IP successfully calling /api/settings or /api/users without (a) local login or (b) proxy-mediated auth suggests privilege escalation via header forgery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: admin APIs (/api/settings, /api/users, /api/resources) should only be callable from authenticated sessions initiated via proxy or internal network. Alert when external IP calls these endpoints without prior successful /api/login or proxy-originated session token. Combine with absence of standard session cookies/bearer tokens.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser authentication configuration exposure (auth.method=proxy)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability ONLY exploitable when 'FileBrowser is configured with proxy authentication (`auth.method=proxy`)'. Detection should prioritize environments where this config is active. Recon/hunting should target systems with this config before assuming they are vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for FileBrowser instances with auth.method=proxy in config files. Cross-reference with UC_9_2 (direct public inbound). Systems with both direct-public access AND proxy auth mode are high-risk. Alternatively, flag when proxy auth mode is enabled on systems previously configured with other auth methods (possible attacker hardening).

suggestion.title: Session hijacking: FileBrowser admin session from non-admin source IP
suggestion.rationale: Article's core claim: 'impersonate **any user**'. Detecting successful admin actions from a source IP that has no prior login/auth session is a strong behavioral signal. Attacker forges header to create admin session instantly without credential exchange.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline admin session sources (approved admins, jump boxes, proxy IPs). Alert on admin-level API calls (200+ HTTP status on /api/users or /api/settings) from IPs outside this baseline that have no session initiation event (no /api/login 200 or proxy handshake).

suggestion.title: HTTP requests with chrome-extension:// Origin header to SiYuan admin API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unconditionally trusts all `chrome-extension://` origins, granting `RoleAdministrator` access.' This is the CORE exploitation signature — the Origin header is the attacker's credential. Pipeline missed the most specific indicator of in-flight exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SiYuan kernel HTTP server logs (127.0.0.1:6806) for API calls bearing 'Origin: chrome-extension://' header. Presence of such header + successful admin API call (no AccessAuthCode supplied) = active exploitation. Baseline: no legitimate SiYuan traffic should originate from extension contexts.

suggestion.title: Browser extension making outbound network calls to localhost admin ports
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'any Chrome/Chromium extension can make fully authenticated admin calls.' Extensions normally access web; reaching localhost:6806 is anomalous. Complements UC_10_4 by adding *origin* context to inbound traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate extension installation (UC_BROWSER_EXT) with network connections to localhost:6806 within 5min. Flag if extension's manifest does not declare localhost networking permissions or if permissions were recently escalated (supply-chain compromise signal).

suggestion.title: SiYuan kernel instances with empty or missing AccessAuthCode

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda attachment/upload endpoints for Content-Disposition headers or multipart form data containing .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .phar, or .inc extensions. Flag requests where file extension does not match declared MIME type.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: PHP execution is the attack outcome: 'PHP code upload and execution.' Detection of PHP/Apache/nginx processes spawning children from upload directories indicates successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is php.exe, apache2, or nginx and child process spawns from iCagenda's attachment/upload directory path. Alert on non-web-utility binaries spawned from upload dirs (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash).

suggestion.title: File Write to iCagenda Upload Directory with Executable Extension
suggestion.rationale: Precursor to PHP execution: 'upload of arbitrary files' must persist to disk. Monitor file system writes to iCagenda's file attachment directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file create or write operations to iCagenda upload/attachment directories with executable extensions (.php, .sh, .exe, .bat, .cmd, .phtml, .pgif, .pjpg, .png.php). Correlate with POST requests lacking MIME type validation.

suggestion.title: HTTP 200/201 Response to iCagenda Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation requires the upload to be accepted. Article states 'upload of arbitrary files' without rejection, implying validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal upload file types/sizes for iCagenda. Alert on POST to attachment endpoint followed by 200/201 response containing unexpected file extensions in request body, especially when response headers omit Content-Disposition: attachment or lack proper MIME type.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted Upload – CVE-2026-48939 Scannable Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry mandates asset exposure hunt per template guidance. Vulnerable iCagenda instances must be inventoried and patched by 2026-07-13.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and version-detection tools for iCagenda versions prior to patch date. Cross-reference with accessible iCagenda installations on external-facing assets. Prioritize remediation per federal due date 2026-07-13.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—HTTP POST requests uploading .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5 files to iCagenda endpoints must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to iCagenda file-upload paths (e.g., /upload, /attachment, /media/upload) with dangerous file extensions in filename or Content-Type header. Flag success responses (HTTP 200/201/204). Correlate with file-creation events in iCagenda directories to confirm payload persistence.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution'—direct evidence that PHP interpreter invocation from iCagenda directories post-upload is the exploitation payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php, php-fpm, httpd process execution with working directories or file arguments pointing to iCagenda upload/temp directories. Correlate with recent POST uploads to file-attachment endpoints. High confidence if process invocation timestamp immediately follows successful file upload.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Creation and Persistence in iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary files' leading to 'PHP code execution'—indicates webshell or persistent backdoor installation. Look for newly created executable PHP files in iCagenda-owned paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of .php, .phtml, .phar files in iCagenda directories with suspicious content (base64_decode, eval, preg_replace /e, system, exec, passthru calls). Escalate if file ownership/permissions allow web-server execution and correlates with failed application functionality or HTTP 500 errors.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status mandates patch verification. Pipeline should flag vulnerability scanner results confirming iCagenda instances remain vulnerable to this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect any Nessus/Qualys/OpenVAS finding reporting CVE-2026-48939 or iCagenda file-upload vulnerability. Verify product version against patch status. If scanner shows vulnerable version, cross-reference scan date with web-access logs and file-creation events to identify possible exploitation window.

suggestion.title: External-Facing iCagenda Instance Inventory Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' and CISA KEV context (federal due date)—any internet-routable iCagenda instance is an active attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for iCagenda deployments; verify each is restricted to internal/trusted networks only. Monitor DNS and certificate transparency logs for iCagenda hostnames. Alert on any external HTTP access to iCagenda paths (/index.php, /upload, /attachment) from non-trusted networks.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Arbitrary File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' Zero UCs were generated for the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file upload POST endpoints for executable file types (php, phtml, php3, php4, php5, pht, phps, jsp, aspx, exe). Correlate with application/access logs for write operations to web-accessible directories. Flag MIME-type mismatches (e.g., php uploaded as image/jpeg) and uploads to attachment directories with double extensions (.php.jpg, .phtml.txt).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly traces attack to 'PHP code upload and execution.' Execution monitoring is a distinct phase absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process spawning or script execution from iCagenda attachment/upload directories. Monitor for unexpected child processes from web server user (www-data, apache, iis apppool) with arguments referencing recently written .php files. Flag HTTP 200 responses to newly uploaded objects in web-accessible paths with php extension.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scan Baseline
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status denotes active exploitation. Baseline vuln-scanner coverage is table-stakes; article emphasizes federal patch due-date 2026-07-13 requiring immediate inventory and remediation tracking.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature

suggestion.title: File Type Validation Bypass Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active wild exploitation; need exploit-specific signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints with patterns consistent with documented CVE-2026-48939 exploitation—specifically multipart uploads with file extension evasion, followed by rapid HTTP GET requests to retrieve and execute the uploaded file. Track frequency spikes against known-vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from PHP in Web Context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) spawned by PHP runtime (w3wp.exe, php-cgi.exe, apache2) in web root directory context, especially within 5 minutes of file write events to iCagenda upload directories. suggestion.title: iCagenda Plugin Reconnaissance / Version Fingerprinting

Alert on repeated requests to common plugin reconnaissance endpoints (/plugins/icagenda/version, /administrator/index.php?option=com_icagenda, or WordPress plugin API queries for iCagenda).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Mismatch

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via iCagenda Upload Directory
