suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a publicly-exploited web application vulnerability in the 'file attachment feature.' CISA KEV implies active exploitation. Pipeline generated zero asset discovery detections despite asset exposure being the canonical first hunt for web app exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all iCagenda instances (via vulnerability scanner, netflow, or HTTP logs). Correlate with firewall rules and WAF logs to flag any instances reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-check against patch inventory; federal due date is 2026-07-13.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files.' Pipeline missed this primary attack vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to iCagenda upload endpoints (e.g., /index.php?option=com_icagenda&view=event&layout=upload or attachment-handling URIs). Flag multipart form submissions containing executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5, .shtml) or polyglot file combinations.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability results in 'PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline reconstructed zero execution-phase kill-chain despite this being the direct stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php-cgi or php-fpm spawning child processes (sh, bash, cmd.exe) originating from web-accessible iCagenda directories immediately following file upload events. Flag high-entropy PHP execution with network egress or file system writes.

suggestion.title: Webshell Persistence via iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation persists uploaded PHP as webshell for post-compromise command execution. No persistence-phase detection generated despite this being the typical C2 foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of new PHP files in iCagenda upload/attachment directories with file timestamps correlating to suspicious HTTP POST events. Flag files containing base64_decode, eval, system, exec, passthru, or common webshell signatures (c99, r57, etc.).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Vulnerability Scan Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal remediation deadline (2026-07-13) and notes that 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline should have mandated confirmation hunt via vulnerability scanner. CVE-2026-48939 is in CISA KEV and therefore confirmed exploited in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results flagging CVE-2026-48939 with asset inventory. Escalate any findings on internet-facing iCagenda instances regardless of patch status. Correlate scanner signal with HTTP/netflow logs for IOCs of active exploitation (suspicious uploads, PHP execution, outbound connections).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Exposure Hunt — CVE-2026-48939
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-07-13 and active exploitation status; baseline requirement is identifying all iCagenda instances on the network regardless of perceived patch status. Article provides no prevalence data, mandating immediate asset hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify iCagenda deployments via HTTP header inspection (/index.php?view=events paths), process enumeration (php.exe serving iCagenda content), or vulnerability scanner integration. Prioritize internet-facing or DMZ-hosted instances. Cross-correlate with patch inventory to flag truly vulnerable assets for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Uploads to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability…upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — detection must monitor for polyglot uploads, extension bypass, MIME-type mismatch, and null-byte injection attempts against iCagenda endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints for non-image file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5, .pht), double extensions (.php.jpg), content-type mismatches (image/* header with PHP binary), or null-byte sequences. Flag any executable uploaded to web-accessible paths.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution' — detection must trigger on PHP interpreter spawning from upload storage locations where iCagenda attachment files are stored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php-cgi.exe executing scripts from typical iCagenda attachment directories (/uploads, /attachments, /files, or installation-specific paths). Correlate file creation timestamps with execution events. Flag child processes spawned from PHP execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl.exe).

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: PHP execution capability enables persistent web-shell deployment; detection should identify PHP files with suspicious names or persistence patterns in iCagenda attachment storage locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify PHP files with suspicious naming conventions (shell.php, config.php, admin.php variants, single-letter names) persisting in iCagenda upload directories with creation dates predating normal application updates. Correlate with outbound TCP/UDP connections to non-RFC1918 addresses from web-server processes.

suggestion.title: iCagenda PHP Execution with Command Output
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'PHP code upload and execution' implies attacker-controlled PHP snippets; detection should identify system command invocation (exec, passthru, system, shell_exec functions) executed within iCagenda context or upload directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP-spawned child processes (cmd.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash) with command-line arguments typically associated with reconnaissance or exploitation (whoami, ipconfig, curl, wget, nc). Correlate process parentage back to php.exe instances serving iCagenda paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Upload to Web Application
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints (typically /upload, /attachment, /files) for .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .php7 file extensions. Alert on successful uploads (HTTP 200-201) followed by file creation in web-accessible directories or PHP execution logs from those paths.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Upload to Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' No detection rule for file-type validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints where uploaded file MIME type or extension does not match an approved whitelist. Flag uploads with Content-Type headers indicating archives (application/zip, application/x-tar) or scripts (application/x-php, text/x-php).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline returned empty IOC object despite CVE-2026-48939 being the primary vulnerability identifier. Basic IOC extraction should capture and correlate this CVE across scanner and exploit attempt logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results identifying CVE-2026-48939 with HTTP request logs to iCagenda instances. Alert on exploitation attempts (POST to upload endpoints) within 24 hours of detection or after federal patch due-date (2026-07-13) has passed.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Attachment Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'PHP code upload and execution' — detection of actual execution in attachment paths is the final stage of the kill chain and essential for incident confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php.exe or php processes spawned with working directory in web attachment/upload paths (e.g., /uploads/, /attachments/, /files/). Alert on PHP error logs showing include/require/eval of files from attachment directories or unexpected PHP function calls (exec, system, shell_exec, passthru, proc_open) from uploaded files.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names iCagenda product with known exploited vulnerability — asset discovery is mandatory first-response action for any KEV. Pipeline provided zero asset-hunting logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for iCagenda instances; flag any exposed to internet-facing ports. Cross-reference against patch-status telemetry to identify unpatched vs. patched deployments. Correlate with federal due date (2026-07-13) to enforce compliance.

suggestion.title: File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — direct statement of attack vector. Pipeline missed the primary exploitation mechanism entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to iCagenda file-upload endpoints; flag uploads of executable types (.php, .phtml, .php5, .phar, .phps, .shtml) or polyglot/double-extension uploads. Correlate with HTTP 200–201 success responses from attachment directories.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution' — the execution phase is the actual compromise. Pipeline failed to generate post-upload execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter invocation (php.exe, php-cgi.exe) from iCagenda upload directories immediately after file-upload activity. Look for web server processes spawning child code-execution processes or unusual eval/include patterns in uploaded PHP.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation culminates in PHP code persisting as 'upload and execution' — threat actors maintain backdoor access. Pipeline produced no web-shell hunting logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload directories for suspicious HTTP access: repeated requests to recently-created .php files, query strings with command execution patterns, high entropy parameter values, or response sizes inconsistent with legitimate file-serving behavior.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-13' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' — patch-status validation is mandatory for KEV. Pipeline generated zero compliance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit endpoint and application patch-status to identify iCagenda instances running vulnerable versions (pre-patch-release date). Flag unpatched instances as critical; validate remediation completion by due date via re-scan.

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—direct indicator of file upload attack vector that pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file upload endpoints (typically /upload, /attachment, /media) on iCagenda instances for POST requests followed by HTTP 200/201. Correlate with suspicious file extensions (php, php3, php4, phtml, phar, exe, sh) written to web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload (Web Shell)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution'—this is the exploitation phase the pipeline completely omitted.
log_sources: web server logs with process spawning
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process spawning (php.exe, php-cgi) immediately following file uploads. Look for php execution from unexpected parent processes (apache, nginx). Cross-reference uploaded filenames with subsequently executed PHP processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Write to Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article describes upload of 'arbitrary files' leading to 'PHP code execution'—absence of detection for PHP writes to web-accessible paths is critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation events where: file extension is .php/.phtml/.php3 AND parent path contains web root (www, htdocs, public_html, var/www). Baseline legitimate PHP writes; flag anomalies from iCagenda upload directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes 'CVE: CVE-2026-48939 — match against your vulnerability scanner' but pipeline returned no IOCs to correlate against scanning tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for iCagenda product instances. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-48939 flags. Prioritize internet-facing instances (implied by T1190 language). Correlate findings with federal patch-due date 2026-07-13.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Command Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase: once PHP is uploaded, threat actor executes commands through it. Article's 'PHP code execution' implies subsequent command activity not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs for HTTP requests to recently-uploaded PHP files containing common web-shell parameter names (cmd, command, exec, shell, c). Look for base64-encoded payloads in query strings. Baseline expected HTTP methods (should only see GET/POST for shells).

suggestion.title: Attribute-Based File Upload Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'unrestricted upload' suggests common bypasses (double extension, MIME type spoofing, null byte injection) were not detected by pipeline.
log_sources: IIS/Apache access logs with Content-Type headers
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect multipart/form-data uploads for: mismatched Content-Type headers (e.g., application/octet-stream for .php), double extensions (shell.php.jpg), special characters (shell.php%00.jpg), or null-byte sequences. Flag any that bypass expected MIME filtering.

suggestion.title: npm Install with Compromised jscrambler 8.14.0
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Compromised jscrambler 8.14.0 npm Release'—direct package version compromise. Pipeline should detect installation of this specific malicious version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify installations of jscrambler package version 8.14.0 or attempts to install it from npm registry. Cross-correlate with subsequent Rust binary execution in node_modules/.bin or anomalous child processes spawned by npm/node postinstall hooks.

suggestion.title: Rust Infostealer Execution from node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Rust Infostealer' payload 'drops' during install—infostealer will execute post-installation. Pipeline missed detection for Rust binary spawning from compromised node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Rust binaries (executable signatures, .exe from unusual paths) executing from node_modules directories. Correlate with npm/nodejs parent processes and look for uncommon CLI flags or environment variable modifications indicative of malware initialization.

suggestion.title: Infostealer Credential Access Post-npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Rust infostealer behavior inherently involves harvesting credentials ('infostealer' designation confirms data collection intent). Article doesn't detail targets but standard infostealer behavior includes browser credential stores and SSH key access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-jscrambler install, detect processes accessing browser credential stores (e.g., Chrome/Edge credential directories, Firefox profile), enumerating SSH key files (~/.ssh/), or reading credential manager APIs. Flag rapid successive file access to known secret locations.

suggestion.title: C2 Exfiltration from Infostealer Payload
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package 'drops' infostealer—payload must establish outbound communication for data theft. Article does not specify C2 IOCs but exfiltration is inherent to infostealer kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections from npm/node process contexts to non-standard external IPs (geoIP anomalies, newly registered domains, or known infostealer C2 infrastructure). Correlate timing with jscrambler install completion.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Hook Abuse for Infostealer Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article states infostealer 'drops during install'—likeliest mechanism is postinstall script in package.json. Pipeline did not identify postinstall script execution as vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node processes executing shell commands (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) from node_modules/.bin or via postinstall triggers. Detect execution of obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads in postinstall scripts. Cross-check jscrambler 8.14.0 package.json for unusual script entries.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Registry Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised release on npm registry indicates either account takeover or registry-level injection. Pipeline should flag supply chain integrity violation at ingestion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare jscrambler 8.14.0 manifest hash against known-good baseline. Alert on unexpected file additions (Rust binary, obfuscated scripts) in package tarball. Cross-reference package signature or publishing timestamp anomalies.

suggestion.title: npm package preinstall script downloads unexpected binary
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious preinstall binary was published via jscrambler package. No detection for preinstall lifecycle hooks downloading or executing binaries was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm preinstall scripts spawning curl/wget/PowerShell to fetch binaries from external sources. Monitor for child processes of npm/node executing from node_modules directories during package installation, particularly scripts that write to .bin or cache locations.

suggestion.title: Supply-chain compromise via malicious npm package version
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: npm package repository hosting malicious code. Article describes package publishing mechanism but no IOCs or package version blocking rules were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm package installations against threat feed of known-malicious package names and versions. Alert on install of jscrambler or similar supply-chain compromise artifacts; baseline package.json against approved registries.

suggestion.title: Unexpected binary installation into node_modules/.bin directory
suggestion.rationale: Malicious preinstall binary would install to node_modules. No file-system detection use case for suspicious binary writes during npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node_modules/.bin/ for unexpected executable file creation during npm install. Flag binaries with no corresponding npm package declaration or cryptographic hash mismatches against published registry metadata.

suggestion.title: npm install process spawns out-of-process binary execution
suggestion.rationale: Preinstall hooks execute malicious binaries. Pipeline missed detection for unexpected child processes spawned during npm lifecycle phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node spawning child processes to non-standard locations (outside node_modules, /tmp, system paths) during preinstall/install/postinstall lifecycle hooks. Alert on executions of binaries with low prevalence or unsigned code.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Content Triggering Zimbra Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'crafted emails' as the delivery mechanism; pipeline missed initial-access detection. Need to identify email-borne payloads before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zimbra SMTP/IMAP logs for emails with unusual MIME structures, encoded payloads, or script-like content (JavaScript, XML, custom protocols) in body or attachments. Flag emails that bypass standard filtering but match known Zimbra exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution Within Zimbra User Session Context
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: code runs 'in user sessions.' Pipeline missed execution-phase detection entirely. This is the exploit moment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned from Zimbra web client sessions (java.exe, scripts), unusual network calls from Zimbra worker threads, or DOM manipulation events in logged user sessions that don't match baseline behavior.

suggestion.title: Zimbra Session Hijacking / Unauthorized Session Activity Post-Email
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker gains session control after email delivery. Missing detection for lateral movement or credential theft within compromised sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid session state changes post-email receipt (e.g., new device fingerprints, geographic anomalies, privilege escalations, mail forwarding rules created, or session tokens reused from anomalous IPs within minutes of high-risk email arrival).

suggestion.title: Zimbra Flaw Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'flaw'; pipeline should model CVE/vulnerability scanning. No attempt to identify version-specific payloads or known exploit signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to Zimbra endpoints containing known vulnerability markers (specific parameter combinations, malformed headers, or payloads matching published Zimbra CVE PoCs). Correlate with email receipt timing.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Delivery to Zimbra Installation
suggestion.rationale: 'Crafted emails' suggests targeted campaign. Pipeline missed reconnaissance for multi-recipient phishing campaigns targeting Zimbra users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden spike in emails to Zimbra domains/users from external sources with similar characteristics (same sender domain, payload structure, or reply-to patterns), especially if emails bypass authentication checks or have suspicious encoding.

suggestion.title: Ransomware file encryption activity — high entropy write operations
suggestion.rationale: Core impact of ransomware; article discusses 'encrypted for impact' phase as payload delivery. Missing detection for rapid file modification patterns and extension changes that precede ransom notes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes performing rapid sequential writes to files with high entropy or unusual batch operations (>500 files in short window). Detect common ransom-note filenames and extension changes (*.gentlemen, *.howling, etc.). Correlate with unusual process parents launching from Windows System or Temp directories.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement and privilege escalation pre-encryption
suggestion.rationale: RaaS affiliate model described in keywords ('affiliate model driving rapid growth') implies multi-stage: initial access → reconnaissance → lateral movement → second-stage deployment. No UCs for credential theft or internal propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track lateral movement signatures: SYSTEM/NETWORK logons followed by interactive logons from unusual source IPs, credential reuse across multiple hosts, and pass-the-hash patterns. Detect PSEXEC/WMI execution chains and scheduled task creation by non-admin users. Flag service account abuse.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration to ransom infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'hospitality and retail' targeting and RaaS operations; implies pre-encryption data theft for double-extortion. No detection for bulk data transfers or API calls to staging/exfil infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data transfers from database/file servers to unknown external IPs or cloud services (S3, Backblaze, etc.). Detect DNS queries for newly registered domains with patterns matching known ransom leak sites. Flag sftp/ftp/http bulk downloads.

suggestion.title: Extortion communication and ransom demand delivery
suggestion.rationale: Gentlemen operates under RaaS affiliate model; ransom notes and contact mechanisms are operational artifacts. Missing detections for HTML/text ransom notes, onion site access, or attacker communication infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of ransom note files (README.txt, GENTLEMEN.txt, etc.) alongside encrypted files. Monitor for TOR client launches or .onion domain connections. Flag credential access to victim email/contact systems used to send extortion demands.

suggestion.title: RaaS affiliate access patterns — staged tooling deployment
suggestion.rationale: Keywords highlight 'affiliate model driving rapid growth.' Pipeline missed detection for initial lightweight access tool deployment, time-delay between compromise and ransomware execution, and multi-stage payload staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN/RDP logon events with delayed (>48 hour) execution of known staging tools (Cobalt Strike, Sliver, MSBuild). Detect attacker reconnaissance patterns (net user, whoami, systeminfo) followed by lateral movement. Look for execution of living-off-the-land binaries (psexec.exe, schtasks.exe) from non-standard locations.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Suspicious File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — this is the exploitation vector. Should detect POST requests to iCagenda upload handlers with non-whitelisted file extensions, especially PHP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda upload/attachment endpoints for file extensions matching executable types (php, jsp, aspx, phtml, phar). Alert on Content-Type mismatches (e.g., image/jpeg with .php extension) or polyglot files. Baseline upload frequency and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes outcome as 'PHP code upload and execution'. Should detect web server process spawning PHP interpreter to execute files in upload paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP process creation (php.exe, php-cgi, /usr/bin/php) by web server user (www-data, IUSR, apache) with working directory or argument pointing to iCagenda upload/attachment paths. Correlate timing with suspicious upload HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 Asset Inventory and Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation indicates active in-the-wild exploitation. Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' — should identify and baseline all iCagenda instances reachable from internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify iCagenda web applications via known administrative URLs (/administrator/index.php?option=com_icagenda, /components/com_icagenda/). Track version info from HTTP headers or page footers. Alert if instances lack patch dated 2026-07-13 or later. Monitor for scanning attempts against known-vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Upload Handler Error Rate Spike
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of unrestricted upload feature will generate application logs and HTTP errors. CISA KEV status means active attacks should correlate with error patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda application logs and web server error logs for upload-related exceptions. Alert on sustained 4xx/5xx error rates >150% of baseline from single source IP, or sudden appearance of 'file not allowed' / 'upload failed' messages correlating with POST traffic to upload endpoints.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Arbitrary File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — no UC exists to detect file uploads to iCagenda endpoints or POST activity to /upload endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda application endpoints (e.g., /upload, /attachment, /media) with HTTP 200/201 responses. Baseline expected file types; alert on executable, script, or archive uploads. Correlate with web shell execution attempts post-upload.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution' — pipeline missed execution-phase detection for PHP files uploaded and subsequently invoked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP file uploads (Content-Type: application/x-php, .php extensions) followed within seconds by HTTP requests to the uploaded file path with process execution logs showing php.exe or php-cgi spawning. Alert on file uploads to web-accessible directories combined with subsequent execution.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Upload Blocking
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability title explicitly names 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' — detection should flag attempts to bypass upload-type restrictions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor failed upload attempts (HTTP 403/413/415 responses) to iCagenda endpoints for patterns suggesting file-type evasion (double extensions like .php.jpg, null bytes, case variation). Escalate to alert if patterns repeat or bypass WAF upload filters.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Web Shell Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes execution risk from uploaded code; detect anomalous process spawning or outbound connections from iCagenda application pool or web process after upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-upload, monitor iCagenda web process (php.exe, httpd, nginx worker) for unusual child process spawns (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget) or outbound connections to non-standard ports. Baseline normal application behavior; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Asset Inventory and Exposure Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due-date 2026-07-13 — requires asset discovery and exposure validation independent of vulnerability scanner results, as patch lag is common.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner, CMDB, and network telemetry for iCagenda instances (product name, version tags, service ports). Cross-reference against deployed assets; flag any instances reachable from untrusted networks or internet-facing. Verify patch status independently of scanner claims.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Dangerous File Upload Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' Pipeline generated zero file-upload UCs. Should detect PHP, PHTML, JSP, ASPX uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment endpoints (typically `/components/com_icagenda/uploadfile/` or similar) for POST/PUT requests with filenames containing executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5, .pht). Correlate with 200/201 HTTP responses. High fidelity if extension is MIME-mismatched or uploaded to unexpected directory.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' No UC addresses post-upload execution detection. Adversary uploads .php shell then accesses it, creating server-side execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter execution (php.exe, php-cgi, php-fpm) spawned from or reading files in iCagenda's upload/attachment directory. Correlate with recent successful file uploads. Look for unexpected php.exe parent process (should be httpd/apache, not cmd.exe or powershell).

suggestion.title: iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE: `CVE-2026-48939`' and establishes this is a known-exploited CISA KEV. Standard asset-exposure hunt template referenced but pipeline generated no scanning UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner matches for CVE-2026-48939 or iCagenda version identification. Inventory all internet-facing iCagenda instances (HTTP fingerprinting by response headers or component paths). Cross-reference against patch status; unpatched instances on public IPs with this CVE warrant immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed iCagenda Application Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly refers to 'public-facing application.' Prerequisite for exploitation. Pipeline generated no asset-discovery UC despite standard template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all iCagenda instances reachable from internet. Fingerprint via HTTP headers (X-Powered-By: Joomla or iCagenda component paths like `/components/com_icagenda/`). Query passive DNS/certificate logs for subdomains hosting iCagenda. Alert if unpatched versions detected on public-facing assets.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Detection in iCagenda Upload Path
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes upload mechanism enables 'PHP code upload and execution.' Post-breach, adversary maintains access via web shell. No UC addresses file content or behavioral signatures of uploaded shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan iCagenda upload/attachment directories for recently created PHP files with suspicious content patterns (e.g., `eval()`, `base64_decode()`, `system()`, `exec()`, `passthru()` function calls). Correlate with HTTP requests to those files showing unusual query strings or POST bodies. High-risk if uploaded after CVE publication date and before patch applied.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload Endpoint Access Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'file attachment feature' as attack vector. Exploitation attempt will involve repeated/clustered requests to upload endpoint. No UC for endpoint access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual volume or rate of requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints (e.g., `/components/com_icagenda/uploadfile/` or `/upload/`). Alert on >N requests in 5min window from single source IP, or requests with 400/403 errors followed by 200 success (indicative of bypass attempts). Baseline per-asset and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: iCagenda PHP File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline missed the core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints containing .php extensions or MIME-type bypass patterns. Correlate with subsequent PHP process spawning from web root within 60 seconds of upload.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Post-Upload PHP Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'PHP code upload and execution' as the exploitation outcome. Pipeline failed to translate this to process-creation or file-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php.exe or php-cgi spawning with parent process w3wp.exe (IIS) or apache2 (Apache) with working directory under iCagenda upload paths. Flag unusual command-line arguments suggesting shell invocation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Web Shell Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states PHP code execution post-upload, establishing web shell risk. Pipeline did not suggest content-based or behavioral detection for web shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan iCagenda upload directories for new .php files with markers like eval(), base64_decode(), passthru(), system(), exec(). Correlate file creation timestamps with POST access logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Positive Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV entry implying active exploitation. Pipeline should have included vulnerability scanner hits as primary detection vector alongside exploit detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-48939 on iCagenda instances. Escalate to immediate remediation workflow given CISA KEV status and active exploitation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Type Validation Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'unrestricted upload' implying validation bypass. Pipeline missed detection of requests that circumvent extension/MIME-type filtering (double extensions, null-byte tricks, case variants).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file upload POST requests to iCagenda with obfuscated extensions (.php.jpg, .php%00, .phtml, .pht) or mismatched Content-Type headers. Flag requests combining executable extensions with benign MIME types.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE: CVE-2026-48939 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and notes patch lag as 'the silent killer.' First-line hunt for unpatched iCagenda instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner reports that flag CVE-2026-48939 in iCagenda product inventory. Correlate with asset inventory to identify public-facing instances. CISA KEV entries are actively exploited; any positive scanner result warrants immediate verification and patching by federal due date 2026-07-13.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' in 'file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Direct evidence of file-type bypass attempt and web shell staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda file-upload endpoints for .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5 extensions or double-extension bypasses (.php.jpg, .jpg.php). Flag requests where Content-Type header mismatches file extension (e.g., image/jpeg with .php). Correlation with 403/400 responses may indicate WAF blocks; successful 200/201 indicates upload succeeded.

suggestion.title: PHP Web Shell Execution Post-iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Post-upload detection must surface when attacker-controlled PHP is invoked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to recently-uploaded file paths (file names matching typical upload directories + timestamp patterns) with execution-like behavior: GET/POST with query string parameters, unusual User-Agents, or requests originating from external subnets. Correlate with server-side execution indicators (PHP errors, process spawn, outbound connections).

suggestion.title: File Type Validation Bypass Attempts on iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism is 'unrestricted upload' implying insufficient MIME-type, extension, or magic-byte validation. Detection should surface bypass techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag uploads with Content-Type: application/octet-stream, missing/spoofed Content-Type, null-byte injection in filename, case-variation extensions (.pHp, .PhP), or double extensions. iCagenda instances should whitelist only safe types (image/*, document types); all others warrant investigation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Upload Directory Index Listing and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Prior to uploading web shell, attackers typically enumerate upload directory structure. Article implies default-world-readable upload paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for directory enumeration attempts (OPTIONS, HEAD requests, 403 responses to index.php, or traversal payloads like /../../../) against known iCagenda upload directories (commonly /uploads/, /attachments/, /media/). Successful 200 responses with directory listing are high-confidence indicators of pre-exploitation reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Reverse-Shell or Command-Execution Indicators Post-PHP Upload
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation does not stop at PHP execution; article implies 'code upload and execution' but attackers will likely escalate to reverse shell or command execution for persistence and control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After PHP upload detection, hunt for outbound connections from web server process (apache, nginx, php-fpm) to external IP:port combinations, especially on ephemeral ports or known C2 infrastructure. Also monitor for shell-spawning indicators: proc names like bash/cmd.exe spawned by PHP process, or suspicious PHP function calls (system(), exec(), passthru(), eval()) in logs.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'upload of arbitrary files...ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution' — core attack step completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT to iCagenda file attachment endpoints for multipart uploads containing executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .pht, .exe, .asp, .aspx). Baseline normal file type distribution; flag anomalies. Correlate successful upload (HTTP 200/201) with file creation events in web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: PHP Process Spawn from iCagenda Directory Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'PHP code upload and execution' as the exploitation outcome; pipeline captured no detection for the execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP interpreter (php.exe, php, php-cgi) spawning with working directory or parent location in iCagenda installation path. Look for timing correlation between file upload and process creation. Flag unusual PHP child processes (curl, wget, powershell, cmd) indicating C2 or data staging.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Exposed Asset Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires vulnerability scanner match against CVE-2026-48939; pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this being mandatory for asset-exposure posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all vulnerability scanner findings matching CVE-2026-48939 with network asset inventory. Identify public-facing iCagenda instances by port/service fingerprinting. Correlate unpatched instances against Federal remediation due date (2026-07-13) to enforce compliance timeline.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Command Execution from Uploaded PHP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful code execution implying attacker-controlled PHP code; pipeline missed post-exploitation detection for shell command execution or reverse shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to user-uploaded files with query string payloads (cmd, exec, system, passthru patterns). Monitor for base64/hex obfuscation in POST body suggesting encoded commands. Detect outbound connections (curl, wget, nc) spawned from web server processes or PHP child processes running as web user.

suggestion.title: iCagenda HTTP Upload Endpoint Baseline Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'file attachment feature' as attack surface; pipeline generated no network-level detection for the upload mechanism itself during active exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal upload request size, frequency, and source IP diversity for iCagenda installations. Flag uploads exceeding baseline file size, rapid-fire multi-upload sequences, or geographic/ASN anomalies. Correlate upload patterns with known attacker scanning signatures or CVE PoC activity.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' via 'file attachment feature' — requires detection of POST/PUT requests to upload endpoints on exposed iCagenda instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests to iCagenda upload endpoints (typically `/upload*`, `/attachment*`, `/media*`) on identified iCagenda instances. Baseline normal attachment types (PDF, image MIME) and alert on .php, .phtml, .phar, .exe, .sh, .jsp uploads.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution' — must detect process spawning from typical web-app upload directories post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or apache/nginx child processes spawn with command-line arguments referencing paths in `/uploads/`, `/attachments/`, `/tmp/`, or other typical upload staging directories. Correlate with recent file-upload activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Type Upload to iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'unrestricted upload' allowing 'arbitrary files' and 'PHP code upload' — WAF/HTTP inspection must detect executable extensions in Content-Disposition or multipart payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse multipart form uploads to iCagenda endpoints; flag uploads with Content-Disposition containing .php, .phtml, .phar, .asp, .aspx, .jsp, .jspx, .exe, .sh, .bat, .cmd, .com, .scr, .vbs, .ps1, .psm1 extensions regardless of declared MIME type.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry requires immediate asset inventory for all iCagenda instances. Exploit scanners will probe for the vulnerable upload endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on web-access logs or scanner output showing probes to iCagenda file-attachment endpoints from non-approved scanners or external IPs. Flag 200/201 responses to upload POST from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: iCagenda Public Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV states exploitation observed in the wild against 'exposed assets' — SOC must enumerate all iCagenda instances with public-facing upload functionality for rapid patching by federal due-date 2026-07-13.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall/proxy/WAF logs for destination ports 80/443 to known iCagenda paths (`/index.php?`, `/component/icagenda/`, `/administrator/`). Cross-reference against asset database to identify unpatched or unknown instances; prioritize for patch verification against 2026-07-13 deadline.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Post-iCagenda Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation via 'PHP code upload and execution' implies attacker can drop persistent backdoors; detection must trigger on suspicious PHP files in upload directories with execution artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when new .php, .phtml, .phar files appear in iCagenda upload directories with suspicious indicators: PHP eval(), base64_decode(), $_GET/$_POST variables, preg_replace with /e modifier, or file-write attempts to web-accessible paths. Correlate with recent upload activity.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Suspicious File Upload to Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—this is the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints for uploads with executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3-5, .phar), double-extension obfuscation (.php.txt, .php.jpg), or null-byte tricks. Alert on any successful 200/201 response followed by HTTP GET to the uploaded file path within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—detection must cover the execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP interpreter invocation (php.exe, php-cgi, Apache PHP module) triggered by HTTP requests to iCagenda upload/attachment paths. Correlate successful .php file uploads with subsequent process creation from web server context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and flags federal patch due date of 2026-07-13. Vulnerability findings are first-stage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all vulnerability scanner positives for CVE-2026-48939 on iCagenda instances. Escalate any unpatched instances found within 7 days of federal due date. Correlate scanner findings with network exposure (internet-facing, accessible from DMZ).

suggestion.title: Malicious File Type Upload to iCagenda Attachment Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit via 'upload of arbitrary files'—without strict MIME validation, executables bypass file-type filters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Content-Type headers on iCagenda attachment uploads for mismatches (e.g., application/x-php sent as image/jpeg). Alert on polyglot file uploads or content that starts with PHP magic bytes but claims image MIME. Block or quarantine for manual review.

suggestion.title: File Upload to Web-Accessible Directory Followed by Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—the canonical attacker chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST to iCagenda file attachment endpoint with HTTP GET to newly-created .php files in web-root within seconds. Pivot on Content-Type mismatch (e.g., image/jpeg with .php extension) and file creation timestamp alignment. Alert if POST succeeds followed by 200-response GET on suspicious path.

suggestion.title: Unexpected PHP File Creation in Web-Root
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PHP code upload and execution'—successful exploitation leaves persistent uploaded PHP in web-accessible directory. File integrity monitoring is primary detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file creation in /var/www, /httpdocs, or iCagenda web root outside scheduled deployments. Exclude legitimate web framework files. Prioritize files created immediately after HTTP upload activity; check file ownership (should match web server user, not attacker context).

suggestion.title: File Extension Bypass Attempts in iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' indicates missing extension/type validation; attackers probe with .phtml, .php5, .php7, null bytes, double dots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload endpoint for filenames with .phtml, .php[5-9], .shtml, double extensions (.php.jpg), or null-byte encoding. High velocity of rejected/accepted uploads with anomalous extension is indicator of active exploitation attempts. Log file hashes for correlation with known webshell signatures.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner'. CISA KEV catalog entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-07-13 (24 hours from article publication).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all assets for iCagenda instances (HTTP ports, 'iCagenda' in banner/cert CN); cross-reference against CVE-2026-48939. Flag any hit with CVSS ≥8.0 and patched_status=false or unknown. Correlate with network exposure (public IP/resolvable DNS) and recent inbound HTTP connection volume.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Process Chain: Unexpected Shell or Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'; successful exploitation results in arbitrary command execution in web-server process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php-cgi, php-fpm, or apache/nginx worker processes spawning /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell, wget, curl, or nc. Alert on unexpected outbound connections from PHP process to non-whitelisted destinations. Parent process must be web server; children spawned from uploaded PHP are suspicious.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Suspicious File Upload to Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—attackers bypass validation to deposit payloads. No hunt for upload attempts to this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT to iCagenda attachment upload endpoints (typically /attachments, /media, /files) for: (1) content-type mismatches (e.g., application/x-php declared as image/*), (2) file extensions in MIME payloads not matching headers, (3) requests from external IPs during off-hours or from unusual geographies. Correlate with 5xx responses indicating processing failures, then 2xx on retry—sign of validation loop exploitation.

suggestion.title: PHP Execution in iCagenda Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' No detection use case for post-upload code execution. This is the exploitation payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of PHP processes (php.exe, php-cgi) spawned by web server identity (e.g., IIS AppPool, www-data) in iCagenda directory tree post-upload. Look for parent process = w3wp.exe or apache with command line containing iCagenda paths. Secondary: correlate with file-write events to .php files in web-accessible directories within 60 seconds before execution.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article implies arbitrary PHP upload enables persistence. Pipeline missed T1505.003 (web shell) as the direct post-exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uploaded .php files that remain accessible and executable in iCagenda's web-accessible directories. Look for: (1) file creation anomalies (e.g., .php in /media or /attachments), (2) subsequent HTTP GET/POST to those URLs with 200 responses, (3) process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) as children of w3wp.exe immediately after HTTP request to uploaded file path. High fidelity if parent process CL includes the uploaded file name.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV with federal patch due-date; standard template mandates asset inventory hunt. Pipeline referenced template but generated no actual detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all iCagenda instances on-network: (1) query DNS/DHCP for 'icagenda' or 'calendar' hostnames, (2) search vulnerability scanner for iCagenda product detections, (3) correlate with web server logs containing 'icagenda' in URI path. Cross-reference patched vs. unpatched versions. Priority: any instance < 30 days from federal due-date (2026-07-13) without patch or workaround applied.

suggestion.title: Anomalous iCagenda File Attachment Endpoint Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'file attachment feature'—attackers must interact with upload endpoint repeatedly to succeed. No hunt for reconnaissance or fuzzing of attachment parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal iCagenda file-upload traffic volume and content-type diversity. Flag: (1) spike in attachment uploads from single source IP, (2) sequential uploads with identical or near-identical file size, (3) upload attempts with double-extensions (.php.jpg, .phtml.txt), (4) requests to upload endpoints with oversized payloads (> 50MB for a calendar app), (5) rapid-fire uploads followed by immediate HTTP requests to /attachments or similar paths.

suggestion.title: iCagenda POST-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: After PHP shell upload succeeds, attacker issues commands. Article implies code execution but no hunt for post-exploitation C2 or command activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST to uploaded .php files (esp. those with suspicious names like shell.php, admin.php, c99.php) with payloads containing: system(), exec(), passthru(), shell_exec() calls in query string or POST body. Secondary: detect outbound DNS queries or HTTP requests originating from w3wp.exe or iCagenda process tree. Correlate POST uploads + file existence + subsequent POST with command payloads within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes iCagenda as public-facing application vulnerable to exploitation (T1190). 'Allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' implies exposed web interface requiring inventory and vulnerability scan correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for iCagenda instances on internet-facing web servers via proxy logs and network telemetry. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48939 matches. Prioritize systems running versions released before 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type...arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' Must detect dangerous file types (.php, .phtml, .php3-5, .phar, .exe) uploaded to iCagenda endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda upload endpoints. Alert on multipart form data containing dangerous executable extensions or double-extension payloads. Correlate with HTTP 200-201 success responses.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability results in 'PHP code upload and execution.' Detection must capture execution phase—newly uploaded PHP files executed via web server process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP interpreter spawning child processes from iCagenda upload/temp directories. Watch web server logs for rapid POST-then-GET patterns to newly uploaded file paths. Flag suspicious outbound connections from PHP process context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Exploitation Attempt Patterns
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation. 'Unrestricted upload' likely exploited via specific endpoint patterns. Detect malformed or enumeration attempts against upload functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests with upload exploitation signatures: multipart payloads missing CSRF tokens/authentication, oversized file payloads, path traversal characters (../), and failed upload retries. Correlate with iCagenda error logs showing file-type validation bypass.

suggestion.title: Beaconing from iCagenda Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, uploaded PHP shells beacon to C2. 'PHP code upload and execution' implies web shell deployment. Detect command-and-control callbacks from iCagenda process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from web server processes (apache, nginx, httpd) to non-standard ports (8080, 4444, etc.). Alert on DNS queries for suspicious domains from web server context. Flag periodic connection patterns consistent with reverse shells.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: After uploading web shell via 'PHP code upload and execution', attackers enumerate system. Implicit in arbitrary file/code execution capabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reconnaissance commands (whoami, id, pwd, uname, ls) spawned from web server process context. Detect file-system traversal and enumeration from iCagenda directory. Flag administrative tool execution (nc, curl, wget) when spawned by PHP/web-server user.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: Article states this is CISA KEV (actively exploited). Pipeline must emit a baselining UC matching any scanner vendor's CVE detection for iCagenda instances. Article: 'CVE-2026-48939 — match against your vulnerability scanner'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any scanner event reporting CVE-2026-48939 against iCagenda. Correlate findings with asset inventory to surface exposed instances. Priority: critical if asset is externally routable.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Attachment Upload Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'. Pipeline must hunt for PHP, .exe, .jsp, or other dangerous file types reaching iCagenda upload endpoints, which would indicate exploit attempt or successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda HTTP POST/PUT requests to file-upload endpoints for Content-Type or filename patterns indicative of code files (PHP, .phtml, .phar, .exe, .jsp). Flag any successful 200/201 responses and correlate with downstream file-system or process events.

suggestion.title: PHP Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'. Post-upload execution is the exploitation payload. Detection must look for PHP processes spawning from known upload temp/attachment paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when php.exe or php-cgi spawns with working directory or image path within iCagenda's upload or temp directories (e.g., /uploads, /attachments, /tmp/iCagenda*). Correlate with preceding HTTP POST events to file-upload endpoints.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Web Shell Post-Exploitation Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Once PHP code is uploaded and executed, attacker will interact with it via subsequent HTTP requests. Article describes 'PHP code upload and execution'; subsequent reconnaissance and command-execution requests are telltale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to uploaded PHP files within iCagenda with suspicious query strings (shell parameters, eval, exec, system) or unusual User-Agents. Correlate timing with file-upload events and outbound process activity.

suggestion.title: iCagenda External Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation in the wild. Article: 'exploit public-facing application'. Asset-exposure hunting (referenced in article: 'asset-exposure hunt') must list all externally-routable iCagenda instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all iCagenda instances in asset inventory and cross-check for external IP assignment, DNS CNAME/A record public resolution, and WAF/CDN exposure. Flag any unpatched instance (version < fix version) as critical with due-date urgency (2026-07-13 stated in article).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Process or Service Anomaly Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful PHP execution may spawn reverse shells, downloaders, or process manipulation. Article: 'PHP code upload and execution' implies runtime behavior beyond upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP or web-server child processes spawning unusual commands (curl, wget, powershell, cmd.exe). Correlate with outbound network connection events from the iCagenda process or its children.

suggestion.title: Detect Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment endpoints for uploads of dangerous executable file types (PHP, JSP, ASP, ASPX, EXE, SH). Alert on POST requests to upload handlers that accept code-executable extensions or suspicious MIME type mismatches (e.g., application/x-php-source labeled as image/jpeg).

suggestion.title: Detect PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability results in 'PHP code upload and execution'—the execution phase is explicitly part of the attack but no detection logic for post-upload execution is included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP GET/POST requests to .php files within iCagenda upload directories occurring within minutes of file upload events. Cross-reference with web application logs showing PHP execution context (uid=www-data or similar) and unexpected function calls (system, exec, passthru, shell_exec).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV inclusion mandates federal remediation by 2026-07-13. Article provides no guidance for scanner-based asset verification despite patch lag being the most common failure mode.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable) for CVE-2026-48939 matches against iCagenda instances. Prioritize internet-facing assets. Cross-reference against patch inventory and flag instances with unpatched versions after the 2026-07-13 deadline; treat scanner false-negatives as risk (version fingerprinting is often imprecise for PHP apps).

suggestion.title: Suspicious iCagenda File Attachment Submission Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'file attachment feature' as the attack surface. Need behavioral detection beyond one-off uploads—attackers iterate on payloads (bypasses, obfuscation, double-extensions).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed and succeeded HTTP POST requests to iCagenda attachment upload endpoints. Flag accounts or source IPs submitting multiple uploads in short timeframes with varying file extensions (shell.php, shell.phtml, shell.phar, shell.jpg.php). Detect file creation in upload directories immediately after POST submissions with command execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Webshell Persistence Detection in iCagenda Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation permits 'PHP code upload and execution'—implying attacker can establish persistence. Post-compromise webshell detection essential for breach response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload directories (/uploads/, /attachments/, /media/) for PHP files not present in baseline or version control. Flag files with generic names (shell.php, admin.php, upload.php, test.php), recently modified timestamps, or high entropy content. Correlate with access logs showing repeated HTTP requests to these files with suspicious parameters (cmd=, exec=, system=).

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed iCagenda Instance Inventory and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: T1190 requires public-facing surface. Article provides a hard deadline (2026-07-13) but no asset-centric detection for exposure and patch lag—standard first step in CVE remediation workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate iCagenda instances accessible from the internet using Shodan, Censys, or internal network discovery. Correlate with asset inventory to identify ownership and patch status. Flag instances running iCagenda versions ≤ the vulnerable version and still unpatched after 2026-07-13; escalate for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Arbitrary File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—no UC generated despite this being the core attack vector. Must detect POST requests to iCagenda upload endpoints with executable payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST requests to iCagenda upload or file attachment handlers. Correlate file upload events with suspicious file extensions (.php, .phtml, .phar, .php5) or MIME type mismatches. Establish baseline upload volume and file type patterns for iCagenda endpoints.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution'—no execution-phase UC generated. Post-upload activity is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP process spawning (php.exe, php-cgi.exe) as child of web server processes (w3wp.exe, apache, nginx).
