suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to known-sanctioned VPN provider domains or ASNs with ransomware-typical patterns (sustained connection during high disk I/O, correlation with file-read loops). Flag VPN tunnel establishment followed by bulk network discovery.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Encryption Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Malware Cryptor Seller'—a supplier of encryption utilities for ransomware deployment. Pipeline produced no cryptography-tool or ransomware-execution detections despite 'crit' severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known cryptor binaries (e.g., rclone, legitdisk) or unsigned process spawn of file encryption utilities. Correlate with high-volume sequential file opens, .exe/.dll file enumeration, and child-process chains from data-staging tools.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note Creation & Bulk File Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware attacks inherently produce ransom notes and encrypted file masses. Article emphasizes ransomware-support infrastructure; pipeline missed both the impact phase and pre-impact staging. Phrase: 'Ransomware Support'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass file creation of .txt or .html ransom notes alongside rapid file extension changes (legitimate-to-.ransomware-ext) in user profile or shared drives. Alert on >10% of drive encrypted in <1 hour; correlate with VSS deletion and backup-mount enumeration.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Network Discovery Pre-Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware-as-a-service operations require network reconnaissance before encryption. Pipeline omitted discovery-phase detections. Article context implies multi-stage attack for maximizing ransom.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child chains: net.exe/quser/systeminfo followed by file-share enumeration (dir \\*\c$, net view \\*). Flag Get-ChildItem recursion on network paths, concurrent SMB 445 handshakes to multiple subnets, and WMI queries (Win32_Share, Win32_LogicalDisk).

suggestion.title: Sanctioned Entity Infrastructure Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article is about sanctions enforcement; pipeline should flag infrastructure IOCs (domains, ASNs, payment wallets) associated with the named VPN and cryptor sellers. No IOCs extracted at all.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a sanctioned-provider blocklist (VPN domains, cryptor-seller hosting, payment infrastructure) and alert on any direct connection attempts, DNS queries, or HTTP requests. Cross-reference with known ransomware-affiliate infrastructure for early warning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Untrusted Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages were 'disguised as student proxies'—malicious npm packages installed via dependency resolution. Article phrase: '148 npm Packages Disguised as Student Proxies'. Pipeline missed detection for supply-chain compromise entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install / yarn / pnpm execution for packages with malicious indicators: names mimicking proxy tools, zero/minimal download history, registry timestamps inconsistent with user history. Alert on suspicious package manifests referencing external scripts or postinstall hooks reaching unknown C2.

suggestion.title: NodeJS Process Establishing Unexpected Outbound Connections
suggestion.rationale: DDoS botnet requires C2 communication. Article: 'Turned Browsers Into a DDoS Botnet' implies command-and-control callbacks from browser/node contexts. Pipeline did not model C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate node_modules network egress. Alert on node.exe, node processes spawned by browsers, or script engines opening connections to non-standard ports, international IPs (especially if not correlating to CDN), or repeated re-connection attempts characteristic of botnet heartbeats.

suggestion.title: Browser JavaScript Injection and Malicious Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes browser transformation into DDoS bot. Malicious code injected via npm→browser. Article phrase: 'Turned Browsers Into a DDoS Botnet'. Pipeline missed behavioral signatures of JavaScript execution and injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser processes (Edge, Chrome, Firefox) for suspicious child process spawning, WebSocket or XMLHttpRequest to attacker C2, or in-memory injection patterns. Cross-reference with npm package installation timeline to correlate postinstall hooks with browser compromise timing.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound HTTP/S Traffic from Browser DDoS Bot
suggestion.rationale: Compromised browsers executing DDoS on external targets. Article: 'Turned Browsers Into a DDoS Botnet'. Pipeline did not suggest impact/exfiltration detection (traffic volume, request patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous traffic volume or rate from single browser instances: sustained > 1000 req/s, target-agnostic flooding patterns, or Request headers identical across floods (fingerprint of script-driven botnet vs. user traffic). Correlate with known DDoS victim IPs or subnets.

suggestion.title: npm Registry or Package Repository Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: 148 packages uploaded or modified by attacker. Article: 'npm Packages Disguised as Student Proxies' implies account compromise or registry injection. Pipeline missed registry-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn package repository access logs for: new package uploads by inactive or suspicious accounts, version bumps with changed package size / hash not matching source repo, metadata injection (homepage, repository URLs pointing to attacker infrastructure), or rapid publish-unpublish cycles indicative of testing malicious artifacts.

suggestion.title: Compromised npm Account Behavioral Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack likely required compromised maintainer accounts or new attacker-owned accounts with rapid org/team membership escalation. Pipeline did not model auth/account layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm account logins from new geographic regions, new API tokens generated and immediately used for package publish, bulk package publishing by low-reputation or newly-created accounts, or accounts suddenly shifting from consumer (install) to publisher (release) profile.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Salesforce API Token Creation or Unauthorized API Access
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters campaigns consistently pivot through API tokens to maintain persistence and escalate access within SaaS targets. Article describes 'three Salesforce attack paths'—API abuse is standard for Salesforce-focused threat actors. Look for: 'Three Salesforce Attack Paths' implies API-centric exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API token creation events outside normal maintenance windows, API calls from IPs/geolocations inconsistent with user baseline, and token usage spikes within minutes of creation. Flag OAuth tokens generated by service accounts during non-business hours or with overly permissive scopes (data:read, data:write on sensitive objects).

suggestion.title: Salesforce Mass Data Export or Unusual SOQL Query Volume
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters operates as a data-theft-for-hire group; article title highlights year-long campaign implying sustained exfiltration. Salesforce breaches typically manifest as bulk queries or exports of customer/opportunity records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SOQL queries returning >10k rows in single session, data exports initiated by non-Admin accounts, or API calls to /services/data/v**/query or bulk API endpoints returning unexpectedly large result sets. Correlate with off-hours access patterns.

suggestion.title: Phishing or Credential Harvest Targeting Salesforce Admins/Users
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'year of ShinyHunters Activity'—initial access for Salesforce compromises typically relies on phishing or credential reuse. No IOCs or phishing indicators extracted despite critical severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails containing Salesforce-lookalike domains, requests for MFA codes or session tokens, and credential submission to non-Salesforce endpoints. Cross-correlate with Salesforce login failures followed by successful logins from new IP/device within hours.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass or Session Hijacking via Stolen Cookies/Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Salesforce-targeting campaigns routinely bypass MFA through token theft or session fixation. Article states 'three attack paths'—MFA evasion likely comprises at least one pathway for sustained access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Salesforce logins with MFA disabled or bypassed, session_id reuse across non-adjacent IPs, or successful logins immediately after failed MFA attempts. Flag browser/device fingerprint changes within same session.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Within Salesforce: Privilege Escalation to Admin or Custom Roles
suggestion.rationale: Once inside Salesforce, threat actors escalate to admin or high-privilege roles to access sensitive data and modify audit logs. Year-long campaign indicates sustained lateral movement within the platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on role assignment changes (especially to Admin or custom high-privilege roles) from non-HRIS automation accounts, permission set group additions by unexpected users, and sharing rule modifications enabling org-wide access to sensitive objects.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Audit Log Deletion or Modification Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated actors disable or delete audit logs to cover tracks. Article describes 'year of activity'—any campaign lasting >3 months without log tampering is rare. No defensive indicators extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for login history record deletions, audit trail export or archival to unexpected destinations, disable of audit logging features (if permissions allow), or gaps in audit timestamps suggesting tampering. Cross-check against immutable cloud logging backups.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Successful Authentication Without Credential Entry
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'forge HMAC-signed cookies' and achieve 'account takeover.' This is the core exploitation path—detect authentication events (session creation, privilege escalation actions) that occur without corresponding password entry or login process. Cite: 'forge HMAC-signed cookies'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful Kimai authentication to admin or privileged accounts when the session bearer token (Symfony PHPSESSID or equivalent) appears in access logs without a preceding login event in the Kimai auth log or without password submission captured in web proxy.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Deployment with Unmodified Default APP_SECRET
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'Docker entrypoint does not override or validate' the default secret value. Detect containers deployed with default configuration. Cite: 'Docker image ships with APP_SECRET=change_this_to_something_unique... does not override'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Kimai container image deployments for missing or unset APP_SECRET environment variable override. Compare deployment manifests, container runtime config, and image metadata against hardened baselines that require explicit APP_SECRET configuration.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Suspicious Web Session Bulk Operations Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker forges cookie and gains 'account takeover,' they will perform lateral movement or data exfiltration. Monitor for bulk timesheet modifications, user creation, or configuration changes tied to hijacked sessions. Cite: 'account takeover' and Kimai's time-tracking purpose.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate session IDs with bulk write operations (mass timesheet edits, user/project creation, rate changes). Flag sessions showing off-hours or impossible-travel bulk modifications inconsistent with the legitimate account holder's behavior.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Impossible Travel Detection on Authentication Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Forged cookies can originate from attacker-controlled infrastructure. Detect session IPs and user-agents that violate geographic/temporal plausibility. Cite: 'unauthenticated attacker' forging cookies from arbitrary network locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Kimai session IPs, user-agents, and source locations per account. Flag sessions from IPs thousands of kilometers apart within seconds, or sessions from countries/ASNs never accessed by the account previously.

suggestion.title: Kimai: HTTP Cookie Header Anomalies (Known-Secret Signatures)
suggestion.rationale: If Kimai logs or proxies capture full cookie headers, HMAC-forged cookies may exhibit patterns (timestamps, signature structure) consistent with the known APP_SECRET. Cite: 'forge HMAC-signed cookies' using 'publicly-known Symfony kernel.secret'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Collect and parse Symfony session cookies (if readable in logs). Correlate cookie HMAC signatures against the known default APP_SECRET hash to identify forged cookies in web traffic.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Docker Image Scanning for Hardcoded Default Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Article's root cause is default secret in the official Docker image. Proactive detection should scan images pre-deployment. Cite: 'official Kimai Docker image ships with APP_SECRET=change_this_to_something_unique'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Kimai container images (registry names, tags matching Kimai) for hardcoded environment variables, .env files, or config artifacts containing the string 'change_this_to_something_unique' or Kimai's documented default secrets.

suggestion.title: TOTP Brute-Force via Unauthenticated 2FA Endpoint (UC_10_1 corrected)
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint 'accepts unauthenticated POST containing only fsNick and fsTwoFactorCode' with TOTP that is 'brute-forceable'; pipeline generated no detections for the core exploit. Article references UC_10_1 but pipeline output was empty. Original UC_10_1 detection hunts for hardcoded poc_2fa_brute.py tool (hallucinated/undocumented), bypassed by custom scripts. Should hunt behavior instead.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to /login?action=two-factor-validation from same source with 5+ distinct fsTwoFactorCode values in <300 seconds. Flag if request lacks prior session password authentication. Look for 401/403→200 response cascade indicating brute-force success. Correlate with immediate downstream authentication or sensitive operations.

suggestion.title: Session Creation Without Password Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states handler 'does not verify the password' yet 'issues full fsNick + fsLogkey session cookie pair'; anomalous authentication flow bypass should be detected at credential creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on session cookie issuance (fsLogkey created) from 2FA endpoint (/login?action=two-factor-validation) when no password-authentication event (hash check, password field submission, or MFA prompt initiation) appears in same session within prior 5 minutes. Indicates bypass of normal login flow.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Account Abuse After 2FA Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation grants full account access; pipeline should include hunt for behavioral divergence from baseline following suspicious 2FA activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate anomalous 2FA session creation with subsequent atypical user activity: invoking admin functions, exporting sensitive data, creating API tokens, modifying account settings, accessing resources outside baseline geography/time-of-day. Flag if baseline profile or geographic travel is impossible.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: Enumeration of FacturaScripts /login Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in public /login endpoint; attackers must first discover FacturaScripts instances. Pipeline provided no reconnaissance-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200/302 responses to /login endpoints from script-like user-agents (curl, Python-requests, Nmap, etc.) with rapid sequential probing. Flag sources explicitly querying /login?action=two-factor-validation, indicating targeted reconnaissance for this CVE endpoint.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Web Interface CSRF Exploitation via /level/15/exec/ URIs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names exploit URIs: '/level/15/exec/-' and '/level/15/exec/-/configure/http'. States these enable 'arbitrary commands' execution. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite clear HTTP-based attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP GET/POST requests to Cisco IOS web interface on ports 80, 443, or device management ports targeting /level/15/exec/* paths. Correlate with Cisco device configuration/command logs for unexpected execution within seconds of suspicious HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Remote Arbitrary Command Execution Post-CSRF
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via (1) show privilege (2) alias exec commands'. No execution-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco device logs for privilege-level-15 command execution without corresponding SSH/console login sessions. Flag atypical source IPs issuing commands via web interface (check syslog for HTTP-originated sessions).

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Vulnerability Indicator Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner'. Pipeline produced no IOC output. Vulnerability CVE is the primary detection anchor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner results for CVE-2008-4128 in Cisco IOS 12.4. Cross-reference affected assets with network exposure (untrusted access paths, internet-facing ACLs). Escalate any matches given CISA KEV status and 2026-07-16 remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS 12.4 Public-Facing Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Standard asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' pattern. Zero exposure-focused use cases generated despite T1190 (public-facing exploitation) applicability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco IOS 12.4 devices with HTTP/HTTPS management ports (80, 443, 8080, 8443) routable from internet or DMZ. Prioritize by asset criticality. Verify patch status immediately given federal due date.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 — Cisco IOS 12.4 Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and names CVE-2008-4128 as the target: 'Cisco IOS 12.4 contains multiple cross-site forgery vulnerabilities.' CISA KEV means active exploitation; federal patch due 2026-07-16.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query endpoint/network inventory for Cisco IOS version 12.4 or CVE-2008-4128 matches. Alert on unpatched systems. Correlate against patch management DB — patch lag is 'the silent killer' per article guidance.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to Cisco IOS Privileged URI Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack URIs: '/level/15/exec/-' and '/level/15/exec/-/configure/http'. These are concrete exploitation routes that should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests (POST/GET) to Cisco IOS management interface URIs ending in /level/15/exec or /configure/http, especially those carrying 'show privilege' or 'alias exec' commands in parameters or body. Flag external/untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS CSRF — Arbitrary Command Execution Signals
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via (1) a certain "show privilege" command' and '(2) a certain "alias exec" command.' These are the actual attack primitives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS devices for sudden privilege escalation (esp. to level 15), alias command definitions, or config changes correlated with HTTP access to the vulnerable URIs. Flag changes outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Web Interface CSRF Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: CSRF exploitation typically involves crafted requests without valid session tokens. Article describes web-based attack surface (/level/15/exec URIs) that can be probed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to vulnerable URIs that lack expected CSRF tokens, session cookies, or auth headers. Look for repeated/scanning patterns, anomalous User-Agents, or requests from external/public IP ranges to internal Cisco IOS management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Cisco IOS 12.4 — Post-Exploitation Command Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: After gaining execution via T1190, attacker will run commands. Article promises 'arbitrary commands' — detection should monitor for anomalous command execution on unpatched devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Cisco IOS 12.4 systems flagged as vulnerable/unpatched, alert on: (a) unexpected command execution via HTTP/HTTPS session; (b) privilege level changes to 15; (c) configuration changes tied to privilege escalation commands.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Timeline Compliance — CVE-2008-4128 Patch Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-16.' CISA KEV imposes hard deadline; organizational compliance is measurable and auditable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated alerting: Any Cisco IOS device flagged for CVE-2008-4128 still unpatched as of 2026-07-16 triggers escalation. Track remediation progress against CISA deadline for regulatory/audit reporting.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Vulnerable Device Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cisco IOS 12.4 contains multiple cross-site forgery vulnerabilities' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL'. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan or query asset inventory for Cisco IOS versions matching 12.4.x running exposed management interfaces. Cross-reference patch compliance database against 2026-07-16 federal due date. Flag any unpatched instances as immediate exploitation risk given CISA KEV status.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to Cisco IOS Privilege Escalation URIs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable endpoints: '/level/15/exec/-' and '/level/15/exec/-/configure/http'. Exploitation requires HTTP requests to these exact URIs on exposed Cisco devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco IOS management interfaces containing URI patterns '/level/15/exec/' followed by command injection payloads. Correlate source IPs with internet-facing Cisco IOS devices. Flag any requests originating from external networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Unauthorized Privilege Level Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'show privilege' command and privilege level manipulation. Successful exploitation would result in arbitrary command execution at level 15 (highest privilege).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS syslog for privilege level transitions to level 15 without corresponding authorization records. Look for 'alias exec' command installations paired with administrative URI access. Baseline normal privilege escalation timing and source—flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Management Interface Web Access from Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerabilities require CSRF capability and HTTP access to management URIs. Article implies public-facing exploitation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco IOS devices with HTTP/HTTPS management interfaces reachable from external networks (non-RFC1918 sources). Correlate with patch status. Alert on any outbound CISA KEV exploitation signatures or cross-site forgery payloads in HTTP headers.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Configuration Backup Changes Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful arbitrary command execution (stated in article) would allow attackers to modify running-config or startup-config. Detection via backup drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline hashes of Cisco IOS running and startup configs from pre-patch inventory. Monitor for unexpected modifications to these configs outside of change-control windows. Particularly flag additions of new 'alias exec' commands or privilege level entries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Cisco IOS Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2008-4128 — match against your vulnerability scanner' in the IOC section and cites standard asset-exposure hunt methodology. Pipeline generated zero detections for this known-exploited CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any successful CVE-2008-4128 vulnerability scan match or Cisco IOS 12.4 identification against internal or external-facing assets. Cross-check against patch baseline. Federal patch due-date 2026-07-16 is SOC escalation trigger.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS HTTP Management Interface CSRF Attack Vector Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific exploitation vectors: 'show privilege command to /level/15/exec/- URI' and 'alias exec command to /level/15/exec/-/configure/http URI'. No detection for HTTP requests matching these CSRF paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco IOS management interfaces (port 80/443) with URI patterns containing /level/15/exec/- or /level/15/exec/-/configure/http, especially those with command parameters like 'show privilege' or 'alias exec' from untrusted sources. CSRF attacks often have anomalous Referer headers or missing session context.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Arbitrary Command Execution Post-CSRF
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'execute arbitrary commands' post-exploitation. No detection for command execution artifacts in device logs following CSRF attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected 'show privilege' or 'alias exec' commands in Cisco IOS audit logs, especially if temporally correlated with suspicious HTTP requests to management interface. Flag configuration changes or privilege escalations without corresponding authorized change tickets.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Cisco IOS Exposure Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active reconnaissance of exposed assets. Article references 'standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated no hunt for identifying vulnerable Cisco IOS on internet-facing networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference internet-wide scan data (Shodan, Censys, Project Sonar) for Cisco IOS HTTP management interfaces. Correlate with internal asset inventory to identify unaccounted exposures. Every exposed instance is exploitation-ready per active KEV catalog status.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS 12.4 Patch Compliance and Version Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Cisco IOS 12.4 contains multiple cross-site forgery vulnerabilities'. Recommended hunt should include baseline inventory for patch-level risk detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Cisco IOS deployments for version 12.4 or equivalent unpatched variants. Identify systems not updated by federal due-date 2026-07-16. Generate remediation worklist ranked by exposure level (internet-facing > DMZ > internal).

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Configuration Tampering via Alias Exec Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'alias exec' command exploitation to /configure/http URI as method to modify device behavior. No detection for unauthorized config changes post-CSRF attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS configuration commit logs for unexpected 'alias' commands or HTTP-related config changes. Baseline known aliases; alert on new ones. Correlate with failed or anomalous HTTP management interface access attempts. Flag if changes occur outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Vulnerable Cisco IOS Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2008-4128 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and identifies Cisco IOS 12.4 as affected; pipeline must surface scanner results for vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results identifying Cisco IOS 12.4 or CVE-2008-4128 matches. Cross-correlate with network routing to flag publicly-routable instances as high-risk.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Privilege Escalation URI Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies two exploitation vectors: 'show privilege' command to /level/15/exec/- URI and 'alias exec' to /level/15/exec/-/configure/http URI. These are direct attack signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco device management interfaces for URIs matching /level/15/exec/* patterns. Alert especially on requests containing 'show privilege' or 'alias exec' payloads from non-authenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Remote Command Execution on Cisco IOS Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows attackers to 'execute arbitrary commands' via CSRF; detection should trigger on unauthorized command execution in device logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of configuration and exec-level commands (privilege level 15) from sources without corresponding authenticated login sessions. Correlate command logs with HTTP access logs showing CSRF-like request patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco Device Unauthenticated Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: CSRF vulnerability implies device is network-accessible; must detect attempts to access management interfaces without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for expected administrative access sources to Cisco IOS devices. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS connections to management ports (typically 80, 443, 8080) from unexpected external networks lacking valid authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Cisco IOS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article source is CISA KEV indicating 'active exploitation in the wild'; detection should identify reconnaissance and exploitation payloads targeting this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests and payloads matching known CVE-2008-4128 exploitation techniques. Alert on enumeration attempts for /level/15/exec/ URIs even from trusted networks, as it indicates attacker reconnaissance activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco Device Configuration Changes Post-Web Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ability to execute 'alias exec' and configuration commands; detect persistence or lateral movement via unexpected device config changes correlated with prior HTTP exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected Cisco device configuration changes with prior suspicious HTTP access to privilege-escalation URIs. Alert if configuration uploads, alias commands, or privilege-level changes occur without matching AAA authentication records.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Cisco IOS Vulnerability Match
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2008-4128 as the primary indicator, mentioned repeatedly as the active KEV. This must be an IOC and a baseline hunt: 'CVE-2008-4128' should match against vulnerability scanner outputs and patch compliance reports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanners for Cisco IOS 12.4 or unpatched IOS endpoints. Cross-reference with network exposure data (ports 80/443) to flag exploitable assets. Federal patch due 2026-07-16 establishes urgency baseline.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to Cisco IOS Privilege Escalation URI
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'show privilege' command exploitation via /level/15/exec/- URI. This is a specific attack vector that should trigger web/firewall alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to /level/15/exec/- path on Cisco IOS devices from external or untrusted sources. CSRF attacks typically lack Referer headers or present suspicious origins. Correlate with failed auth or privilege-check attempts.

suggestion.title: HTTP-Triggered 'alias exec' Command Injection on Cisco IOS
suggestion.rationale: Article names second vector: 'alias exec' command via /level/15/exec/-/configure/http URI. This creates command shortcuts on the device, establishing persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS running config for new or modified 'alias exec' entries. Correlate creation time with HTTP requests from non-management addresses to /level/15/exec/-/configure/http. Flag as high-severity (indicates post-exploitation persistence).

suggestion.title: Remote Command Execution via Cisco IOS Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands' without authentication. RCE must be detectable via command logging after CSRF exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS for unexpected command execution (e.g., show, alias, configure, reload) from HTTP sessions rather than SSH/Telnet sessions. Flag commands with no corresponding authenticated user session as high-priority compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Management Interface Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires HTTP/HTTPS access to IOS management interface (/level/15/exec/ paths). CISA KEV status means exploitation is active; exposed instances need immediate visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run internal scans to identify Cisco IOS devices with HTTP/HTTPS management ports (80, 443, 8080, 8443) accessible from untrusted subnets or external networks. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm expected management access paths.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS 12.4 CVE-2008-4128 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies two attack URIs: 'show privilege' to `/level/15/exec/-` and 'alias exec' to `/level/15/exec/-/configure/http` with remote command execution payload. Pipeline produced no detection for these explicit network indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Cisco device mgmt interfaces matching URI patterns /level/15/exec/- or /level/15/exec/-/configure/http with suspicious commands (show privilege, alias exec). Correlate source IP + request timing with credential-less access attempts to identify CSRF exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Device Inventory + Vulnerability Match (CVE-2008-4128)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and requires federal remediation by 2026-07-16; recommends fleet-wide exposure hunt. Pipeline omitted asset-exposure UC despite article's explicit reference to template guidance.

suggestion.title: HTTP CSRF Exploitation Attempts to Cisco IOS Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vectors: 'show privilege command to /level/15/exec/- URI' and 'alias exec command to /level/15/exec/-/configure/http URI'—exploits accessible via HTTP to the web interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to URIs matching `/level/15/exec/-` or `/level/15/exec/-/configure/http` patterns against known Cisco IOS devices. Flag requests lacking CSRF token or with token mismatches. Monitor for anomalous referer headers indicating external CSRF source.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Command Execution Post-Exploitation from Cisco IOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands' via CSRF—requires behavioral detection of command shells spawned by web interface processes on compromised devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS process audit logs for command execution spawned by web interface services (usually running as 'httpd' or equivalent). Look for anomalous commands issued without corresponding CLI user sessions. High-risk commands: 'configure terminal', 'write memory', 'reload'.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Privilege Escalation Detection
suggestion.rationale: The URIs referenced (`/level/15/exec/-`) indicate privilege level 15 (maximum) access—exploitation grants unintended privileged command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication or privilege escalation events in Cisco IOS audit logs where a non-privileged session suddenly acquires level 15 rights via HTTP interface. Correlate with failed prior attempts or external IP addresses.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Ensure vulnerability scanner coverage for CVE-2008-4128 explicitly; article states this CVE is actively exploited in the wild per CISA KEV status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Confirm all vulnerability scanners include CVE-2008-4128 detection rules. Verify scan results against Cisco IOS 12.4 endpoints. Flag any 'not scanned' or 'inconclusive' results as gaps requiring manual verification given active exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Vulnerability Inventory Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs use of vulnerability scanner: 'CVE: CVE-2008-4128—match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline produced zero IOC or inventory-based detection despite this being the core detection vector for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system for CVE-2008-4128 matches. Flag any unpatched instances; cross-reference against patch remediation records to identify assets missing federal deadline (2026-07-16).

suggestion.title: HTTP URI-Based CSRF Command Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names explicit attack paths: 'show privilege command to /level/15/exec/- URI' and 'alias exec command to /level/15/exec/-/configure/http URI.' Pipeline captured neither URI pattern nor command signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for paths containing '/level/15/exec/' or '/configure/http'. Correlate with Cisco device audit logs for unexpected execution of 'show privilege' or 'alias exec' commands. Alert on external-origin requests to these URIs.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS 12.4 External Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and recommends checking 'across your fleet.' Standard asset-exposure hunt for internet-facing vulnerable instances is missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco IOS 12.4 devices; cross-reference with network exposure data (ports 80, 443, 8080). Flag any unpatched instances found internet-accessible. Correlate with patch management to identify assets exceeding federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Privilege-Level 15 URI Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacks against '/level/15/exec/-' path, indicating privilege-escalation vector. No detection for privilege-level URI traversal or access outside administrative baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco device logs for requests to URIs containing '/level/15/' from non-administrative source IPs. Alert on repeated failed attempts or successful access from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery to Cisco Management Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is explicitly 'cross-site forgery vulnerabilities'; attack includes '/configure/http' path suggesting HTTP-based config manipulation. CSRF detection is absent from all outputs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/PUT requests to Cisco management URIs lacking Origin/Referer headers or with mismatched origins. Alert on config change operations lacking expected CSRF token validation responses.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Command Execution via Cisco IOS CLI Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands'—this is T1059 execution phase, completely missing from kill-chain and use-case outputs despite being the attacker's final objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline 'show privilege' and 'alias exec' command usage by legitimate administrators. Alert on execution outside administrative windows, from unexpected source IPs, or with anomalous payloads (e.g., embedded shell metacharacters, configuration changes).

suggestion.title: Malware C2 Registration & Domain Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'ORB Network' expansion with new 'LONGLEASH' malware—implies infrastructure acquisition; likely C2 domains or IP registration patterns if article details hosting providers, domain registrants, or DNS records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries to newly registered or newly seen domains associated with ORB infrastructure. Correlate domain registration metadata against known LONGLEASH C2 infrastructure patterns. Alert on successful connections from endpoints to suspected C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: China-Linked APT UAT-7810 Malware Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Actor name 'UAT-7810' and malware 'LONGLEASH' are introduced in title; article likely describes delivery mechanism, staging, or lateral movement using this malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for LONGLEASH process execution patterns, file writes, and behavioral indicators (code injection, network beaconing). Correlate with known UAT-7810 TTPs. Alert on child-process spawning or DLL injection chains consistent with malware post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via ORB Network Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'expansion' of ORB network—implies infrastructure being weaponized for multi-stage deployment or persistence across compromised hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track internal traffic flows initiated from suspected ORB C2 endpoints to secondary targets. Detect anomalous inter-subnet scanning, SMB-based exploitation, or Windows Admin Share usage originating from actor-controlled pivots.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 asset-exposure hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...] Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2008-4128'. Pipeline ignored direct instruction and generated zero UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Cisco IOS systems in asset inventory missing patch dated ≤2026-07-16, or with CVE-2008-4128 in active scanner results. Correlate with network exposure scans to identify internet-facing targets.

suggestion.title: HTTP exploitation attempts to /level/15/exec/ URIs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies two attack vectors: (1) 'show privilege' to /level/15/exec/- URI and (2) 'alias exec' to /level/15/exec/-/configure/http URI. Concrete IOC patterns and request signatures not extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests (especially POST with command-like params) to URIs matching /level/15/exec/- on Cisco IOS targets from external sources. Alert on missing/forged Referer headers, which is signature of CSRF exploitation.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary command execution on Cisco IOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands'. Pipeline mapped only T1190; missed T1059 and privilege escalation mechanics via show privilege and configure commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS web server processes for unexpected spawned system commands; flag execution of configure terminal or show running-config triggered by HTTP request with privilege 15 context.

suggestion.title: CSRF exploitation sequence on Cisco IOS web interface
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability type is explicit CSRF; attack mechanism (crafted requests bypassing SOP) is core to exploitation chain but not reconstructed in pipeline kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multi-stage request sequences from single external IP to Cisco IOS HTTP interface with anomalous Referer/Origin headers or missing CSRF tokens. Flag within 30s windows indicative of scripted attack.

suggestion.title: Federal compliance—CVE-2008-4128 patch by 2026-07-16
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date' and 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators'. Compliance tracking absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compliance report: all Cisco IOS systems must show patch or documented workaround by 2026-07-16. Non-compliant assets escalate to owner with KEV active-exploitation advisory.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS 12.4 Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cisco IOS 12.4 contains multiple cross-site forgery vulnerabilities' and is in CISA KEV (observed exploitation). Asset inventory is the foundation for any patch-due-date compliance hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search inventory for Cisco IOS devices running version 12.4. Correlate against patch status to identify unpatched instances. Federal remediation due: 2026-07-16.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to Vulnerable Cisco Management Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article names two specific attack URIs: '/level/15/exec/-' (show privilege command) and '/level/15/exec/-/configure/http' (alias exec command). Direct IOCs for malicious HTTP patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to Cisco device IPs on ports 80/443 containing the URI patterns /level/15/exec/- or /level/15/exec/-/configure/http. Cisco IOS default management port is 80; flag any outbound CSRF payloads to these paths.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Exposed Management Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attackers' exploiting HTTP-based URIs, implying Internet-exposed management. 'Allows remote attackers' + CISA KEV active exploitation = exposed interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco IOS HTTP management interfaces exposed to untrusted networks (WAN-facing). Look for device identification banners, HTTP 200 responses to /level/15/ paths, or Cisco-specific HTTP headers (Server: Cisco-IOS). Correlate with version 12.4 to flag critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Command Execution Post-CSRF on Cisco Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands.' Detection should cover the command-execution phase, not just the CSRF delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS command execution logs (syslog, SNMP trap logs) for commands executed by unauthorized or suspicious sources. Look for show/configure/alias commands not initiated by authenticated users. Correlate timing with HTTP requests to /level/15/ URIs.

suggestion.title: Cisco Device Configuration Changes via HTTP Interface
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector includes 'alias exec command to the /level/15/exec/-/configure/http URI' — implies modification of device configuration state. Detection should monitor unauthorized config changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration modifications to Cisco devices (running-config changes, alias commands added, new privilege levels created) that are NOT preceded by authenticated CLI sessions or SNMP v3 management. Cross-reference with HTTP access logs to identify CSRF-originating changes.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Patch Compliance — CVE-2008-4128 by 2026-07-16
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due-date of 2026-07-16. Regulatory compliance tracking is a critical use case for CISA KEV entries, and this date is enforcement-relevant for federal contractors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all Cisco IOS deployments for patch status of CVE-2008-4128. Generate daily compliance dashboard showing % remediated, % at risk, and % overdue (after 2026-07-16). Flag any unpatched instances as critical for audit trail.

suggestion.title: Cross-tenant workflow version read access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated tenant could read workflow version snapshots belonging to other tenants.' This is unauthorized disclosure—detection must key on auth logs or app logs showing a tenant context accessing workflow versions owned by another tenant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on n8n-mcp application logs when a tenant ID in the auth context attempts to read or retrieve workflow version endpoints where the resource owner tenant differs. Correlate successful reads (HTTP 200) with tenant isolation configuration to identify access-control bypass.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized cross-tenant workflow backup deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could delete or destroy other tenants' stored backups.' Monitor for deletion of versioned snapshots by a tenant that does not own them—a direct impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor deletion/modification of workflow version history files or backups in multi-tenant n8n deployments. Alert when a tenant context deletes snapshots belonging to a different tenant_id, or when backup counts/integrity hashes diverge unexpectedly across tenant scopes.

suggestion.title: Multi-tenant workflow resource enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Cross-tenant access presupposes discovery. Article's phrase 'workflow version history... was not isolated per tenant' implies attackers can enumerate backups across tenants via API or file listing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authenticated requests that enumerate or list workflow version endpoints or backup directories outside the authenticated tenant's namespace. Flag API calls to /workflows/versions or similar that reference foreign tenant identifiers in path parameters or response metadata.

suggestion.title: n8n-MCP multi-tenant isolation bypass exploitation
suggestion.rationale: T1190 exploitation of publicly-exposed HTTP server. The vulnerability is in the HTTP deployment's tenant-isolation logic; successful exploitation manifests as cross-tenant data access following n8n-specific paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests targeting n8n-mcp endpoints for CVE-2026-54052 exploitation patterns: requests to /workflows/{id}/versions/ where tenant isolation is bypassed, path traversal attempts to cross-tenant backup directories, or requests with forged/missing tenant-context headers.

suggestion.title: Anyquery ATTACH DATABASE command in query traffic or logs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attackers ... use the ATTACH DATABASE command' — this is the exploitation primitive itself. No UC directly hunts for ATTACH DATABASE in Anyquery query stream or audit logs, yet it is the signature of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Anyquery server query logs or MySQL wire protocol traffic for ATTACH DATABASE statements from unauthenticated or external sources. Look for ATTACH DATABASE followed by filesystem paths like /etc/cron.d, /var/www, /root/.ssh. High-confidence alert if ATTACH targets writable persistence locations.

suggestion.title: Network listener exposed for Anyquery (asset exposure recon)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'connecting to the MySQL-compatible server port'—implies port discovery. Current UCs check process cmdline; should include network listener state and open port exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Anyquery process in LISTEN state on any network interface (default or custom port). Correlate with external connection attempts and absence of auth/TLS. Indicates attack surface exposed to unauthenticated clients.

suggestion.title: AD FS Unauthorized Privilege Escalation (CVE-2026-56155)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-56155 is 'actively exploited' with 'insufficient granularity of access control in Active Directory Federation Services allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.' No detection hypothesis generated despite confirmed active attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AD FS service logs for access control modifications or token issuance anomalies. Alert on ADFS admins performing privilege escalation or token claims escalation outside normal baseline. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to higher-privilege AD FS endpoints.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Unauthenticated Remote Access Exploitation (CVE-2026-56164)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2026-56164 'actively exploited' with 'missing authentication for critical function' allowing 'unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.' This is a pre-auth RCE pattern requiring immediate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to SharePoint critical endpoints (typically /sites/, /_api/, /_layouts) from external networks without valid authentication tokens. Flag requests with missing Authorization headers or invalid session cookies to admin functions. Correlate with subsequent process execution or privilege elevation.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Bypass Exploitation (CVE-2026-50661)
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses CVE-2026-50661 as publicly available bypass allowing 'attackers to gain access to encrypted data' via 'physical access to the target.' Detection should focus on BitLocker state monitoring and bypass indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BitLocker status changes, decryption events, or disabled BitLocker protection on system drives. Alert on recovery key access or PowerShell/WMI calls querying BitLocker configuration post-patch. Flag systems running unpatched versions still vulnerable to CVE-2026-50661.

suggestion.title: Critical Elevation of Privilege Detection (254 EOPs in Patch)
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 254 elevation of privilege vulnerabilities in this patch alone. Pipeline generated zero detection rules despite EOP being the largest vulnerability category and primary attack vector post-initial-access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline process execution privileges at patch date. Post-patch, alert on processes running with unexpected elevated tokens (e.g., System/Admin running from user directory). Monitor for parent-child process anomalies where low-privilege processes spawn system-level children via known EOP services.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vendor Zero-Day Coordination Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Progress Software ShareFile emergency shutdown, Cisco CVE-2026-20230 active exploitation, Adobe ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 exploitation — pipeline missed correlated detection across ecosystem. These suggest coordinated scanning/exploitation campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exploitation attempts across Microsoft, Adobe, Cisco, and Fortinet products within 24-hour windows. Alert on scanner fingerprints (User-Agent, HTTP patterns) probing multiple vendors' known CVE endpoints. Flag networks with simultaneous patch Tuesday day-0 exploitation across vendors.

suggestion.title: Linux Januscape VM Escape Exploitation (Host Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: Article states Linux kernel Januscape flaw 'allows attackers to escape a virtual machine and execute arbitrary code on the host.' This is a hypervisor escape with direct host-compromise implications not addressed in use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Linux guest VMs for suspicious kernel module loading or cgroup manipulation attempts post-Januscape publication. Alert on VM-to-hypervisor process anomalies (e.g., guest processes accessing host memory directly). Flag bare-metal Linux systems running vulnerable kernels with network-facing container workloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Repository Commit Modifying CI/CD Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Compromised CI/CD Pipelines in Two Repositories'—the attack surface is unauthorized commits that inject malware into build automation. No detection use case addresses anomalous git activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits to .github/workflows, Dockerfile, package.json scripts, or build configuration files from unexpected user accounts, anomalous geographies, or outside business hours. Flag modifications that add new package dependencies or install scripts, especially targeting AsyncAPI-related modules.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation Spawning Unexpected Outbound Network Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Miasma RAT Delivered via Compromised CI/CD Pipelines'—the RAT payload executes during npm install, establishing command-and-control. No use case covers C2 beaconing from package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process hierarchies where npm or Node.js spawns child processes initiating outbound connections to non-standard ports or suspicious destinations shortly after install. Detect regular connection patterns (beaconing) or encrypted payloads consistent with RAT C2.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from npm Package Installation with Unsigned/Unusual Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware executes scripts during installation phase ('Delivered via Compromised CI/CD Pipelines'). Article implies arbitrary code execution through package installation hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned from npm/Node.js installation (npm install, yarn install) running unsigned or rare binaries, shell interpreters, or network utilities. Prioritize execution chains with high entropy process names or paths outside standard node_modules.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency Injection into AsyncAPI Generator Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Malicious AsyncAPI Generator' components. Attack injects unauthorized dependencies into legitimate packages. No use case detects package.json / lock file tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package metadata (package.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock) for AsyncAPI-related packages; flag version pins to unusual registries, git URLs instead of npm registry, or suspicious version strings. Cross-reference against known legitimate AsyncAPI package versions.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation Post-Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: RATs establish persistence ('Miasma RAT Delivered'). No detection use case monitors for post-installation persistence hooks (cron jobs, systemd services, registry modifications).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm package installation events with subsequent creation of scheduled tasks, cron jobs, systemd services, or shell rc-file modifications that reference paths within node_modules or invoke node/npm. Flag persistence mechanisms created within seconds of package install completion.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via CI/CD Artifact Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Compromised pipelines affect 'two repositories'—artifacts flow downstream to other systems via published npm packages. No use case tracks downstream propagation to consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package downloads for AsyncAPI generator variants; correlate download events with subsequent process execution and network anomalies on downstream systems. Flag packages with recent publish timestamps, unusual maintainer accounts, or elevated download velocity.

suggestion.title: FacturaScripts API key privilege escalation: limited-scope key accessing restricted resources
suggestion.rationale: Article states PoC used 'scoped ApiKey with fullaccess=0 and allowget=1 on clientes resource only,' yet SQLi enabled access beyond intended scope. Missing detection: ApiKey requesting resources outside its declared scope post-SQLi injection.
log_sources: Access logs with API key context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track ApiKey grants (fullaccess, allowget scope) and alert when single ApiKey accesses /api/3/* resources not in its allowget list. Correlate timing with filter parameter mutations. Requires API key lifecycle logs or WAF/API gateway that logs both auth token and requested resource.

suggestion.title: SQL error message exfiltration in HTTP response body (SQLi information disclosure)
suggestion.rationale: Article PoC 'response body' contains injected SELECT results. Missing: detection of abnormally large HTTP response bodies from /api/3/* containing SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, FROM, TABLE) or error messages (syntax, database, column).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on /api/3/* requests where response size exceeds baseline for that URI by >200%, AND response body matches regex for SQL keywords or error patterns. Baseline per resource (clientes, proveedores, etc.) to avoid FP on bulk exports.

suggestion.title: FacturaScripts filter parameter encoding mutation sequence (obfuscation attempt)
suggestion.rationale: Article uses '%20', '%28', '%5b' encoding mixed with literal syntax. Missing: detection of repeated filter parameter mutations (mixed URL encoding, case variations, comment syntax like /**/,-- ) within short time window from single source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track filter parameter values per source over 5-min windows. Alert if same source submits >3 distinct encodings of same logical filter (e.g., (SELECT), %28SELECT%29, %28SELECT/**/), indicating obfuscation testing or WAF evasion.

suggestion.title: Successful data exfiltration via UNION SELECT: response row count inflation
suggestion.rationale: Article PoC response contains injected UNION SELECT output. Missing: detection of response object count inflation—when clientes resource normally returns N objects, but single request returns N + K (K = exfiltrated admin user table or password hash rows).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If available, correlate FacturaScripts application logs showing object counts returned per request. Alert when count exceeds 3-sigma from baseline for that endpoint. Supplement with response time anomalies (SELECT from injected table with millions of rows causes delay).

suggestion.title: Authenticated API key abuse post-SQLi: rapid credential enumeration or mass data download
suggestion.rationale: After exfiltrating user credentials via SQLi, attacker reuses/replays ApiKey or creates new ones. Missing: detection of ApiKey usage spike (request rate >5x baseline) or new ApiKey creation immediately following SQLi attempt from same source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline request-per-minute for each ApiKey. Alert if any key jumps >5x within 10 min of a filter parameter injection attempt from same source. Cross-reference ApiKey creation timestamps with SQLi attempt times.

suggestion.title: Detect NVIDIA-branded process with suspicious behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states malware 'masquerades as NVIDIA software'—pipeline missed defense_evasion through process/file spoofing. Legitimate NVIDIA processes should not spawn shells, write to system directories, or contact unexpected IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes with NVIDIA-related image names (nvidia*.exe, nvidiaupdate.exe, etc.) that deviate from expected NVIDIA application behavior: spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or connecting to non-NVIDIA IP space. Legitimate NVIDIA processes typically run from restricted directories and connect only to nvidia.com or NVIDIA CDNs.

suggestion.title: Detect unsigned executable masquerading as NVIDIA software
suggestion.rationale: RAT delivery mechanism relies on trojanized installer mimicking real NVIDIA software. Article premise ('masquerades') implies file-level spoofing without proper code signing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of files with NVIDIA product names in filename (nvidia*.exe, nvidiadriver*.exe, nvidiacontrolpanel*.exe) that lack valid Authenticode signatures or whose signatures don't chain to NVIDIA's trusted CA. Cross-check file hashes against known-good NVIDIA distributions.

suggestion.title: Detect RAT command-and-control callback from Windows hosts
suggestion.rationale: As a remote access trojan, LabubaRAT must establish C2 for 'control'—pipeline extracted zero network IOCs or behavioral signatures for callback detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from recently-executed NVIDIA-branded processes to non-NVIDIA IP addresses or domains. LabubaRAT likely uses HTTP/HTTPS or raw TCP for C2; look for beaconing patterns (periodic callbacks at fixed intervals) or encrypted traffic from suspicious processes to infrastructure not associated with GPU software updates.

suggestion.title: Detect persistence mechanisms deployed by LabubaRAT on Windows
suggestion.rationale: RAT 'masquerading' delivery typically followed by persistence (scheduled task, registry run key, DLL injection). Article describes 'control of Windows hosts'—implies sustained access, yet pipeline did not surface persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications to Run/RunOnce keys, creation of scheduled tasks with suspicious executable references, or DLL registration under NVIDIA-like paths. Watch for elevation of privilege attempts (UAC bypass) following initial NVIDIA process execution.

suggestion.title: Detect trojanized NVIDIA installer distribution and delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies malware 'masquerades as NVIDIA software'—implies delivery via fake installer. Pipeline missed initial_access phase entirely, which is where phishing, supply-chain compromise, or watering-hole attacks would be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails distributing EXE files with NVIDIA installer names; track downloads of suspicious files from non-NVIDIA domains claiming to be NVIDIA drivers or utilities. Cross-reference file hashes against threat-intel feeds. Alert on file delivery from external sources with NVIDIA branding but unsigned or improperly signed.

suggestion.title: SonicWall SMA1000 CVE-2026-15409 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' exploiting SSRF. No UC generated to detect exploitation attempts against public-facing SMA1000 instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SonicWall SMA1000 appliances for unauthenticated requests to known vulnerable endpoints or API paths associated with CVE-2026-15409. Correlate with failed authentication attempts and external source IPs. SSRF exploitation typically manifests as unexpected request patterns in appliance access logs.

suggestion.title: SonicWall SMA1000 Anomalous Internal Request Forwarding
suggestion.rationale: Article states SSRF 'could allow appliance to make requests to unintended location' — implies appliance initiates unexpected outbound/internal requests post-exploitation. No UC to detect this behavior.
log_sources: Proxy logs if SMA1000 routes through proxy
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound traffic from SonicWall SMA1000 appliances. Alert on anomalous internal IP targeting (RFC1918 ranges), localhost requests (127.0.0.1, ::1), or requests to administrative interfaces (port 22, 3389, 443 to unexpected internal hosts). SSRF post-exploitation often attempts credential harvesting or service enumeration.

suggestion.title: SonicWall SMA1000 Vulnerability Scan Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch due date (2026-07-17) and 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Pipeline generated zero vulnerability scanning hunts despite this being primary detection path for unpatched SMA1000 instances.
log_sources: Vulnerability management scanner logs (Tenable, Qualys, etc.)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for any SonicWall SMA1000 appliances with CVE-2026-15409 unpatched status. Cross-reference with CMDB for asset owner, location, internet-facing status. Escalate any unpatched internet-facing SMA1000 to priority due to active KEV exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Patterns to SMA1000 Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability is 'remote unauthenticated' — reconnaissance phase likely includes discovery of SMA1000 instances via open ports/management interfaces. No UC to detect scanning/probing of SMA1000 before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SMA1000 appliance access logs for repeated failed authentication attempts from external sources, particularly to known management ports (admin dashboard, API endpoints). Correlation with network scanning patterns (sequential port probing) may indicate active exploitation reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repointing to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' This is the core obfuscation mechanism enabling the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository tag events for deletions followed by creations pointing to commits not reachable from any branch. Flag when a semantic version tag (e.g., v35) suddenly points to a commit with orphan status or unusual commit timestamp.

suggestion.title: External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Runners
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted external domains. Establish baseline of known external dependencies (npm, pip, etc.) and flag connections to new or suspicious hosts during workflow execution.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secrets in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core impact: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs' and 'This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions run logs for patterns matching secret formats (AWS keys, GitHub tokens, database credentials). Correlate with secret rotation events and flag logs containing unencrypted credentials older than expected secret lifetime. Track public vs. private repo exposure.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Write Access to GitHub Action Repository
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit.' Unknown attribution method, but the enabling factor for all downstream attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new write-permission grants on public/popular GitHub Actions repositories. Flag commits to Action repos from contributors without prior merge history. Alert on sudden code pushes outside normal development windows or from unusual geographic/IP origins.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain: Popular GitHub Action Sudden Version Drift

suggestion.title: Orphaned Git Commit Access in CI/CD Execution

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and alert when GitHub Actions workflows check out or execute commits via hash that do not exist on any branch (main, develop, release/*). Flag git operations referencing direct commit SHAs instead of branch/tag refs in third-party Actions.
