suggestion.title: Unauthorized Mass Device Purge / Reset (KNX Impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could purge all devices without additional security options enabled'; this is the concrete impact. Detect unexpected batch device state resets or data wipes across KNX infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX gateway logs and protocol captures for group/broadcast commands triggering device memory clear or reset operations. Alert on unexplained mass device state transitions. Correlate with failed device heartbeats or management interface access anomalies.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Compromise or Unauthorized Device Lock
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'could set a BCU key to lock the device'; BCU (Backbone Coupler Unit) key write is device credential compromise and lock-out. Detect unauthorized BCU key manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KNX protocol frames writing to BCU key material or triggering device-lock operations. Alert on unexpected changes to device security state. Correlate with failed downstream authentication attempts on locked devices.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Standard CISA KEV baseline control; federal patch due 2026-07-29. Mandatory vulnerability scan detection and asset tracking for unpatched KNX Connection Authorization Option 1 instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2023-4346 against known KNX Association product instances. Alert on any unpatched or unknown-version devices. Track remediation status against federal due date of 2026-07-29.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and references canonical template with this CVE as the substitution target. Zero use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all systems detected as vulnerable to CVE-2023-4346 (KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1) in vulnerability scanners. Prioritize exposed KNX devices on internet-facing or untrusted network segments given CISA KEV status (active exploitation).

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Service Reconnaissance / Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires discovering KNX installations first. Article describes 'purge all devices' implying network enumeration phase. No reconnaissance detection included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or service enumeration targeting known KNX protocol ports. Correlate failed KNX service discovery attempts followed by successful connections or authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Device Configuration / BCU Key Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'set a BCU key to lock the device' and 'purge all devices without additional security options.' Exploitation phase completely absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized BCU key writes, device lockout/purge commands from unauthenticated or out-of-band sources, and bulk configuration resets on KNX devices.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Inventory Gap / Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation; T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) flags exposed assets. Article calls for 'quick check across your fleet.' No asset-exposure baseline generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all KNX devices accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with CVE-2023-4346 scanner results. Escalate any internet-exposed KNX installations for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Asset Exposure — Unauthenticated Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploit applies to 'public-facing applications' and implies network exposure (T1190 context). Phrase: 'exploit public-facing application' in MITRE guidance; also 'federal civilian agencies required to remediate' implies active scans/exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify KNX devices (port/service fingerprints) or KNX protocol traffic accessible from untrusted networks. Alert on inbound connections to KNX control services (typically TCP/3671 or UDP) from external subnets or internet-routable IPs.

suggestion.title: KNX Bulk Device Purge / Reset Events
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'purge all devices'. This is a system-wide manipulation action that would generate device deletion/wipe logs if captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk deletion or reset of KNX devices within a short time window. Look for API/management interface calls that delete multiple device objects, or firmware reset commands issued to multiple devices consecutively. Baseline: normal maintenance typically affects 1–3 devices; anomaly threshold >10 devices in 5 min.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Lock / Modification Events
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'set a BCU key to lock the device' as direct impact. BCU (Board Control Unit) key modification is a privileged action that should be audit-logged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on attempts to read, modify, or lock BCU keys on KNX devices, especially when triggered by non-administrative or unexpected accounts. Flag any BCU key changes that do not correlate with scheduled maintenance or approved change requests.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Anomaly — Overly Restrictive Mechanism Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability class: 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'. Attacker can exploit this to trigger mass lockouts. Phrase: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusually high rates of account lockout events on KNX control systems, especially if lockouts affect all or most accounts in a short window. Correlate with failed authentication attempts; if lockout rate is disproportionate to failed logins, suspect exploitation of the lockout vulnerability.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 KNX Device Purge Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled.' No detection hypothesis exists for bulk device removal or state-zeroing events in KNX environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX network for sudden mass device state changes, bulk device removal commands, or configuration resets. Correlate with failed or bypassed authentication lockout events. KNX protocol analyzers should flag unauthorized purge commands on Option 1 deployments.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 BCU Key Lock Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—specific cryptographic/configuration manipulation. No detection for BCU (Building Controller Unit) key state changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected BCU key modifications, re-keying operations, or lock-state transitions. Monitor for commands that manipulate Building Controller Unit security parameters outside change-management windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 KNX Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'T1190 — Exploit Public-Facing Application (KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets).' Standard exposure hunt template referenced but no use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for KNX devices exposed on public/untrusted networks (ports 3671/UDP, 3672/TCP typical). Cross-reference inventory against CVE-2023-4346 product list. Correlate scanner findings with firewall logs for ingress attempts to KNX services.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Unauthorized Access via Lockout Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—suggests attacker can bypass or circumvent the lockout protection entirely. No detection for lockout-mechanism abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid authentication attempts following account lockout (should be blocked), successful authentications during lockout window, or lockout-mechanism disablement commands. Monitor for Option 1 deployments where lockout protections are absent or misconfigured.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'CVE-2023-4346' as the vulnerability identifier. Standard asset-exposure hunt template should fire for any vulnerability scanner detecting this CVE on KNX devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for vulnerability scan results or asset inventory updates identifying CVE-2023-4346 on KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 devices. Alert on any detection in federated vuln management systems.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Mass Purge / Bulk Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can purge all devices without additional security options enabled.' This implies programmatic bulk deletion capability; abnormal mass device removal should trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX device management APIs and logs for bulk device deletion or purge commands, especially those that affect 5+ devices in a short time window or without corresponding change tickets. Baseline normal device lifecycle events and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Modification Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'can set a BCU key to lock the device.' BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key changes should be rare and auditable; unauthorized modifications indicate compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification of BCU cryptographic keys or authorization credentials on KNX devices, particularly bulk changes or changes originating from non-administrative IPs. Correlate with failed authentication attempts preceding key changes.

suggestion.title: KNX Authorization Option Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly an 'Account Lockout Mechanism' bypass. Exploit attempts would manifest as circumvention of normal authorization or brute-force patterns against KNX authentication endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for repeated failed authentication attempts against KNX devices that don't result in expected account lockout, or successful authentications immediately after excessive failed attempts. Track authorization option configuration changes.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Mass Lockout Events
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker can 'lock the device' via BCU key manipulation. Simultaneous device locking or access denial across fleet segments suggests exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for correlated device unavailability or lock status events affecting multiple KNX devices in a short timeframe. Cross-reference with administrative actions; unexplained fleet-wide lockouts warrant immediate investigation.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Authentication Bypass / Device Purge
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could purge all devices without additional security options enabled'—direct exploitation outcome requiring hunt coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol connections for unauthorized device purge commands or mass device state changes. Look for burst of device removal/reset events from single source or account within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could set a BCU key to lock the device'—specific technical indicator of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on KNX Bus Coupling Unit (BCU) key changes from unauthorized sources or outside change-control windows. Flag any BCU key lock operations.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Exploit Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—suggests exploitation path via authorization bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt KNX protocol traffic for repeated failed authentication attempts followed by device state changes. Look for connection patterns that exploit the lockout mechanism bypass.

suggestion.title: Exposed KNX Protocol Interface Access from Internet
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates 'observed exploited in the wild'—KNX management interfaces must be inventory'd for exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed KNX protocol ports (typically UDP 3671). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2023-4346. Flag any external-to-internal connections to KNX devices.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV: Vulnerability Scan Match CVE-2023-4346
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2023-4346; pipeline extracted no IOCs at all.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner matches for CVE-2023-4346 in asset inventory. Cross-reference with patch deployment logs to identify systems still unpatched beyond federal due date (2026-07-29). High fidelity given active exploitation status in KEV.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Purge or Access Removal Events
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an attacker to purge all devices without additional security options enabled'—direct impact indicator with no corresponding detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol logs for bulk device purge commands, mass device removal operations, or unauthorized device list wipes. Correlate with BCU key modification events. Baseline normal device lifecycle operations to filter authorized administrative purges.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Modification or Lock Events
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'set a BCU key to lock the device' as a direct attack outcome—device lockout is a measurable IOC requiring dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on BCU (Backup Control Unit) key modifications, especially unauthorized key writes or key lockouts that prevent legitimate access. Flag rapid sequences of key modifications across multiple devices as potential mass compromise.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing KNX System Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: T1190 mapping requires exposed assets; article references T1190 ('Exploit Public-Facing Application') but no asset-exposure hunt was generated despite template reference in source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Sweep for KNX systems exposed to internet/DMZ using Shodan, Censys, or internal port scans (common KNX ports: 3671/UDP, 3671/TCP). Cross-reference exposed systems against patch status. Federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-29.

suggestion.title: Authorization Bypass via Account Lockout Mechanism Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'Overly Restrictive Account Lockout Mechanism' as the vulnerability vector—suggests attacker can abuse lockout logic to gain unauthorized access or purge protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal account lockout patterns: rapid repeated lockouts of privileged accounts, lockouts followed immediately by administrative actions, or lockout events from uncommon source IPs. Attackers may trigger false lockouts to exploit the 'overly restrictive' mechanism.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2023-4346 and is CISA KEV entry meaning active in-the-wild exploitation. Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE substitution; federal remediation due 2026-07-29.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CVE-2023-4346 detections from vulnerability scanners targeting KNX Protocol systems. Prioritize exposed instances; CISA KEV requires federal patch compliance by 2026-07-29. Flag even 'patched' systems due to common patch-lag risk.

suggestion.title: KNX Account Lockout Mechanism Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism' that 'allow[s] an attacker to purge all devices'. Account lockout is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid successive authentication failures or abnormal lockout patterns in KNX systems, followed by elevated-privilege device operations. Flag account lockout events within minutes of device purge or BCU key modification commands from same source.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Purge Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled'. Device purge is the primary destructive impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk reset or purge commands in KNX systems, especially when affecting multiple devices in a single operation. High-fidelity indicator when preceded by account lockout events or originating from network segments outside approved administrative ranges.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Manipulation and Device Lockdown
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'set a BCU key to lock the device'. BCU (Backend Configuration Unit) key modification represents persistence and denial of service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for attempts to modify Backend Configuration Unit (BCU) keys or authentication credentials in KNX systems. Flag any key-setting operations that result in device state transitions to 'locked' or 'unavailable' status, particularly when unauthorized.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Protocol Source Access
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'exploit public-facing application' pattern, implying network-exposed KNX systems receiving attacker-controlled traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect KNX protocol traffic (typically port 3671 UDP for standard mode) from unexpected external sources or during non-maintenance windows. Flag any successful authentication to KNX devices from IP addresses outside the approved administrative/device subnet.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Device Purge Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled'—mass device deletion from KNX network is a direct impact indicator and should be detectable via protocol/management logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk device removal operations in KNX networks, especially from unauthorized sources or outside maintenance windows. Baseline legitimate device lifecycle events and flag anomalous deletion patterns correlated with connection auth bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized BCU Key Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key state changes are critical device-integrity mutations requiring alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BCU key creation, modification, or deletion events tied to vulnerable Connection Authorization Option 1 implementations. Cross-reference with device lockout incidents and unauthorized access logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Protocol Authorization Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1190 exploitation against 'Connection Authorization Option 1'—protocol-level auth bypass must be detectable at initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect KNX protocol connection attempts with malformed or missing authorization credentials, or connections from unexpected network segments. Flag successful connections to KNX systems that bypass Connection Authorization Option 1 validation.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Mechanism Abuse on KNX
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability exploits 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—abusing this mechanism as a denial/evasion vector requires detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster rapid account lockout events or authentication failures on KNX services. Distinguish malicious lockout flooding from legitimate security events by correlating with successful unauthorized device operations and anomalous BCU key changes.

suggestion.title: Entra ID Passkey Enrollment from Impossible Geolocation or Off-Hours
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake passkey enrollment as attack vector; passkey/authenticator device registration from geographically impossible location, off-hours, or from high-risk IP should be flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Entra ID device enrollment (passkey, authenticator) originates from location inconsistent with user baseline, outside business hours, or from flagged IP reputation. Prioritize if followed by successful sign-in within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: New Passkey-Based Sign-in Immediately After Device Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Attackers enroll fake passkey then immediately use it to compromise M365; correlation of device registration and auth success from same device in narrow window indicates account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful passkey/authenticator device registration with subsequent successful sign-in from the same device within < 15 minutes, especially to sensitive applications (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, Outlook).

suggestion.title: Burst of Failed Entra ID Authentications Followed by Passkey-Based Success
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors often probe valid credentials before obtaining passkeys; pattern of 3+ failed attempts followed by successful passkey auth within 24 hours indicates credential stuffing or account enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts with ≥3 failed sign-in attempts from same or related IP in 2-hour window, followed by successful passkey-based authentication from different device, location, or user agent.

suggestion.title: Authenticator Device Enrollment Without Corresponding MFA Approval Request
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate passkey enrollment triggers approval prompts; silent or spoofed enrollment lacking expected MFA challenge logs suggests attacker-controlled enrollment flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify authenticator device or passkey registrations in Entra ID audit logs that lack corresponding MFA push notification, approval request, or user-interaction events in endpoint telemetry.

suggestion.title: M365 Sign-in with Recently-Enrolled Passkey from New User-Agent
suggestion.rationale: Fake passkey enrolled via phishing or account compromise typically used by attacker on different browser/device; detect sign-ins from new passkey + new user-agent + new IP triplet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful M365 sign-in using passkey enrolled <24 hours prior, where the sign-in originates from never-before-seen user-agent + IP combination for that user.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2023-4346 is in CISA KEV (active exploitation observed). Pipeline generated zero IOCs and no detection rule. Must hunt for vulnerable instances via scanner.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any scan result reporting CVE-2023-4346 in KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 systems. High-priority: CISA KEV entries are already exploited in the wild.

suggestion.title: Exposed KNX Devices — Network Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attack targets exposed KNX devices. T1190 (exploit public-facing app) requires network-accessible KNX systems. No hunt exists to enumerate them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify systems running KNX protocol services (typically port 3671 UDP/TCP, or vendor-specific). Cross-reference with asset inventory; flag any unauthenticated or unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Purge / BCU Lock Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled' and 'set a BCU key to lock the device.' These are the actual exploit impact — must hunt for abnormal device-state modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX devices and controllers for unexpected purge operations, BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key modifications, or authorization resets. Correlate with failed login/bypass attempts on the same device within preceding 1h.

suggestion.title: KNX Connection Authorization Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is in 'Connection Authorization Option 1' — the authorization mechanism itself is flawed. Hunt for successful or failed bypass sequences in KNX protocol logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed KNX connection attempts followed by immediate successful commands from same source, suggesting authorization bypass. Flag repeated 'Option 1' connection failures against the same device.

suggestion.title: KNX Configuration Changes Post-Patch
suggestion.rationale: Federal due-date is 2026-07-29. Post-patch, unexpected configuration changes (BCU keys, device lockout states, purge status) indicate either delayed exploitation or compromise before patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX device configuration audits for unauthorized changes to BCU keys, authorization policies, or device-enable/disable states during and after patch windows. Baseline expected admin changes.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Exposure and Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and template reference; no UCs generated. 'CVE-2023-4346' must be tracked against exposed KNX devices in vulnerability scan and CMDB.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when KNX Association KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 devices appear in internet-facing scans or lack current patches. Query CMDB for unpatched KNX installations; baseline expected device count and flag new/unknown instances. Correlate with Shodan/Censys for external exposure.

suggestion.title: KNX Account Lockout Mechanism Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability description: 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism' — implies authentication testing or enumeration. No UCs captured the account-layer abuse vector cited in the CVE description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or repeated failed authentication attempts against KNX devices that trigger the overly-restrictive lockout (may lock legitimate accounts permanently). Alert on anomalous lockout event clustering or accounts locked for extended periods without unlock events. Correlate with failed login sources to detect brute-force or enumeration attempts.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Purge and BCU Key Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled and set a BCU key to lock the device.' No UCs for device wipe or key/credential modification detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX device logs for purge/erase commands, BCU key creation/modification, or device lock state changes. Alert on bulk device purge operations or unauthorized key manipulation. Establish baseline for legitimate key rotation and escalate deviations.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Anomalies and Unauthorized Device Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of 'Connection Authorization Option 1' flaw requires protocol-level access; no detection for malformed or unauthorized KNX protocol frames or device discovery scans.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Capture and decode KNX protocol traffic (KNX/TP, KNX/IP); alert on unauthorized connection attempts, invalid authorization credentials, or scanner-like probing (multiple failed connection option negotiations). Establish baseline for legitimate device discovery from trusted subnets.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV CVE-2023-4346 Patch Compliance Deadline
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries mandate federal remediation by due date (2026-07-29 per article). No use case for deadline tracking or compliance reporting generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and vulnerability scan systems for CVE-2023-4346 across all KNX installations. Generate compliance report showing remediation status by deadline (2026-07-29). Alert on any KNX devices still unpatched within 14 days of due date.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 KNX Device Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2023-4346' as the vulnerability identifier and recommends standard asset-exposure hunts. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KNX Association KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 installations in vulnerability scanner outputs. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed instances. Filter for versions prior to the vendor patch release.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Device Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker capability to 'set a BCU key to lock the device' — this is a configuration change that must be monitored. No use case addresses this post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX bus traffic and device logs for unexpected BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key modifications or device lockout events. Alert on configuration commands originating from unauthorized sources or anomalous timings.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Purge/Reset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled' — mass device reset is a destructive impact indicator requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect simultaneous or rapid sequential reset/purge commands across multiple KNX devices in a single facility. Establish baselines for legitimate maintenance windows and alert on anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: KNX Network Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: KEV designation means active exploitation against public-facing instances. Pipeline did not suggest network discovery or exposure-detection for KNX devices per article's implied attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external-facing network segments for open KNX ports (typically UDP 3671). Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify unanticipated KNX device exposure on the internet-routable side of firewalls.

suggestion.title: KNX Connection Authorization Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is rooted in 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism' — attackers exploit this to bypass authorization. Article does not name specific attack method, but lockout bypass is the exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated failed authentication attempts against KNX devices followed by successful access or configuration changes. Watch for patterns consistent with account lockout exhaustion or authorization bypass.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: KNX Protocol Vulnerable Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' against CVE-2023-4346; template invocation suggests this should auto-generate. Pipeline did not output it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for vulnerability scanner matches against CVE-2023-4346 affecting KNX Protocol Connection Authorization products. Filter for unpatched or end-of-life versions. High-value if correlated with network-facing device IPs (port 13671 typical for KNX).

suggestion.title: Rapid Account Lockout on KNX Devices
suggestion.rationale: Core exploit mechanism: 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism vulnerability' + 'set BCU key to lock device'—attacker abuses lockout policy to lock out legitimate users and gain control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed authentication attempts against KNX devices within short time window (< 5 min), followed by account lockout or BCU key modification events. Look for auth failures from single source or credential spray patterns.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Configuration / State Destruction
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices' and 'set BCU key to lock the device'—indicates configuration wipe or device reset capabilities post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on KNX device reset, factory-reset, or configuration purge commands from non-administrative sources. Monitor for BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key lock/unlock operations outside maintenance windows. High severity if affecting critical infrastructure KNX deployments.

suggestion.title: KNX Network Lateral Movement Post-Initial Compromise
suggestion.rationale: After exploiting one device via account lockout bypass (T1190), attacker likely pivots to adjacent KNX bus members; article does not explicitly address KNX-to-KNX lateral movement but implied by 'purge ALL devices' capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal KNX telegram traffic from a single compromised device to multiple peer devices in rapid succession. Look for unicast frames from non-hub sources, protocol fuzzing, or replay of known administrative commands.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 vs CVE-2024-4885 Reconciliation
suggestion.rationale: Article title references CVE-2024-4885 (Progress WhatsUp Gold) but full body consistently describes CVE-2023-4346 (KNX). Mismatch indicates either transcription error or multi-CVE incident. Pipeline did not flag or reconcile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If both CVEs are in scope, perform separate hunts for each product family. If only one is true, correct the record immediately. Verify which product(s) your organization actually operates before over-allocating remediation effort.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — CVE-2023-4346 Unpatched KNX Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [..._TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE: CVE-2023-4346'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite explicit templating instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and patch systems for KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 instances lacking CVE-2023-4346 remediation. Cross-reference against network inventory to surface exposed KNX infrastructure. Federal patch due-date 2026-07-29 provides compliance baseline for asset owners.

suggestion.title: KNX Authorization Mechanism Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker to purge all devices without additional security options enabled' and 'set a BCU key to lock the device' — indicating direct exploitation of the authorization layer. No UC for exploitation attempt detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed KNX connection-authorization requests, repeated authentication failures targeting Building Control Unit (BCU), or anomalous option-1 configuration changes. Baseline normal KNX traffic first — low-volume protocol on most networks, high signal-to-noise if not tuned correctly.

suggestion.title: KNX Bulk Device Lockdown or Purge Command
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled' — explicit impact indicator. Pipeline missed this control-plane attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk device operations (purge-all, factory-reset) lacking corresponding maintenance tickets or approved changes. Flag unauthorized account lockout events in KNX systems, especially from non-admin accounts or anomalous source IPs. Correlate with failed authentication spikes.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Unauthorized Modification or Reset
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'set a BCU key to lock the device' — credential/key management indicator specific to KNX impact phase. No UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BCU key creation, modification, or emergency-reset events outside maintenance windows. Correlate key changes with system administrator login logs; unexpected resets should trigger escalation as potential persistence mechanism post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as baseline. KNX/IP services (UDP/TCP 3671) on external-facing segments are the attack surface. Phrase 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled' establishes attacker must reach KNX management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify KNX/IP services (UDP/TCP 3671) on untrusted network boundaries. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner data for KNX Association products against observed service versions. Enumerate device lists from exposed KNX management consoles.

suggestion.title: Bulk KNX Device Purge or Reset Operations
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation objective stated explicitly: 'purge all devices'. Attack action is mass device removal/reset. Article provides direct evidence of impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX engineering tools and management APIs for bulk device removal, factory reset, or purge commands. Flag device list resets that occur outside maintenance windows or from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with network reconnaissance events.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Substitution or Lock Activation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker capability to 'set a BCU key to lock the device' establishes direct key/credential manipulation. This is post-compromise persistence and device lockout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key change operations in device logs and ETS audit trails. Flag unauthorized commissioning key updates, particularly those originating from non-standard management hosts or outside scheduled maintenance.

suggestion.title: KNX Network Reconnaissance and Device Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover device topology before mass purge. Phrase 'purge all devices' implies prior enumeration of target scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect KNX-specific scanning: repeated queries to group addresses, ETS tool activation on unexpected hosts, port scans targeting KNX broadcast/management ports (3671, 54100), or unusual frequency of KNX/IP describe requests.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Exposure Hunt (CVE-2023-4346)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' templates apply; pipeline generated zero UCs despite this direct instruction and T1190 mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scans for CVE-2023-4346 findings. Prioritize KNX devices exposed on internet-routable interfaces. Cross-check patch status against CISA due date (2026-07-29) for remediation tracking.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Purge Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled'—this is a direct operational impact indicator; pipeline omitted behavioral hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX environments for bulk device deletion or purge commands. Alert on mass device removal events, especially from untrusted or unexpected administrative sources.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Lock Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions attacker can 'set a BCU key to lock the device'; this operational impact requires detection rule but pipeline omitted it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BCU key lock commands in KNX protocol logs. Alert on unexpected key configuration changes or lock operations from non-administrative IP ranges or user accounts.

suggestion.title: Authorization Bypass Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is specifically an 'authorization bypass'—pipeline should hunt for exploitation attempts against KNX authorization layers, not just exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search KNX device logs for failed or anomalous authorization requests, repeated authentication attempts, or protocol-level bypass attempts. Correlate against known exploit signatures for CVE-2023-4346.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV CVE-2023-4346 Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly marks this as 'currently being exploited' (CISA KEV definition). Must query asset inventory and public scan data for KNX Connection Authorization Option 1 deployments. Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure UC despite the template being referenced in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB and Shodan/Censys for KNX protocol instances and vulnerable product versions. Flag any exposed KNX devices not patched to dates after federal due-date 2026-07-29. Correlate with internal vulnerability scans showing CVE-2023-4346.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Authorization Bypass — CVE-2023-4346
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core exploitation: 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism vulnerability that could allow an attacker to purge all devices without additional security options enabled.' This is the initial-access/execution vector. Pipeline failed to map it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol traffic for abnormal authentication attempts, rapid account lockout cycles, or authorization bypass patterns. Flag credential reuse or privilege escalation in KNX management interfaces. Correlate with vulnerable firmware versions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Device Purge Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker capability: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled.' This is explicit impact behavior and should trigger post-exploitation hunting rules. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt KNX management logs for bulk device deletion, reset, or wipe operations. Flag mass device state changes initiated by unauthorized accounts or outside change-control windows. Correlate timing with CVE-2023-4346 exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Locking — Persistence / DoS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'set a BCU key to lock the device.' This is both persistence (device lockout prevents legitimate access) and impact (denial-of-service). Pipeline categorized neither.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX device management logs for BCU key creation, modification, or lock-setting events initiated by non-admin accounts or from non-trusted IPs. Flag key-locking operations preceded by failed authentication bursts or exploit attempts on the same device.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers npm supply chain attacks; standard attack pattern is malicious post-install hooks. Article meta: 'wormable malware, CI/CD persistence'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install execution for spawning unexpected child processes (curl, wget, bash) immediately after node_modules extraction. Flag packages with obfuscated install scripts or scripts that modify .git, .npmrc, or CI configuration files.

suggestion.title: npm Worm Propagation via Package.json Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions wormable malware and multi-stage attacks. Worms propagate by modifying dependency lists in projects they compromise, then re-publishing modified packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification of package.json or package-lock.json followed by npm publish commands within the same execution context, especially if the modified entries reference newly-created or recently-registered packages.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Credential Theft via npm Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically cites 'CI/CD persistence' as a tactic. Malicious npm packages exfiltrate CI secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN) during build.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install or build processes reading environment variables prefixed with sensitive key names (TOKEN, SECRET, KEY, CREDENTIAL) and transmitting them via outbound HTTP(S) or DNS queries.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload in npm Package Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'obfuscation, payload' explicitly. Malicious npm packages embed base64/hex-encoded malicious code or download secondary payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag node_modules packages containing base64-encoded strings >512 bytes that decode to shell commands or JavaScript eval() calls. Alert on npm processes initiating outbound connections to non-standard registries or raw GitHub URLs.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Impersonation (Typosquatting)
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use package name confusion. Article domain (paloaltonetworks) and 'npm packages' keyword indicate package confusion is a vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry queries for typo-variants of popular packages (lodash → lodahs, react → reac-t). Flag installations from newly-created packages with zero version history and install scripts matching obfuscation signatures.

suggestion.title: IoT Device Anomalous Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses TuxBot v3 as an IoT botnet — implies code execution on constrained devices. Pipeline failed to propose detection for unexpected process spawning or script execution on resource-limited IoT platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation on IoT devices (identified by device type/OS) where parent process is non-standard or execution originates from network-accessible service. Compare against baseline of legitimate firmware/vendor processes to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Suspicious C2 Traffic from IoT Subnet
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes botnet — requires command & control communication. No UC proposed despite this being central to botnet operations and most reliable detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IoT device subnets for connections to unexpected external IPs, domains with newly-registered registration dates, or suspicious DNS resolution patterns (fast-flux, homograph, high-entropy subdomains). Correlate with threat feeds for known TuxBot C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Firmware or Boot Persistence on IoT Devices
suggestion.rationale: IoT botnets typically achieve persistence through firmware modification — article title mentions 'evolution' implying upgraded capabilities. No detection proposed for persistent mechanisms specific to IoT architecture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected changes to device firmware, bootloader, or configuration files. Compare current firmware hashes against device inventory baseline and authorized update catalogs. Flag devices reporting unexpected boot parameters or init scripts.

suggestion.title: Public IoT Service Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article references IoT botnet evolution; botnets propagate via public-facing vulnerabilities. Pipeline missed initial access detection despite being critical for early containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repeated failed login attempts or exploit payloads (SQL injection, command injection, buffer overflow patterns) targeting IoT management interfaces (typical ports: 8080, 443, 22 on IoT). Correlate with public CVE advisories for TuxBot target devices.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Resource Consumption on Resource-Constrained Devices
suggestion.rationale: IoT devices typically have limited CPU/memory; botnet activities (cryptomining, DDoS, scanning) cause detectable spikes. Article mentions TuxBot evolution but pipeline proposed no resource-monitoring detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained high CPU or memory utilization (>70%) on IoT devices with no corresponding legitimate process activity. Flag sustained network bandwidth usage inconsistent with device function (e.g., surveillance camera consuming 50% upload bandwidth). Use device-type baselines to avoid false positives.

suggestion.title: LLM-Generated Malware Artifacts Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly highlights 'LLM-assisted development' as distinguishing feature — this suggests code obfuscation, uncommon patterns, or telemetry signatures. Pipeline ignored this novel aspect entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag binaries with unusual code patterns (high entropy sections, statistical anomalies in instruction sequences, or variable naming patterns inconsistent with human reverse-engineering). Cross-reference with LLM-generated malware signatures if available from threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Phishing form injection via XSS into install.php response
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'credential-phishing form injection' via form-action bypass. Article: 'The CSP is missing a form-action directive, allowing exploitation via credential-phishing form injection.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses from admin/install.php containing injected <form> tags with action attributes pointing to external domains or unusual POST handlers. Look for responses where query-string parameters are reflected directly into <form action=...> attributes, especially with method=POST or targets to credential-harvesting infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Meta-refresh / open-redirect injection in admin/install.php
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions explicit attack primitive: 'meta open redirects' enabled by missing form-action CSP directive. Article: 'allowing exploitation via credential-phishing form injection and <meta> open redirects.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect <meta> tags with http-equiv or refresh attributes in responses from /admin/install.php, especially when the content attribute points to external domain (indicator of redirect injection). Match against query parameters reflected into meta tags.

suggestion.title: CSP form-action directive absence detection on admin install script
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies the root cause: 'CSP is missing a form-action directive'. Detection of this misconfiguration enables proactive remediation. Article: 'A Content Security Policy (script-src 'self') prevents inline JavaScript execution, but the CSP is missing a form-action directive...'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response headers for Content-Security-Policy on /admin/install.php. Alert when CSP is present but missing form-action directive or form-action is set to 'self'/'none'. Absence of CSP entirely on install script is highest-risk indicator.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated probe for install.php on production endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes installation script should never be accessible post-deployment: 'install.php should be removed or restricted'. Repeated successful HTTP 200 access by unauthenticated user indicates either misconfiguration or reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated HTTP GET requests to /admin/install.php, /install.php, or similar installer endpoints with HTTP 200 response. Prioritize when requests originate from external IP or show progressive payload testing (repeated requests with different query parameters).

suggestion.title: XSS payload reflection in print_test_result() output
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerable function by name: 'User-supplied parameters are echoed into HTML without escaping via print_test_result()'. Direct detection of this function's output catching attacker-controlled input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses from install.php containing unescaped reflections of query parameters, particularly those matching known XSS payload patterns: script tags, event handlers (onerror, onload), HTML meta tags, or form-action injections. WAF signatures should match patterns seen in UC_8_5 (form, meta, http-equiv, onerror, onload).

suggestion.title: MantisBT self-registration followed by SOAP API replay from same source
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'self-registration is enabled' on default installs and recommends hunt UC_10_2 for 'self-registration followed by SOAP API replay from same source IP.' Pipeline failed to extract this existing recommended hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on source IPs that hit signup.php followed by mantisconnect.php (SOAP endpoint) within a short window, indicating account creation then immediate API exploitation. Look for rapid signup-to-SOAP patterns suggesting automation.

suggestion.title: High-volume SOAP endpoint POST requests (mass enumeration/exfiltration)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends UC_10_3 for 'SOAP endpoint high-volume request burst' detecting mass data exfiltration, explicitly noting this as a phase:actions indicator for CVE-2026-47156 at Medium confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal SOAP query volume per source IP. Flag sources making >100 POST requests to mantisconnect.php in 10-minute windows, with particular attention to large response bytes. Timing correlation with SOAP auth events strengthens signal.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation: SOAP-authenticated access to admin account functions
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can authenticate as any other user (knowing their username), including the administrator' — this is privilege escalation but no detection covers the post-auth admin activity. Missing lateral movement detection after the bypass succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful SOAP auth via reused cookie, monitor for operations performed under admin context (user_id=1 or admin flag in SOAP logs). Correlate SOAP login_string reuse events with downstream admin-level operations (config changes, user deletion, role modification). Flag if admin functions called from non-administrative source IPs.

suggestion.title: SOAP API session cookie exfiltration (cookie value reuse across distinct sources)
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'Any user knowing any valid cookie_string can authenticate as any other user.' No detection suggested for the session-cookie exfiltration or cross-source reuse pattern. Article mentions T1539 (Steal Web Session Cookie) but no hunt covers detecting that cookie in use from unexpected source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all SOAP login_string values (or hash them). Detect when same session cookie is used from multiple distinct source IPs within a time window, or same cookie reappears hours/days later from different geography — indicates exfiltration and reuse.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Redirection to Orphaned Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' This is defense evasion: using legitimate-looking version identifiers (v35) to obscure malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git tag creation or movement that points to commits orphaned from all branches, or tag reassignments that differ from commit lineage expectations. Monitor for version tags (v\d+) suddenly referencing orphaned commits in public-facing repositories with high downstream dependency counts.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Public Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' as a key enabling factor. Orphaned commits are abnormal and warrant alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when commits are created but never merged to any branch (remain unreachable from main/release branches). Cross-reference with tag creation to detect orphaned commits immediately claimed by release tags. High signal in repositories with CI/CD dependency.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Leaked to Plaintext in CI/CD Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Article describes deliberate secret exposure in public logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions logs for patterns matching AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, private keys, or other secret prefixes in plaintext. Correlate with workflow changes that modified secret handling or debug/echo statements. Flag any secrets appearing in public logs (world-readable repos).

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Calls from GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This was the detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from GitHub Actions runners to non-standard ports or suspicious domains. Baseline expected dependencies (package repos, S3, etc.) and alert on deviations. Flag runners fetching code from untrusted sources or using obfuscated domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Commit to High-Dependency Public Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Any commit to such repos should undergo scrutiny for code changes affecting CI/CD or secret handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For repositories with >1000 dependent repos (detected via GitHub API), alert on commits that modify secret-handling code, GitHub Actions workflow files, or add network calls. Require high-confidence authorship verification and correlate with push access provisioning.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Modification Affecting Secret Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code that 'caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext.' This requires modifying how secrets are handled in workflow YAML or action code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect changes to GitHub Actions workflows or action code that remove secret masking, add echo/debug statements outputting secret environment variables, or disable log obfuscation. Flag commits adding `::set-output` or `::debug` statements that reference secret contexts.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Mass Purge Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an attacker to purge all devices without additional security options enabled'—explicit impact capability requiring detection. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX network for bulk reset/purge commands to multiple devices within short timeframe. Baseline normal purge operations and alert on anomalous patterns. Cross-reference target device IPs against asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized BCU Key Lock Operation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker capability to 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—specific post-exploitation impact activity. Pipeline generated zero use cases for device lock patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on BCU key modification events from unexpected sources or at irregular times. Monitor for mass BCU lock operations. Track authorization failures preceding successful locks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerable Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries are in-the-wild exploited vulnerabilities requiring immediate asset hunting. Article identifies vulnerable product with federal remediation deadline 2026-07-29. Pipeline returned empty IOC set—failed to extract CVE as primary search indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2023-4346. Cross-reference asset inventory for 'KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1' devices. Flag instances on external-facing segments or lacking compensating controls.

suggestion.title: KNX Authentication Bypass via Lockout Mechanism Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—the lockout logic itself is weaponized. Devices without 'additional security options' are vulnerable. Article implies credential/access-control attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX devices for rapid failed authentication attempts followed by unexpected privilege gain or device control. Flag lockout logic anomalies. Alert on authorization state changes post-lockout.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Inventory — CVE-2023-4346
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'purge all devices' — detection starts with knowing what KNX assets exist. Article mentions 'KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1' and 'BCU key' which are KNX-specific identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify KNX devices on the network via EDS (Electronic Device Specification) announcements, UDP port 3671, or IEC 101/104 protocol signatures. Baseline known-good KNX devices; flag new or unexpected KNX participants.

suggestion.title: KNX Exploitation Attempt — CVE-2023-4346 Protocol Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'Connection Authorization Option 1' — this is a protocol-level vulnerability. Need to detect malformed or unauthorized KNX protocol messages attempting to bypass authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX network traffic for connection attempts lacking proper BCU key challenge-response, unauthorized telegramming, or bypass of the overly-restrictive lockout mechanism. Look for rapid connection attempts or invalid authorization sequences.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Lockout/Purge Detection — CVE-2023-4346 Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'purge all devices' and 'set a BCU key to lock the device.' These are high-confidence impact indicators that warrant detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KNX telegram messages that clear device memory (purge commands), modify BCU keys, or trigger lockout states. Look for batch device resets, loss of device responsiveness in groups, or emergency shutdown commands in KNX logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Scan Results — KNX Asset Remediation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV sets federal patch due-date of 2026-07-29. Need tracking of scan results showing vulnerable KNX devices to measure remediation progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Consume vulnerability scan results (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.) filtered for CVE-2023-4346. Identify KNX devices with 'vulnerable' status, group by risk tier, and alert on devices still unpatched as patch-due-date approaches (2026-07-29).

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Reconnaissance — Pre-Exploitation Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes device-level attacks but does not mention reconnaissance. However, KNX attackers must discover topology and device types before exploitation; missing detection for network scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for KNX broadcast storms, group address scanning, or repeated parameter read requests (GroupValueRead telegrams) against unknown or all group addresses. Baseline normal KNX traffic patterns and alert on anomalies suggesting topology enumeration.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Lockout or Purge Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled and set a BCU key to lock the device.' No detection rule was generated for this core attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for KNX protocol frames indicating device state changes (offline, reset, lockout). Alert on bulk device lockout events or rapid sequence of device purge commands. Correlate with successful authentication to KNX management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Connection Authorization Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Connection Authorization Option 1' as the vulnerable feature, yet pipeline suggests no detection for unauthorized modifications to this access control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to KNX Connection Authorization settings, particularly Option 1 feature toggles or account lockout policy modifications. Flag any disabling or override of security-relevant authorization mechanisms.

suggestion.title: KNX Management Interface Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation must transit a KNX management interface or bus access point; article does not specify path but implies remote or local access to trigger lockout/purge. Pipeline failed to generate access-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed authentication attempts against KNX management interfaces followed by successful login. Detect connections from unexpected source IPs or outside-hours access. Correlate with subsequent device state changes.

suggestion.title: Bulk KNX Device State Synchronization Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'purge all devices' suggests coordinated multi-device impact. Pipeline generated no detection for abnormal bulk-device state transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal patterns in KNX device status changes—rapid simultaneous offline events, synchronized configuration resets, or coordinated firmware/state rollback across multiple devices in the same KNX area.

suggestion.title: HTTP/3 Server Crash via Malformed QUIC Ring Buffer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Unpatched XRING Flaw...Lets Remote Clients Crash HTTP/3 Servers'—direct availability impact from remote unauthenticated request. Pipeline generated zero detection logic for this primary threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected termination of QUIC/HTTP/3 server processes (h3-server, xquic, quiche) with preceding UDP 443 packet anomalies: out-of-order frame offsets, oversized stream-offset fields, or malformed QUIC variable-length integers indicating ring-buffer trigger.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: QUIC/HTTP/3 Server Implementation Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must identify vulnerable XQUIC instances. Detection gap: no rules for Version Negotiation probes, Alt-Svc header enumeration, or TLS certificate fingerprinting targeting HTTP/3 services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated QUIC Version Negotiation (0x6b3343cf) requests to port 443 from single IP, or connection attempts with invalid version bytes followed by rapid reconnection—consistent with capability probing.
