suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to known FortiSandbox endpoints (typical ports 443, 8443, 8000) for anomalous payloads, repeated request patterns, or parameter injection attempts. Flag unauthenticated source IPs attempting exploitation against exposed FortiSandbox instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution Spawned by FortiSandbox Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection' enabling 'unauthorized command execution'—detection of subprocess spawning from FortiSandbox process context is essential for post-exploitation visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation or command invocation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) initiated by FortiSandbox daemon/service processes. Establish baseline of legitimate child processes; flag reconnaissance utilities (whoami, ipconfig, curl, wget) or shell escapes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Asset Exposure Validation (Patch Due 2026-07-19)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes patch-lag risk—'even if scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, one quick check' is needed. Federal due date is 2026-07-19; inventory must validate exposure and patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Cross-reference against scanner output confirming patch status. Identify internet-routable instances lacking patches prior to federal deadline; flag for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Product Banner Disclosure and Version Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Product identification in HTTP headers or login banners (article names 'FortiSandbox' explicitly) enables attacker reconnaissance and pre-staging; should be monitored for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP responses from suspected FortiSandbox instances for product banners, Server header disclosure, or login page metadata leaking Fortinet product/version info. Correlate with CVE-2026-25089 version ranges to identify active reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox Admin/API Endpoints from External IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—requires detection for external HTTP access to known FortiSandbox admin or API ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiSandbox instances (common ports 8000, 8080, 443) from external IPs. Flag requests originating outside your organization's known admin subnets or VPNs. Correlate against asset inventory to identify exposed FortiSandbox instances.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Patterns in HTTP Request Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'—detect payloads containing shell metacharacters, command separators (&&, |, ;, $()), or backticks in query strings and POST bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request payloads (GET/POST parameters, headers) targeting FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection indicators: pipes (|), semicolons (;), backticks (`), command substitution $(), redirection operators (>, >>), logical operators (&&, ||). Flag requests matching regex patterns like `(%7c|%26%26|%3b|`.*`)` in URL-encoded form.

suggestion.title: Process Execution Spawned from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in 'execute unauthorized commands'—detect child processes launched by FortiSandbox service processes with unusual executable paths or command lines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events where parent is a FortiSandbox worker/service process (e.g., java.exe, python.exe spawned from fortisandbox worker) with command lines containing shell interpreters (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh, powershell.exe) or suspicious executables outside expected application directories.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Accessible FortiSandbox Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' and CISA KEV implies active scanning/exploitation—identify FortiSandbox instances reachable from the internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network vulnerability scans and asset management systems to identify FortiSandbox instances with public-facing IP addresses or accessible via external hostnames. Priority: any instance without VPN/IP whitelisting.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Request Patterns to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'—detect statistical anomalies in request volume, user-agent diversity, or parameter cardinality targeting FortiSandbox endpoints from single source IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP traffic to FortiSandbox endpoints; flag deviations: single IP sending >N requests in short window, requests with unusual User-Agent strings or absent User-Agent headers, repeated requests to non-existent endpoints (404 scanning), or requests with extremely long parameter values suggesting payload injection.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attacker' exploiting exposed instances; standard asset-exposure hunt is mandatory to locate vulnerable instances on network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound traffic to FortiSandbox management ports (typically 8080/8443) and correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-25089 patch status. Identify all FortiSandbox variants (OS, Cloud, PaaS) in asset inventory.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Malformed HTTP Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' required for exploitation; pipeline must hunt for anomalous request patterns against FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiSandbox admin endpoints for query parameter injection, header manipulation, oversized payloads, or path traversal sequences consistent with command injection probing.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox RCE Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection vulnerability enables arbitrary code execution; pipeline must detect unexpected child processes spawned from FortiSandbox service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, system utilities) spawned from FortiSandbox service accounts or parent processes. Correlate with anomalous HTTP requests to sandbox endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scan Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs re-scanning fleet even if prior scans showed compliance; enable rapid CVE-based threat hunt across asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system for all assets running affected FortiSandbox versions or flagged for CVE-2026-25089. Correlate with federal patch-due date (2026-07-19) to identify overdue remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Vulnerable Asset Discovery (CVE-2026-25089)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected products (Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS) with federal due date 2026-07-19. Pipeline generated zero asset-enumeration use case despite CISA KEV status mandating urgent patch compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management systems and asset inventories for Fortinet FortiSandbox instances running pre-patch versions. Cross-reference network exposure scans (Shodan/Censys) to identify internet-facing deployments. Triage by federal due date for remediation tracking.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP Command Injection Payloads to FortiSandbox Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' enabling 'OS command injection'. Pipeline zero detection rules for network-layer payload inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (/api/*, /cgi-bin/*, /admin/*) for OS command metacharacters and encoded variants: pipe |, semicolon ;, command substitution $()/backticks, logical operators &&/||. Payload inspection with elevated priority on unauthenticated externally-sourced requests.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation injects commands into service context. Article states 'execute unauthorized commands' but pipeline failed to generate execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts (fortisandbox, root/SYSTEM running fortisandbox processes) invoking shell interpreters (cmd.exe, /bin/bash) or system recon utilities (whoami, id, ifconfig, ipconfig). Focus on parent process = web-exposed service.

suggestion.title: Baseline Unauthenticated Access to FortiSandbox Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' — implies missing auth checks. Pipeline missed authentication-bypass as detection anchor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of valid authentication sessions to FortiSandbox web interfaces. Alert on HTTP requests to admin/API endpoints from external IPs lacking valid session tokens or API keys. Spike in 401/403 responses from single external source suggests exploitation probing.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts via HTTP Request Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article characterizes attack as 'specifically crafted' HTTP requests — behavioral detection on request shape/content required. Pipeline generated zero anomaly-based hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Apply WAF rules and IDS signatures for FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 exploitation. Monitor for HTTP parameter pollution, oversized payloads, unusual header combinations, or encoding schemes targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Correlate with successful 200 responses + subsequent process creation from service account.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Command injection grants attacker code execution in FortiSandbox context (often privileged/network-accessible). Pipeline missed post-compromise activity detection despite CISA KEV implying active attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, monitor for network reconnaissance or lateral movement from FortiSandbox host: scanning adjacent subnets, DNS queries to internal hosts, credential dumping attempts (mimikatz, secretsdump), or outbound C2 connections. Establish baseline for FortiSandbox egress traffic.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entry with CVE-2026-25089; scanners targeting this CVE are the direct IOC baseline for any FlexVPN/FortiSandbox asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner match for CVE-2026-25089 against internal FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or FortiSandbox PaaS instances. False positives minimal; presence indicates exposed/at-risk asset.

suggestion.title: HTTP request anomalies to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' to unauthenticated endpoint; WAF/proxy logs should surface malformed or fuzzing-pattern requests to known FortiSandbox API routes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with suspicious payloads (command injection patterns: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes) sent to FortiSandbox API endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /cgi-bin/*). Spike in 400/403 responses from single source may indicate exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: OS command execution from FortiSandbox service account
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection requires execution flow from vulnerable process; article states 'execute unauthorized commands,' implying post-RCE execution via shell spawning from service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent is FortiSandbox process (e.g., fortisandbox, nginx, java running as sandbox service user) spawning shell (cmd.exe, bash, sh, powershell). Filter known maintenance tasks; focus on unexpected spawns with suspicious command lines.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated access logs to FortiSandbox admin/API interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker' can trigger RCE; access logs showing requests without valid auth tokens to known protected endpoints are direct exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiSandbox API or admin interfaces (e.g., /api/*, /admin, /dashboard) that return 200/execution success codes without valid authentication headers (missing/invalid Bearer token, session cookie). Correlate with subsequent command execution.

suggestion.title: Network-based detection of FortiSandbox exploitation signature
suggestion.rationale: IDS/IPS signatures should be tuned for CVE-2026-25089 command injection patterns; network-level detection avoids endpoint log dependency for exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy/verify IDS rule coverage for CVE-2026-25089-specific payloads (command injection in HTTP params); alert on matches from external or untrusted networks to FortiSandbox listening ports (default 80, 443, 8080).

suggestion.title: Reverse DNS/asset lookup for FortiSandbox exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies exploitation against exposed assets; simple asset-discovery hunt to identify any FortiSandbox instances reachable from internet (banners, SSL certs, service fingerprints).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query external scan data (Shodan, Censys, internal reverse-DNS / port-scan logs) for FortiSandbox fingerprints (HTTP Server headers, SSL subject, service banners). Any match = external-facing instance at risk; cross-reference against patch status.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero detection logic for HTTP payloads containing command injection metacharacters targeting FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox service ports (default 8443, 8080) for command injection patterns: backticks, pipe operators, semicolon-separated commands, $() substitution, and &&/|| operators in request URI/parameters/headers. Baseline legitimate API calls and alert on anomalous encoding or payloads.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthorized Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability...execute unauthorized commands.' Pipeline missed detection for processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts outside normal baseline operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FortiSandbox processes (fortisandbox daemon, fsand worker processes) spawn unexpected child processes. Track command-line arguments for reverse shells, data exfiltration commands (curl, wget, nc), or privilege escalation. Exclude known maintenance and update processes.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Exposure Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV exploitation requires externally-accessible FortiSandbox. Article implies public-facing exposure. Pipeline should detect exposed instances at risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and port scanners for FortiSandbox instances reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against patch inventory for unpatched versions. Prioritize any exposed instance running vulnerable versions against CVE-2026-25089 pre-patch baseline.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Patch Compliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-07-19 for CISA KEV entry. Pipeline omitted vulnerability management verification despite CISA enforcing deadline compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiSandbox instances and confirm patch status against CVE-2026-25089. Flag any unpatched instances accessible from external networks as critical risk. Track remediation progress against 2026-07-19 deadline and alert SOC if patch gap remains after cutoff.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Anomalous Outbound Connections
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection RCE could lead to data exfiltration or C2 callbacks. Article does not detail post-exploitation but detection should span potential impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiSandbox outbound traffic (vendor updates, license servers, syslog). Alert on connections to non-whitelisted IPs, dynamic DNS domains, known C2 ranges, or non-standard ports. Correlate with process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: Default credential bruteforce / password spray to pheditor.php
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'There is no mechanism to force a password change on first login' and hardcoded default is 'admin'. Pipeline missed detection for repeated failed auth attempts followed by success, a key signal of credential attacks against known-vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 401 responses to pheditor.php followed within short window by 200/302 success, especially with identical User-Agent or source IP across requests. Correlate with common default credentials (admin:admin) if HTTP basic auth is logged.

suggestion.title: pheditor.php file discovery or presence on web-accessible path
suggestion.rationale: The core issue is that pheditor.php exists with default credentials. Article states it enables 'file upload, and terminal features'—detection should flag the presence of this administrative tool in production, not just exploitation post-discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to pheditor.php (404 → 200 transition indicates new installation), or file-system scans detecting pheditor.php in /var/www, /html, /public_html. High-confidence if detected in web root and admin processes didn't deploy it.

suggestion.title: Pheditor.php source modification or default credential hash replacement
suggestion.rationale: Article notes SHA-512 hash of default password stored at pheditor.php:11. Detection of file modification to pheditor.php or replacement of the hardcoded hash would indicate hardening or post-compromise remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pheditor.php for content changes, checksum mismatches, or source-control commits that modify password hashes. Flag if pheditor.php is rewritten without a documented change control ticket.

suggestion.title: Pheditor file-upload followed by PHP execution from uploaded path
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Pheditor enables 'file upload' feature; pipeline missed pairing file-upload with subsequent execution from the same upload directory, indicating webshell drop and execution in a single attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST/PUT to pheditor upload endpoint with subsequent file creation and process execution from the same upload directory, within seconds. High-confidence if the upload is a .php file followed by sh/bash spawn.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or default-auth access to pheditor.php terminal action
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes no forced password change and hardcoded default—critical UC missing detection of terminal action (T1059.004) invoked without re-authentication or with default credentials, implying compromise without legitimate admin context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests with action=terminal parameter in pheditor.php URLs combined with 'admin' username in query/POST or absence of valid session token. Pair with shell process spawning (UC_3_2) for confirmation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline missed detection for any HTTP traffic reaching FortiSandbox without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to known FortiSandbox instances (port 8080, 8443, or product-specific endpoints) originating from unexpected sources or lacking authentication headers. Baseline normal traffic first; spike detection on request volume or source diversity.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox OS Command Injection Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection' allowing 'execute unauthorized commands.' Pipeline should detect injection payloads in HTTP request bodies (semicolons, pipe operators, backticks, $() syntax).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox for command injection signatures: unencoded shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, ||), command substitution syntax ($(), backticks), or common OS commands (bash, sh, cmd, powershell). Baseline benign API calls first.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Successfully injected commands result in 'unauthorized commands' execution. Detection should capture child processes spawned by FortiSandbox (FSSand, fsagent) with unexpected parents or arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by FortiSandbox services with unexpected command lines (non-service maintenance, reverse shells, file operations outside sandbox dirs). Baseline normal operations; flag any process spawning not in whitelist.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Inventory & Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status and 'federal patch due 2026-07-19' require asset exposure hunt. Article confirms FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS are in scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for open FortiSandbox ports (8080, 8443) and certificate/banner signatures. Cross-reference against patch inventory for CVE-2026-25089 remediation status. Flag any system without evidence of patch deployed by federal due date.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Application Error Logs (Injection Attempts)
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts often leave traces in application logs (malformed requests, injection payloads, parsing errors). Article does not provide log signatures, but 'specifically crafted HTTP' implies detectable anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox application logs for HTTP 400/403 errors, malformed parameter errors, or injection-related exceptions. Spike in errors from single source or time window indicates scanning or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: HTTP requests with OS command injection payloads to FortiSandbox endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—this is the exploit vector and directly detectable in proxy/WAF/firewall logs via payload signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to known FortiSandbox management ports (8080, 8443, 8888) containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, `, $(, ${) or command substitution in query parameters or POST body. High confidence if source IP is external/untrusted and user-agent indicates scanning or scripting.

suggestion.title: Process creation from FortiSandbox application service context
suggestion.rationale: Successful command injection results in arbitrary process execution from the vulnerable service's user account. Article explicitly states 'execute unauthorized commands' which manifests as child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation with parent process = FortiSandbox service (fortisandbox.exe, java running as fortisandbox user) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, curl, wget, or other system utilities that are anomalous for a sandbox appliance.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox appliance exposed on public internet
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires network-accessible endpoint; article's 'public-facing application' phrasing confirms exposure risk. Asset inventory and external scanning can detect unauthorized FortiSandbox exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Shodan/Censys for Fortinet certificate subjects and FortiSandbox HTTP signatures on public IPs. Cross-reference against approved management network ranges; flag any FortiSandbox instance with global routing + open 8080/8443 as T1190 exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Successful HTTP 200 responses on FortiSandbox endpoints from untrusted sources
suggestion.rationale: Command injection attacks typically return HTTP 200 on successful payload execution. Correlating access logs + HTTP status + source reputation can identify active exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP 200 responses on API/admin paths (/api/*, /admin/*, /upload*) originating from external IP addresses, especially if requests contain suspicious parameter values or command strings. Anomalous response times or binary content-type changes can indicate command output exfiltration.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'public-facing application' and recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt'; pipeline generated zero UCs. Exposure is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for external HTTP/HTTPS connectivity to FortiSandbox ports (4003, 8080, 8443) from untrusted networks. Enumerate exposed instances via service fingerprints and correlate with patch inventory to identify vulnerable assets within the 2-day federal remediation window.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'; no HTTP-layer detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints containing shell metacharacters (;|&$()`), command substitution syntax, or encoded command payloads. Unauthenticated requests with suspicious parameters represent exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Child Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Command injection execution culminates in spawned OS processes; article mentions 'unauthorized commands' but pipeline omitted process-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash, or ping spawning as children of FortiSandbox service processes. Establish baseline of legitimate spawning; any deviation is high-fidelity since command injection should not spawn processes under normal operation.

suggestion.title: Spike in 401/403 to FortiSandbox API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation path is unauthenticated; reconnaissance probing and auth-bypass attempts should precede successful command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained spikes in 401/403 responses to /api/*, /upload/, or admin endpoints on FortiSandbox instances. Correlate with successful command execution (200 responses with unusual parameters) to identify exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'CVE-2026-25089 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the core IOC and recommends scanner-based verification; pipeline output contains no IOCs whatsoever.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify that your scanner has CVE-2026-25089 detection enabled and confirm all FortiSandbox instances in scope. Federal remediation deadline is 2026-07-19; correlate scanner results with asset management to identify unpatched systems and prioritize based on exposure level.

suggestion.title: Application Error Spike on FortiSandbox (500/502/503)
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts may trigger application errors or service crashes; sudden error spikes are a behavioral indicator of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal 4xx/5xx response rates for FortiSandbox services. Alert on anomalous spikes, especially 500/502/503 errors, which may indicate exploitation attempts or successful compromise causing service instability.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'unauthenticated attacker' via 'public-facing application' (Cloud/PaaS variants). Initial access requires discovery of exposed FortiSandbox instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory FortiSandbox management interfaces exposed to untrusted networks (port 8443, 8080, 443). Cross-reference against CVE-2026-25089 patch status (due 2026-07-19). Alert on FortiSandbox instances running unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'; detections must identify malicious payloads targeting FortiSandbox HTTP handlers, particularly command injection markers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks), URL encoding abuse, and system command keywords (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell). Flag requests with unusual parameter lengths or encoding patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly allows 'execute unauthorized commands'; detection must capture OS-level process spawning from the vulnerable HTTP service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell/cmd.exe/powershell spawned as child of FortiSandbox HTTP service (httpd, nginx, java). High confidence if parent runs under system/network service account. Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP access logs.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Configuration or Credential File Access
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker harvests credentials from config files; article describes command execution capability enabling lateral movement or persistence setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reads to FortiSandbox credential stores (/etc/forti*, /opt/forti*, config DBs) following evidence of unauthorized command execution. Flag file reads from non-privileged or unexpected process contexts.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Restart or Crash Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Command injection exploitation may corrupt or crash the sandbox service; unusual service restarts correlate with failed or successful attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FortiSandbox service restarts, crashes, or unclean shutdowns. Correlate with HTTP access logs showing anomalous requests in the preceding 5-10 minutes. Baseline service uptime and alert on unexpected restart frequency.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Exposed to Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker can execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—the vulnerability presupposes network reachability without auth enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (ports 80, 443, 8080, 5000) from untrusted networks with no valid session tokens or authentication headers. Alert on successful responses (200/201) or error codes indicating the service is reachable and processing requests without credential validation.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution Following HTTP to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly 'allows unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands'—successful exploitation manifests as process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service processes (sandboxd.exe, or related daemons) with unusual parent-child relationships, especially command-line tools (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) executing within seconds of HTTP requests to the service. Flag commands containing recon keywords (whoami, ipconfig, systeminfo, net user).

suggestion.title: Malformed HTTP Request Payloads to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'—should detect request payloads with command injection syntax before execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox API/UI endpoints for shell metacharacters (|, &&, ;, backticks, $()), base64-encoded payloads with command prefixes, or parameter values containing path traversal sequences. Correlate with HTTP response codes indicating injection attempts were processed.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Instance Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV exploitation requires 'unauthenticated attacker' access—presupposes internet-reachable FortiSandbox instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset exposure hunt: scan for FortiSandbox instances reachable from untrusted ASNs (identify via banner grabbing, SSL cert CN patterns, HTTP headers). Cross-reference against unpatched version inventory. Alert on any instance accessible to internet without WAF/network segmentation.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Data Exfiltration Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Command injection success grants arbitrary execution—attackers would pivot to establish persistence or exfiltrate data via subsequent shell commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections initiated by FortiSandbox child processes to rare/suspicious destinations, reverse shells via common tools (nc, bash -i, powershell -rev), or data staging/compression (tar, zip) followed by exfiltration channels.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active in-the-wild exploitation—need direct signature-based detection for known payload patterns once published by Fortinet or security vendors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests matching CVE-2026-25089 exploitation signatures (when published by Fortinet/ICS-CERT/vendors), Metasploit module indicators, or proof-of-concept payloads. Flag all matches regardless of response code, as reconnaissance activity is threat-relevant.

suggestion.title: HTTP requests to exposed FortiSandbox instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Asset-exposure hunt template explicitly referenced but no UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate your external-facing FortiSandbox instances (prod names, IPs, FQDN patterns). Baseline normal HTTP request volumes and methods. Flag requests with suspicious parameter names, encoded payloads, or anomalously high request rates from single sources to vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: OS command execution post-FortiSandbox ingestion
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' — detection must pair HTTP ingestion with downstream process execution. No UC captured this execution indicator.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for any host tagged 'FortiSandbox' with CVE-2026-25089. Cross-reference with network scans for listening ports (8080, 8443). Confirm absence of vendor security patches via software inventory or package manager logs.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox authentication bypass or unauthenticated session establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker', indicating no auth required. Hunt for HTTP sessions to FortiSandbox endpoints that do not include valid session tokens, API keys, or credentials, yet receive HTTP 200 responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox /api/* or /admin/* endpoints lacking Authorization headers or valid session cookies, yet returning 200/201 status. Correlate with source IPs external to trusted admin subnets.

suggestion.title: Reverse DNS/IP lookup or banner grab for FortiSandbox fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Precursor to exploitation. Article mentions 'specifically crafted HTTP requests', implying attackers must first identify/confirm FortiSandbox presence. Hunt for fingerprinting attempts (banner grabbing, HTTP OPTIONS, User-Agent probing) from external IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests with unusual User-Agents, OPTIONS method, or HEAD requests to FortiSandbox root path from external/untrusted IPs, especially if followed by POST with command injection patterns within minutes.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Exposure Hunt (CVE-2026-25089)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template reference and CVE substitution guidance. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search your vulnerability management system and asset database for FortiSandbox instances running vulnerable versions. Correlate exposed FortiSandbox services (port/HTTP profile) against public-facing asset inventory. The attack surface is any unauthenticated HTTP endpoint—scan recursively for exposed management or API ports.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Command Injection HTTP Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' enable exploitation. Pipeline missed this execution-phase detection despite explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (typical ports: 8080, 8443, 8000) containing OS command injection metacharacters (backticks, `$()`, pipes, semicolons, &&, ||) in POST/GET parameters. Focus on unauthenticated sessions (no auth header or failed auth) combined with shell command syntax (cmd.exe, /bin/sh, powershell, etc.).

suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute unauthorized commands' post-injection. Detection of actual command execution activity on compromised sandbox host is a critical post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FortiSandbox hosts: detect process creation from unusual parents (httpd, tomcat, java processes spawning shell or command interpreter). Flag execution of reconnaissance commands (whoami, id, ipconfig, systemctl, ps) or outbound connections from sandbox process contexts following suspicious HTTP requests.

Flag instances with stale scanner profiles, disabled vulnerability checks, or patches that failed validation. Corroborate with log-based version detection (server headers, version disclosure in HTTP responses).

Flag connection attempts to high-value targets (domain controllers, backup systems, monitoring infrastructure) from the sandbox's network context.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article describes OS command injection leading to unauthorized command execution. The attack executes arbitrary OS commands, which means child processes spawned from FortiSandbox daemon are the smoking gun; pipeline missed this execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FortiSandbox child processes (expect only approved utilities; scripts/shells are anomalous). Alert on spawning of sh, bash, powershell, cmd.exe, perl, python, or wget/curl from FortiSandbox parent. Inspect command-line arguments for data exfiltration, lateral movement, or persistence indicators.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Network Egress (Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker achieves command execution via injection, next step is typically outbound communication. Article phrase 'unauthorized commands' implies attacker is in control; detection should capture C2 beaconing or data exfil from compromised FortiSandbox context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections originating from FortiSandbox process context (unusual for normal operation). Flag DNS queries from the service, unexpected HTTPS/HTTP connections, or beaconing patterns. Correlate timing with web-server logs showing exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Error/Status Code Anomalies (Indicator of Exploitation Failure/Success)
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts and successful command injection may leave traces in FortiSandbox application logs (error codes, exceptions, unusual status transitions). Article notes specific HTTP exploitation mechanism; logs should reflect abnormal behavior during or after attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FortiSandbox service logs for exploit-related error codes, segfaults, or unexpected exception patterns. Look for log entries following HTTP requests with command-injection payloads. Baseline normal error rates and alert on deviations in timing or context.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Privilege Escalation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE may run as the service user; attacker would attempt privilege escalation to persist or widen impact. Article does not explicitly cover post-exploitation, but CISA KEV entries imply forensic hunting for lateral movement or privilege elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege-escalation attempts (sudoedit, CVE-style kernel exploits, process injection) in the timeline following FortiSandbox exploitation. Look for fork/exec calls with elevated privileges, or process migration patterns consistent with token theft or reflective DLL injection.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandate requires all federal agencies (and sensible enterprises) to scan and patch. Pipeline must extract CVE identifier as IOC for cross-reference against vulnerability scanner and asset inventory; this is missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-25089 across FortiSandbox asset inventory (all versions). Correlate scanner results with patch-date metadata. Flag any asset running affected version; cross-correlate with web-server/proxy logs from 2026-07-16 onward to identify potential exploitation window and forensic timeline.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — no use case generated for detecting malicious HTTP payloads targeting FortiSandbox APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox service endpoints for patterns matching command injection syntax (shell metacharacters, backticks, command separators). Baseline legitimate API calls and alert on requests with anomalous payloads from non-expected sources. Correlate with CVE-2026-25089 scanner findings to confirm exposure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection' allowing 'unauthorized commands' — pipeline missed detection for child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts as result of injection exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process execution under FortiSandbox service context (e.g., fortisandbox user/service account). Baseline normal processes and flag deviations, especially shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash) launched from FortiSandbox processes with unusual parent-child chains.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Exposure Hunt (Asset Inventory)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' for CVE-2026-25089 using template approach, but pipeline generated no asset discovery use case despite guidance provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for exposed FortiSandbox service ports/endpoints in your environment using vulnerability scanner data, network flow data, or CDR logs. Cross-reference with patch inventory to identify systems running vulnerable versions (pre-2026-07-19 patches). Prioritize external-facing instances as T1190 exploitation requires public accessibility.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-25089, but no IOC or use case was generated for this primary detection method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CVE-2026-25089 CVE feed into vulnerability management platform. Alert on any detection of Fortinet FortiSandbox or Fortinet FortiSandbox Cloud instances in your asset inventory. Flag as critical priority due to CISA KEV active exploitation status and federal due date 2026-07-19. Cross-reference with patch deployment logs to identify unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Attempts to FortiSandbox APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' exploiting the service — no use case for detecting initial reconnaissance or failed auth patterns from reconnaissance attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox API/web interface logs for patterns of unauthenticated access attempts, parameter fuzzing, or requests with unusual User-Agent strings. Since exploitation is unauthenticated, baseline normal API traffic and alert on sources making requests without valid credentials or suspicious header manipulation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero detection for this vector despite it being the attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox admin endpoints (known ports: 8008, 8443, 443) originating from external IPs without prior authentication context. Correlate with subsequent process creation events on the FortiSandbox host showing shell command execution (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) spawned from HTTP handler processes (e.g., tomcat, nginx).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Child Process Spawning from HTTP Handler
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability explicitly enables 'execute unauthorized commands.' Pipeline missed detection of the execution phase—monitoring for shell processes spawned by FortiSandbox handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiSandbox daemon or web handler process (java, python, nginx, tomcat) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, or /bin/sh as a child process, especially if preceded by inbound HTTP POST requests to non-standard URIs or requests with command-like payloads in headers or body.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Remediation Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-19.' Pipeline omitted the critical compliance and asset-tracking UC tied to the patch deadline and CISA mandate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all Fortinet FortiSandbox (on-prem, Cloud, PaaS) instances in your environment via asset inventory and vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-25089. Cross-reference patch dates against the federal deadline (2026-07-19); flag any unpatched or unconfirmed instances after the deadline for immediate escalation and remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Product Instance Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies three affected products (FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS). Pipeline produced no asset-discovery or enumeration UC to identify exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Fortinet FortiSandbox endpoints accessible from external or untrusted networks via port scanning, DNS discovery (*.forticloud.com, *.fortisandbox.com domains), and cloud provider APIs. Flag any publicly routable or internet-facing admin interfaces (default ports: 8008, 8443) and correlate against a baseline of approved external services.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Payload Patterns to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as the delivery vector. No detection rule was generated to identify the exploitation payloads themselves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for patterns indicative of command injection (shell metacharacters: pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), command substitution patterns, escape sequences) in request headers (User-Agent, Referer, Cookie) or POST body. Flag requests without valid session tokens or authentication headers combined with suspicious payload patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'public-facing' FortiSandbox and is actively exploited by unauthenticated attackers. Pipeline generated no asset-exposure hunt despite referencing template at ../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox instances (CloudProbe, management console, PaaS endpoints) listening on internet-facing ports. Check for CVE-2026-25089 presence in vulnerability scanner output. Cross-reference against patch inventory for systems not yet patched by deadline 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically notes exploitation via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' This HTTP pattern should be a distinct detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for unusual URI patterns, suspicious parameter encoding, or shell metacharacters in request body/headers. CISA KEV entry implies specific attack vectors are actively weaponized.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Execution from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'execute unauthorized commands' via the vulnerability. Pipeline failed to generate command-execution detection despite this being the exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawning from FortiSandbox daemon/service processes (fortisandbox-daemon, sandboxd, etc.) with unexpected parent-child relationships. Look for shell execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) or suspicious command-line arguments originating from FortiSandbox process context.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Injected commands may establish C2 or lateral movement. Article does not specify payload behavior, but command execution primitives warrant network-behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiSandbox network behavior and alert on deviations: new outbound connections to non-Fortinet infrastructure, unusual protocols, or connections to known malicious IP ranges.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Container/Sandbox Escape Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions FortiSandbox Cloud and PaaS variants, implying containerized deployments. OS command injection in containerized contexts may indicate escape attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious syscalls from FortiSandbox container processes (ptrace, mount, namespace creation, cgroup manipulation). Alert on any process attempting to interact with host kernel or escape sandbox boundaries.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-25089 as CISA KEV (actively exploited in wild) and explicitly directs to 'asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution. Pipeline generated zero use cases. Federal patch due 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner logs for Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or FortiSandbox PaaS instances with CVE-2026-25089 or missing patches dated after 2026-07-19. Correlate inventory with external-facing asset database to identify exposed instances requiring immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — direct exploitation pathway with no auth required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web service process associated with FortiSandbox for child process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash). Correlate with HTTP request logs to FortiSandbox endpoints, flagging requests with encoded payloads or shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick). Alert on process lineage: web service → shell command execution.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox External Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes unauthenticated remote exploitation via HTTP — implies internet-facing infrastructure. Standard CISA KEV remediation includes inventory and exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network logs for inbound connections to Fortinet FortiSandbox management/API ports (default 80, 443, 8080, 8443) from untrusted networks. Baseline historical external traffic; flag any FortiSandbox instances receiving internet-routable traffic outside security boundary.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to FortiSandbox Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — establishes HTTP-based initial access without authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox administrative or API endpoints from external networks without corresponding authentication events. Flag request patterns immediately preceding process execution or unusual HTTP status codes.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' — direct implication is arbitrary command execution via child processes spawned from the vulnerable service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service (parent: sandbox.exe or fgsandbox) with suspicious command lines (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh with unusual arguments). Cross-correlate with unauthenticated HTTP access in preceding 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection for CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation indicates active exploitation in the wild. Reconnaissance scans for this CVE should trigger asset-exposure hunts given federal remediation deadline of 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for third-party vulnerability scanner hits specifically targeting FortiSandbox version detection or public IP enumeration queries listing Fortinet products. Cross-check with internal inventory to confirm exposure status.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Payload Patterns in HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector — payload inspection is necessary to detect injection attempts before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request bodies to FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection metacharacters and patterns: $(cmd), backtick substitution, pipe (|), semicolon (;), ampersand (&), output redirect (>, <), newlines, and URL-encoded variants in parameter values.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Network Egress After Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful OS command injection enables secondary actions; C2 or data exfiltration traffic typically originates from the compromised FortiSandbox host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound DNS and HTTP/S traffic from FortiSandbox host to external destinations not in whitelist of known update/telemetry servers. Prioritize alerts if initiated within minutes of unauthenticated HTTP access attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' applies and references template substitution. CISA KEV status means active in-the-wild exploitation against exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for FortiSandbox (all variants: on-prem, Cloud, PaaS) instances exposed on internet-facing borders. Cross-check against patch management for CVE-2026-25089 remediation status. High priority: patch lag is the silent killer per article body.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — explicit payload pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP requests containing OS command syntax (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, |&) in query/POST parameters. Flag unauthenticated requests reaching FortiSandbox API endpoints. Correlate with CVE-2026-25089 exploit PoC signatures if available.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Authentication Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' can reach admin-level command execution — evidence of auth bypass chaining with RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests bypassing FortiSandbox authentication controls: missing/invalid session tokens accessing restricted endpoints, anonymous access to /admin or /cli interfaces, repeated 403→200 transitions in single session.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthorized Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'execute unauthorized commands' — process/command audit logs are source of truth for active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On vulnerable FortiSandbox instances, hunt for sudden command execution from system processes with no corresponding admin-initiated requests. Look for reverse shells, data exfil commands, lateral movement probes initiated outside normal administration windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status guarantees active wild exploitation; network signatures should be available from threat feeds within days of publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy CVE-2026-25089 exploit signatures to edge networks. Monitor for HTTP POST/GET to FortiSandbox endpoints with known PoC payloads (check Exploit-DB, GitHub, vendor advisories post-2026-07-16). Federal due date 2026-07-19 creates 3-day exploitation window rush.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Remote Code Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE capability via OS command injection; post-exploitation activities (data theft, persistence, lateral movement) are common sequelae.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise: monitor FortiSandbox for unexpected outbound connections, scheduled task creation, credential dumping utilities, or ransomware-staging activities. Correlate temporal cluster of suspicious commands on vulnerable assets with external IP reputation feeds.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public-Facing Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit via 'HTTP requests' against FortiSandbox instances. Standard asset-exposure hunt is the canonical first response to any unauthenticated RCE per threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify publicly-exposed Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances via DNS resolution, port scanning, and service fingerprinting. Correlate CVE-2026-25089 vulnerability scanner results with network exposure to prioritize remediation against federal deadline (2026-07-19).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Detections
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV entry: 'observed exploited in the wild.' Any scanner hit is actionable urgency regardless of reported patch status. Federal civilian agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CVE-2026-25089 detections across all FortiSandbox product variants. Escalate immediately; CISA KEV status means exploitation observed in wild, patch lag is 'silent killer' per threat profile.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack delivery mechanism: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Must detect payloads attempting OS command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests targeting FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection markers (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, shell metacharacters) in URL parameters and POST bodies. Validate against FortiSandbox WAF/IPS sensor logs for correlation.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from FortiSandbox Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'execute unauthorized commands.' Successful exploitation spawns processes under FortiSandbox app identity, anomalous to baseline service behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems running vulnerable FortiSandbox versions, monitor for unexpected child process creation (shells, command interpreters, curl, wget) initiated by FortiSandbox processes. Establish baseline of legitimate administrative commands; alert on deviations, especially preceded by external unauthenticated HTTP traffic.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control from Compromised FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Successfully exploited command-injection can pivot to lateral movement or C2. Monitor for attacker-directed outbound network activity from FortiSandbox appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from FortiSandbox instances to non-standard destinations, anomalous ports, or known attacker infrastructure. Baseline should reflect only expected Fortinet management, update, and sandbox-legitimate cloud traffic.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Failure or Abnormal Restart Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Command injection exploitation may crash or destabilize service. Application logs can reveal forensic trace of attack attempts even if direct payload is not logged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox application and OS logs for unexpected restarts, crashes, segfaults, or error spikes correlated with external HTTP traffic anomalies or CVE-2026-25089 scanner alerts within 0–60 minute window.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Accessible FortiSandbox Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker requires 'unauthenticated' access via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' to an exposed FortiSandbox endpoint. CISA KEV status means exploitation is active in the wild. Template-driven asset-exposure hunt referenced in article body is the canonical detection for this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints (default ports 10888, 10889) from external sources or suspicious originating IPs. Correlate with Fortinet asset inventory to identify instances that should not be internet-facing. Presence of traffic from non-whitelisted external IPs to these ports indicates potential exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Command Injection: Suspicious HTTP Request Payloads to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploited via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' No specific payload syntax is disclosed, but command injection typically uses shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, backticks, `$()`, etc.) in request parameters, headers, or body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for common command injection indicators: shell metacharacters in query parameters, POST body, or headers; URL-encoded command separators; base64-encoded command strings; or requests matching known exploit POC signatures. Pair with authentication checks to ensure requests are unauthenticated.

suggestion.title: Process Execution: Unexpected Command Spawning from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands.' Successful exploitation results in command execution on the FortiSandbox host. Monitor endpoint telemetry for anomalous process spawning from FortiSandbox processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts (e.g., `fsdb`, `admin` service user). Legitimate FortiSandbox operations spawn a known set of child processes; anomalies (reverse shells, credential dumping, lateral movement tooling) indicate exploitation. Cross-correlate with firewall/proxy logs to establish timing and HTTP trigger.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass: Unauthenticated Admin Function Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker' can reach endpoints that should require authentication. This represents authentication bypass (T1078 adjacent). Detection should flag successful access to admin/privileged endpoints without valid authentication tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP 200/302 responses to admin console, API, or config endpoints that occur without prior successful authentication (no auth cookie, token, or credential submission). Baseline legitimate admin source IPs; flag access from untrusted or external sources to these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Command Execution to Adjacent Systems from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection on FortiSandbox allows attacker to execute arbitrary commands *on the FortiSandbox host*. If FortiSandbox has network access to internal systems, adversary can pivot laterally. Article does not detail scope but appliance position (sandbox, network visibility) implies lateral movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After identifying FortiSandbox compromise (via command injection detections above), hunt for suspicious outbound network connections from FortiSandbox to internal systems or external C2. Look for tunneling, port scanning, credential dumping tools, or lateral movement frameworks executed from the FortiSandbox process context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Inventory & Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date (2026-07-19) and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'; explicitly references asset-exposure hunt template. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the canonical detection for a CISA KEV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-25089 matches on Fortinet FortiSandbox instances. Cross-reference patch status and network exposure (internet-facing vs. internal). Flag any unpatched instances and track patch lag history against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' executing OS commands. No payload-level detection use case generated despite clear attack vector and exploitation methodology described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, ;, &), environment variable expansion, command substitution syntax. Correlate with HTTP 200/502 responses and unexpected process spawning.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Unauthorized Process Execution from Service Account
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection vulnerability enables arbitrary command execution. Article specifies 'execute unauthorized commands'—process-telemetry detection should capture resulting RCE, but pipeline omitted execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by FortiSandbox services (especially Java/web processes). Alert on unexpected system binaries (sh, cmd.exe, powershell), reverse-shell tools (nc, socat), or data exfiltration commands (curl, wget) with FortiSandbox service account lineage.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Vulnerable Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' as precondition. No authentication-bypass or anonymity detection use case generated despite this being the critical access-control failure enabling exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox administrative or API endpoints lacking valid authentication tokens/sessions. Alert on requests from external IP ranges or high-velocity reconnaissance patterns (parameter fuzzing, endpoint enumeration).
